properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — raspberry season in June is when the stalls are best
properties.tip: Go on a weekday before ten; on summer Sundays the lanes are a single-file queue and every courtyard has become a breakfast restaurant.
properties.rev: People love the lanes and the breakfast and then say it has been half-turned into a theme park by weekend crowds and identical souvenir stalls; the cobbles are genuinely hard on ankles.
properties.onward: Bursa city, then the 22 bus or a 25-min taxi east to the village car park; no parking inside

properties.name: Yalova Termal
properties.desc: Roman, Byzantine and Ottoman baths in a wooded valley 12 km up from the Marmara shore, fed by water that has come out at 55–60 °C for two thousand years. The lead-domed Kurşunlu bath is the one to use; the 1930s republican buildings around it are period pieces in cracked marble. Plane trees keep the valley several degrees below the coast.
properties.season: Oct–Apr — the point of a hot bath is not August
properties.tip: Buy a session at the historic Kurşunlu rather than a hotel spa, and go midweek; on Sundays the valley is one long day-trip queue from İstanbul.
properties.rev: Regulars swear by the water and the setting; complaints are tired changing rooms, weekend crowding and modern hotel spas charging resort prices for the same source.
properties.onward: İstanbul Yenikapı–Yalova fast ferry (about 75 min), then a 20-min dolmuş up the valley from Yalova terminal

properties.name: Polonezköy
properties.desc: A Polish village founded in 1842 by exiles granted land by the sultan, sitting in forest above Beykoz with a Catholic church, a Polish cemetery and a few families still carrying Polish surnames. It survives on Sunday lunch: pork — rare in Turkey — smoked sausage, pancakes and mulberry trees you can eat straight from in June.
properties.season: May–Jun for mulberries, Oct–Nov for the forest colour; midweek always quieter
properties.tip: Book a table before you drive out on a Sunday, and walk the marked forest paths in the nature park behind the village rather than just eating and leaving.
properties.rev: People enjoy the oddity and the food, but say the Polish character is now thin, restaurants are overpriced for what arrives, and weekend traffic on the narrow forest road out of Beykoz is grim.
properties.entry: Free · nature park charges a small entry per car
properties.onward: Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) then M5 to Üsküdar and bus to Beykoz plus a minibus; realistically it is a 45-minute drive from the Asian side

properties.name: Riva
properties.desc: A river mouth on the Asian Black Sea coast with a ruined Genoese castle on the bluff, a long empty beach and a handful of fish shacks where the Riva stream meets the sea. It is thirty minutes from Beykoz and most Istanbullus have still never been; the football federation's training camp is its only landmark.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for the beach; the castle walk is best in Apr–May
properties.tip: Park at the village and walk north over the bluff to the castle ruin, then eat at one of the river-mouth places where the fish comes from the boats tied outside.
properties.rev: Those who go like the emptiness and the cheap fish, but note the same Black Sea rip currents with no lifeguards, a scruffy village centre, and construction creeping along the coast road from Beykoz.
properties.onward: Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) then M5 to Üsküdar and bus 15 to Beykoz, then a local minibus; a car makes it a 45-minute run

properties.name: Uludağ
properties.desc: The ancient Mysian Olympus, a 2,543 m limestone bulk that puts snow within sight of the Marmara. Winter is Turkey's oldest ski scene — hotels packed at the base, long lift queues, firs furred with hoar frost. In summer the meadows above the treeline fill with crocus and day walkers who came up on the cable car.
properties.season: Jan–Mar for snow, Jun–Sep for walking — Apr–May and November are mud and closed lifts
properties.tip: The Teleferik from Teferrüç in the city is the cheap way up and drops you at Sarıalan; the road via Kirazlıyayla charges a national-park fee per car and jams on winter weekends.
properties.rev: Skiers call the terrain limited but the snow reliable and the prices low; everyone complains about weekend crowds, the cable car queue and hotels that feel like 1980s package blocks.
properties.entry: National park vehicle fee ≈₺200 (≈€5) · cable car ≈₺600 (≈€14) return
properties.onward: Bursa city, then the Teleferik from Teferrüç (35 min) or 33 km by the Kirazlıyayla road; İstanbul Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) is 3 h away

properties.name: Karaca Arboretum
properties.desc: A private arboretum on a hillside above Yalova, begun by one collector in 1980 and now holding thousands of taxa, with the country's largest collection of grafted weeping and cut-leaf forms. It is laid out as a garden rather than a plantation — ponds, a Japanese section, and maples and liquidambars that turn hard in November.
properties.season: Apr–May for magnolia and blossom, late Oct–Nov for maple colour
properties.tip: It closes on Mondays and shuts early in winter; the November colour week is the best of the year and almost nobody outside Turkish plant circles knows about it.
properties.rev: Gardeners call it world-class for the size of the site and the labelling unusually good for Turkey; the complaints are the steep paths, limited shade and no café worth the name.
properties.onward: İstanbul Yenikapı–Yalova fast ferry, then 10 km south-west by taxi towards Samanlı; signposted from the Termal road

properties.name: Şile
properties.desc: Istanbul's own Black Sea town, seventy kilometres from Üsküdar over forest roads: a white and black striped lighthouse on the cliff, a Genoese castle on an offshore rock, and long sand beaches with real surf. The cotton cloth called şile bezi is woven here and sold from shops around the square, cheaply and without much ceremony.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for the sea; the town half closes Nov–Mar and the wind is bitter
properties.tip: The rip currents off the town beaches are genuinely dangerous — swim only where the flags and lifeguards are, and use Ayazma or Kumbaba rather than the unpatrolled coves.
properties.rev: Locals rate the beaches and the fish, but every account mentions dangerous currents and drownings each summer, weekend traffic out of the city, and a town centre that is more concrete than picturesque.
properties.entry: Free · beach clubs charge for sunbeds
properties.onward: Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) then bus 139 from Üsküdar via Şile road, about 90 minutes; a car is far easier and the forest road is good

properties.name: İznik (Nicaea)
properties.desc: Nicaea of the church councils, still boxed inside five kilometres of Roman and Byzantine wall with gates you drive straight through. The grid inside is low, green and slow, ending at a lake lined with fish restaurants. Working studios have brought back the quartz-bodied İznik tile that died out in the 1600s, and you can watch a kiln being loaded.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — the lake plain is humid and still in August
properties.tip: The Lefke Gate's triple arch and the Roman theatre are free and usually deserted; buy tiles only from a studio that fires its own kiln, not from the shops on the main street.
properties.rev: Travellers find the walls and the tile workshops rewarding and the town pleasantly unpolished, while noting the lakefront is scruffy and several monuments were shut for restoration for years.
properties.entry: Town free; İznik Museum ≈₺150 (≈€4) · covered by Museum Pass Türkiye
properties.onward: İstanbul Sabiha Gökçen (SAW), 2 h by road round the gulf; from Bursa it is 80 min by dolmuş via Orhangazi

properties.name: Ağva
properties.desc: A village on the Black Sea coast where two rivers, the Göksu and the Yeşilçay, come down through forest to the same beach. Small hotels line the riverbanks with jetties and rowing boats, and the whole point is doing nothing for two days: river breakfast, a boat upstream under overhanging trees, grilled fish, sleep.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct — August weekends are booked out, winter is wet and shut
properties.tip: Take a boat up the Yeşilçay rather than the Göksu, and book a riverside room midweek; on Saturdays the two-hour drive from Istanbul can double.
properties.rev: Couples call it the easiest escape from the city and the river setting genuinely lovely, while complaining about heavy weekend traffic, hotel prices that spike in July and August, and a beach with the same Black Sea currents as Şile.
properties.entry: Free · boat trips priced per hour, agree the fare first
properties.onward: Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) then bus 139 to Şile and a connecting minibus, roughly two hours; most people drive

properties.name: Kartepe
properties.desc: A 1,600 m ridge above Lake Sapanca with the most reliable snow within an hour of İstanbul: a handful of lifts, one long blue running down into beech forest, and a view north over the Gulf of İzmit. It is a day-trip mountain rather than an alpine resort. In summer the summit road becomes a picnic and paraglider spot.
properties.season: Jan–Mar for snow, Jun–Sep for the summit road — April and May are mud
properties.tip: Drive up before nine at weekends or the access road jams solid; lift tickets sell out and the car park fills long before the queues form.
properties.rev: Skiers call it convenient rather than good — short runs, thin snow in mild winters — while the summit view and the drive up get consistent praise.
properties.entry: Road/park entry ≈₺150 (≈€4) per car · day lift pass ≈₺900 (≈€21)
properties.onward: İstanbul Sabiha Gökçen (SAW), 1 h on the O-4 to Kartepe, then 20 km of switchbacks; shuttles run from Sapanca in season

properties.name: Bilecik and the Şeyh Edebali Tomb
properties.desc: The tomb of Osman's father-in-law and teacher stands on a bluff above the Belkoz gorge with a modern complex around it and two hundred metres of cliff below. Down in the old quarter, the Orhan Gazi Mosque of 1331 is among the oldest Ottoman buildings still standing — small, square and completely plain, which is the point.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — the plateau is cold, windy and often foggy in winter
properties.tip: Walk down from the tomb terrace into the old quarter instead of driving; the stepped lane past the Orhan Gazi Mosque is the only part of Bilecik that still looks Ottoman.
properties.rev: Pilgrims and history travellers find the site well kept and the view genuinely dramatic; others say the modern complex has smothered the tomb and the rest of the town is unremarkable concrete.
properties.onward: High-speed train from İstanbul or Ankara to Bilecik station, then a short taxi up to the tomb terrace

properties.name: Osmaneli
properties.desc: A Sakarya-valley town of Greek and Armenian merchant houses in stone and timber, a good number of them restored, one of them a hamam that still runs. The old quarter climbs from the river to the shell of the Hagios Georgios church, and the whole circuit takes an hour. The Ankara–İstanbul high-speed line stops here, which is a strange privilege for a town this size.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — the valley is humid and heavy in July and August
properties.tip: The high-speed train from İstanbul or Ankara puts you ten minutes' walk from the old town, which makes this the easiest car-free day trip in the whole region.
properties.rev: Rail travellers are pleasantly surprised by the streetscape and the quiet; the complaints are that restoration is patchy, the church is usually locked and there is almost nowhere to eat properly.
properties.onward: High-speed train from İstanbul Söğütlüçeşme or Ankara direct to Osmaneli station, then a 10-min walk uphill

properties.name: Maşukiye
properties.desc: A stream village on the northern skirt of Kartepe where restaurants build platforms out over the water and grill trout on them. Above the houses the road climbs through beech to the Suadiye waterfall and the plateaus. It is unashamedly a weekend eating destination and entirely worth it if you turn up on a Tuesday.
properties.season: May–Oct for the streamside tables — the beech colour in late October is the best week
properties.tip: Prices roughly double at the places nearest the main junction; drive two kilometres further up the valley for the same trout at half the money.
properties.rev: Families love the setting and the noise of the water; the standard complaints are tourist-trap pricing, near-identical restaurants and a valley road gridlocked on summer Sundays.
properties.onward: İstanbul Sabiha Gökçen (SAW), 1 h on the O-4 then 10 km south from Kartepe; dolmuş from İzmit runs hourly

properties.name: Söğüt
properties.desc: The winter pasture where Ertuğrul Gazi settled and where his son Osman began an empire, which is why the tomb here — rebuilt by Abdülhamid II — draws a state-backed ceremony every September with hundreds of costumed riders. The town itself is a quiet Bilecik market place with a small ethnography museum and not much else.
properties.season: September for the Ertuğrul commemorations; otherwise Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct
properties.tip: The tomb takes fifteen minutes, so drive on up to the ridge above town where busts of seventy-two Turkic rulers stand in a row — faintly absurd and completely photogenic.
properties.rev: Turkish visitors find it moving and foreign visitors often find it thin — a rebuilt 19th-century tomb rather than anything medieval — and September brings crowds the small town cannot absorb.
properties.onward: İstanbul (SAW) or Ankara (ESB) then the high-speed train to Bilecik or Bozüyük, and 30 min by road to Söğüt

properties.name: Kerpe
properties.desc: Sandstone cliffs eroded into overhangs, arches and stacks on the Black Sea coast north of Kandıra, with a small harbour and a beach at the foot of them. The water is cold and unusually clear for this coast, and the rock turns orange in late light. Kerpe, Kefken and Cebeci run in a line, each with its own cove.
properties.season: Jun–Sep — swell shuts the beaches for days at a time and winter is bleak
properties.tip: Cebeci and Sarısu are quieter than Kerpe itself, and the currents at the river mouths are genuinely dangerous — they drown people most summers.
properties.rev: Weekenders praise the rock formations and cheap fish, and complain about litter after August, rough pension standards and a sea that is too cold and too rough half the summer.
properties.entry: Free; some beaches charge ≈₺100 (≈€2.50) for a sunbed
properties.onward: İstanbul Sabiha Gökçen (SAW), 1.5 h by road via Kandıra; dolmuş from İzmit via Kandıra in summer

properties.name: Lake Sapanca
properties.desc: A 45 km² freshwater lake between two forested ridges, an hour from İstanbul on the motorway, ringed by walnut and cherry orchards and a great many weekend hotels. The southern shore road is the quiet side; the northern one carries the traffic. Morning mist lifting off the water with the ridges behind it is what everyone comes to photograph.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — autumn colour on the ridges is the best of it
properties.tip: The lake is a drinking-water reservoir, so swimming is banned and actually enforced; hire a pedalo or walk the southern shore path instead of arriving in a swimsuit.
properties.rev: İstanbullus love it as the nearest green weekend and warn each other about Friday-evening traffic, hotel prices that double at weekends, and the disappointment of learning you cannot swim.
properties.onward: İstanbul Sabiha Gökçen (SAW), 1 h on the O-4 motorway; or the high-speed train to Arifiye and a 10-min taxi

properties.name: Justinian's Bridge (Sangarius Bridge)
properties.desc: Justinian's 430 m bridge over what used to be the Sakarya, built in the 560s to carry the imperial road east. The river moved centuries ago, so seven enormous arches now stride across dry farmland and a stream, with the stub of a triumphal arch at one end. You can walk the whole deck without meeting anyone.
properties.season: Year-round — spring greens the fields, winter turns the approach track to mud
properties.tip: It is signed as Beşköprü off the Adapazarı–Kaynarca road; come at low sun so the arches throw shadows across the fields, and walk the full length rather than shooting it from the roadside.
properties.rev: Everyone who finds it is astonished it is not famous and equally astonished at the litter, the grazing sheep on the deck and the total absence of any information board.
properties.onward: İstanbul Sabiha Gökçen (SAW), 1.5 h on the O-4 to Adapazarı, then 8 km south-west on the Kaynarca road

properties.name: Taraklı
properties.desc: Some two hundred Ottoman timber houses in a steep valley, whitewashed with dark beams and jettied upper floors, saved before the concrete arrived and now a cittaslow. The Yunus Paşa mosque of 1517 has a wooden interior and the hamam still works. Wooden spoons, the town's old trade, are still turned in workshops on the main street.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov — it snows properly here in winter, which is beautiful and very cold
properties.tip: Stay a night in one of the restored konaks: the day-trip crowd is gone by five, and the lit lanes after dark are the entire reason to come.
properties.rev: Visitors call it the most convincingly intact Ottoman town near İstanbul; the complaints are that half the houses are still derelict, there is little to do after dusk, and weekend day-trippers fill the two cafés.
properties.onward: İstanbul Sabiha Gökçen (SAW), 2 h by road via Geyve; buses from Sakarya (Adapazarı) run several times a day

properties.name: Acarlar Floodplain Forest
properties.desc: The largest alder floodplain forest in Turkey, some 1,500 hectares of trees standing in shallow black water behind the Black Sea dunes near Karasu. Flat-bottomed boats and a boardwalk get you in among the trunks, where herons, cormorants and otters work the channels. Ten kilometres north the Sakarya meets the sea across a wide grey beach almost nobody uses.
properties.season: Apr–Jun for high water and birds — Nov–Mar is wet, grey and mostly shut
properties.tip: Boat trips leave from the Karapınar side and only run when enough people turn up, so ring ahead or go on a weekend morning.
properties.rev: Birdwatchers rate the forest highly and everybody complains about mosquitoes, unreliable boat departures and the industrial port creeping along the coast nearby.
properties.onward: İstanbul Sabiha Gökçen (SAW), 2 h by road via Adapazarı to Karasu; the longoz is signposted from the Kaynarca road

properties.name: Çeşme
properties.desc: The tip of the peninsula facing Chios, with a Genoese castle over the harbour and a chain of coves running south to Pırlanta and Altınkum. The water is startlingly clear and colder than the rest of the Aegean because of the meltemi. Out of season it reverts to a quiet fishing and thermal town.
properties.season: Jun and Sep are ideal — July and August are gridlocked and the meltemi can blow for a week
properties.tip: Skip the town beaches and drive 8 km south to Altınkum's string of small sandy coves; the last one along has no music and a shack selling grilled fish.
properties.rev: Reliably clear water and good day-trips to Chios, offset by İstanbul-level summer prices, a motorway that jams solid on Friday afternoons and a wind that can shut the beaches down.
properties.entry: Free · beach clubs charge ₺500–1,500 for a lounger in season
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 80 min west on the O-32 motorway; frequent coaches from İzmir Üçkuyular otogar

properties.name: Çeşme Castle
properties.desc: A squat Genoese fortress rebuilt by Bayezid II in 1508, sitting directly above the ferry quay with a dry moat and six towers you can walk. Inside is a small archaeological museum and a room on the 1770 naval battle of Çeşme, when the Russian fleet burned the Ottoman one in the strait you are looking at.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — the ramparts are shadeless at midday
properties.tip: Climb the seaward tower late in the afternoon when the Chios ferry comes in; the castle closes earlier than the harbour bars suggest, usually around 17:00 out of season.
properties.rev: A quick, cheap and genuinely well-preserved fort with harbour views; the museum inside is thin, the labelling minimal, and in July the courtyard is an oven.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 80 min west on the O-32; the castle is above the ferry terminal in the town centre

properties.name: Ilıca Beach
properties.desc: A long shallow bay of pale sand where hot springs bubble up through the seabed, so the water in places is noticeably warmer than the rest of the peninsula. You can wade a hundred metres and still be waist-deep, which makes it the family beach of the Çeşme coast. Thermal hotels line the back of the sand.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct — the public end is packed solid through August
properties.tip: Walk to the far eastern end past the last hotel to find where the hot springs actually vent — you feel the warm patches with your feet and almost nobody swims there.
properties.rev: Parents rate the shallow warm water highly; the standard complaints are the crowds, the wall of hotel loungers blocking access and seaweed in still weather.
properties.entry: Free at the public section · beach clubs ₺400–1,000
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 75 min on the O-32; Ilıca is 5 km before Çeşme town and served by the same coaches

properties.name: Alaçatı
properties.desc: A Greek stone village of blue shutters and bougainvillea that became Türkiye's most photographed small town, plus a shallow bay four kilometres south with reliable side-shore wind that is one of the best windsurf and kite spots in Europe. Old stone windmills line the ridge. Mastic, herbs and sea beans on every menu.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep for wind and space — August is expensive and shoulder-to-shoulder
properties.tip: Sleep in the village but eat in Alaçatı's back lanes rather than Kemalpaşa Caddesi, and check the wind forecast — the same meltemi that makes the bay perfect makes the beaches unusable.
properties.rev: The stone streets and the windsurf bay both live up to the hype; the near-universal complaint is that prices are the highest on the Aegean and the village is now more boutique hotel than village.
properties.entry: Free · windsurf board and wetsuit hire ≈€40–60 a day
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 70 min on the O-32; the bay is a further 10 min south by road from the village

properties.name: Erythrae
properties.desc: One of the twelve Ionian cities, spread over a hill above the fishing village of Ildır with its theatre cut into the slope and city walls running through olive terraces. Sheep graze the orchestra. The bay below is scattered with islets and the water off the ancient harbour is shallow enough to see submerged walls.
properties.season: Mar–Jun and Sep–Nov — the hill is unshaded and hot from July
properties.tip: The site is unfenced and free; park in Ildır village by the harbour and walk up the track past the mosque rather than trying to drive the last stretch.
properties.rev: Visitors love having a whole Ionian city to themselves with a sea view, but note that there is essentially no signage, the paths are goat tracks and the museum finds have all gone to İzmir.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then the O-32 to Çeşme and 20 km north-east on a small road to Ildır village

properties.name: Karaburun Peninsula
properties.desc: A long empty finger of limestone north of Çeşme with almost no development: narcissus fields in winter, wild olive, goat herds and a corniche road that hangs over the sea for forty kilometres. Coves like Ardıç and Denizgiren are reached down dirt tracks. Monk seals still use the caves on the western cliffs.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — winter narcissus in Jan–Feb, but many places shut Nov–Mar
properties.tip: Drive the western coast road from Mordoğan to Sarpıncık lighthouse in the late afternoon and carry water and fuel — there is one petrol station on the whole peninsula.
properties.rev: Consistently described as the emptiest coast within reach of a major Turkish city; the trade-offs are potholed side tracks, thin phone signal and restaurants that close entirely out of season.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 2 h north-west via Urla and Mordoğan; there is no realistic public transport beyond Mordoğan

properties.name: Mordoğan
properties.desc: The only real town on the Karaburun peninsula's east coast, a strip of low houses facing the gulf with Foça visible across the water. Small pebble beaches, a fishing harbour, one street of shops and a promenade where the whole town walks at dusk. Almond and tangerine groves come right down to the shore.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for swimming; May and Oct are the pleasant quiet months
properties.tip: Buy the local almonds and mandarins directly from the roadside stands north of town rather than in the shops, and eat at the harbour fish restaurants where the boats tie up.
properties.rev: Regulars value it as an unglamorous, affordable alternative to Çeşme; newcomers sometimes find it plain, with narrow stony beaches and a summer weekend traffic crush on the single access road.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 90 min via Urla and the peninsula road; minibuses run from İzmir Üçkuyular otogar
properties.credit: The original uploader was Atacameño at Turkish Wikipedia.

properties.name: Urla
properties.desc: A market town on the peninsula that has become the centre of Türkiye's Aegean wine and food revival: a dozen boutique wineries along the Urla Bağ Yolu, an artichoke festival in April, and a restored Greek quarter of art shops on Necati Bey Caddesi. Urla İskele down at the water is where the seafood is.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — the artichoke festival is early April, harvest events in September
properties.tip: Book winery visits in advance and hire a driver; the Bağ Yolu is a proper tasting route with six or seven producers and no public transport whatsoever.
properties.rev: The wine route and the seafood get genuine praise, though visitors regularly report İstanbul prices, wineries that turn away walk-ins, and a town centre that is now more concept store than market.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 45 min west on the O-32; İZBAN does not reach Urla, so a car is the practical option

properties.name: Foça
properties.desc: Ancient Phokaia, the city that founded Marseille, now a low harbour town of stone houses in two bays split by a Genoese castle wall. Fishing boats, a seafront of meyhanes, and offshore the Siren Rocks, a protected reserve where one of the last Mediterranean monk seal populations breeds in sea caves.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep — August fills with İzmir weekenders and prices double
properties.tip: Take a boat tour that circles the Siren Islands rather than one that lands on them; the seal caves are closed to landing and the operators who promise otherwise are the ones to avoid.
properties.rev: People come back for the harbour atmosphere and the seal-watching chance, while noting that actually seeing a monk seal is rare, the town beaches are small, and summer weekend parking is hopeless.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 70 min north on the O-33 and the Menemen road; regular coaches from İzmir otogar

properties.name: Klazomenai
properties.desc: An Ionian city on the Urla shore whose great find is a sixth-century BC olive oil workshop, reconstructed and working: the crushing stone, the settling tanks and the lever press have been rebuilt so you can see how classical oil was actually made. The rest of the site is low walls, mosaics and a causeway to Karantina Island.
properties.season: Mar–Jun and Sep–Nov — flat, exposed and hot at midday in summer
properties.tip: Combine it with the causeway walk to Karantina Island, the 1860s Ottoman quarantine station, which is restored and open and almost nobody joins the two visits up.
properties.rev: Archaeology-minded visitors find the working oil workshop genuinely unusual; others report a small, dusty site with limited English signage and irregular opening hours out of season.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 45 min west on the O-32 to Urla and 4 km down to İskele

properties.name: Sığacık
properties.desc: A village built inside a 16th-century Ottoman fortress, with houses using the curtain wall as their back wall and lanes barely wide enough for a handcart. A marina sits outside the gate and a Sunday producers' market fills the castle square with village women selling herbs, cheese and sea beans.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — the Sunday market runs year-round, the marina empties in winter
properties.tip: Come on a Sunday morning for the market inside the walls, then walk the two kilometres to Akkum beach rather than driving into the marina car park.
properties.rev: The castle village and the market are widely liked; complaints focus on the marina development changing the feel, tight parking and restaurants that have raised prices well past the village's means.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 50 min south-west via Seferihisar; minibuses run from Seferihisar centre

properties.name: Teos
properties.desc: The birthplace of Anacreon and the headquarters of the Dionysian actors' guild, set in olive groves a kilometre from the sea. The Temple of Dionysos has been substantially re-erected in recent seasons and its columns now stand again among the trees. There is also a theatre, a bouleuterion and two silted harbours.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov — the grove gives some shade but July heat is heavy
properties.tip: Walk on past the temple to the south harbour, a quiet sandy inlet where the ancient mole is still visible underwater and you can swim after the site visit.
properties.rev: The re-erected temple among olive trees is called the loveliest small site on this coast; the site is unfenced, unstaffed and unsigned, so visitors without a guidebook often miss half of it.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 50 min to Seferihisar and 5 km down the Sığacık road; signposted from the village

properties.name: Yenifoça
properties.desc: Old Foça's quieter twin twenty kilometres up the coast: a Genoese-era grid of stone houses with carved doorframes, a tiny harbour and a shoreline of flat rock slabs people swim off. Almost no hotels, a handful of pensions in restored houses, and a coast road north past deserted bays toward the wind farms.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for the water; Apr–May and Oct for the village with nobody in it
properties.tip: Swim from the rock shelves north of the harbour instead of the small town beach, and eat at a village lokanta rather than the seafront — the seafront is priced for the weekenders.
properties.rev: Described as what Foça was twenty years ago, with the caveats that there is little to do beyond swim and eat, most places shut from November, and the sea is weedy in still weather.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 80 min north via Menemen and Foça; minibuses connect from Foça in about 25 min

properties.name: Seferihisar
properties.desc: Türkiye's first Cittaslow town, which in practice means tangerine groves, a seed-exchange market, restored village houses in Ulamış and Düzce, and a deliberate refusal of the apartment blocks that ate the rest of the coast. Doğanbey, an abandoned Greek hill village above the town, is being slowly repaired house by house.
properties.season: Mar–Jun and Sep–Nov — the mandarin harvest and its festival fall in December
properties.tip: Drive up to Doğanbey village in the late afternoon: it is empty apart from a couple of cafés, the light on the stone is extraordinary, and there is no sign from the main road.
properties.rev: Praised for keeping its shape while its neighbours built high, though several visitors say the Cittaslow branding is thicker than the substance and the town centre itself is unremarkable.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 45 min south-west on the Seferihisar road; frequent minibuses from Üçkuyular

properties.name: Gediz Delta Bird Paradise
properties.desc: Twenty minutes from downtown İzmir the city stops and forty thousand hectares of salt pans, lagoons and reedbed begin. Around ten thousand flamingos breed here on a purpose-built island, the largest colony in Türkiye, and pelicans, avocets and marsh harriers work the shallows. Flat gravel tracks, hides, and no crowds at all.
properties.season: Nov–Apr for numbers, Jun–Jul for flamingo chicks — Aug is hot, still and mosquito-heavy
properties.tip: Bring your own binoculars and go early: the hides face east, so morning light is behind you and the salt-pan haze has not started.
properties.rev: Birders rate it world-class for flamingos, while casual visitors often leave disappointed: the birds are distant without a scope, the access road is rough and parts close during the breeding season.
properties.entry: Free — the adjoining Doğal Yaşam Parkı charges separately
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then İZBAN to Çiğli and a taxi to Sasalı; a car is realistically necessary for the dyke tracks

properties.name: Mount Nif and the Karabel Relief
properties.desc: Above Kemalpaşa, on the old pass road, a life-size Hittite warrior is carved into a rock face — spear, bow, curved sword, hieroglyphs — the figure Herodotus mistook for an Egyptian pharaoh. The mountain behind holds a Lydian fortress, Byzantine ruins and cherry orchards that supply half of İzmir in June.
properties.season: Apr–Jun for cherries and green slopes, Sep–Oct for clear air; the pass road is grim in winter rain
properties.tip: The relief is in a damp gully off the Kemalpaşa–Torbalı road with one small brown sign; park at the layby and walk down, and go in the morning when light reaches into the cleft.
properties.rev: Hittite enthusiasts think it worth the detour, but most visitors report a weathered, graffiti-scratched carving behind a rusty grille, poor signposting and nowhere sensible to park.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 35 min east to Kemalpaşa; the relief is 20 km further on the Torbalı road

properties.name: Basmane Station
properties.desc: The 1866 terminus of the Ottoman line to Aydın, a low stone building with a cast-iron train shed and a clock that still keeps time. Trains to Denizli and Selçuk leave from platforms that look unchanged since the 1930s. The quarter around it — cheap hotels, tea houses, Syrian bakeries — is the unpolished counterweight to Alsancak.
properties.season: Year-round — the district is livelier and safer in daylight
properties.tip: Take the regional train from here to Selçuk instead of the coach: it costs almost nothing, runs along the Küçük Menderes plain and drops you a walk from the Artemision.
properties.rev: Rail travellers appreciate the intact Victorian shed and cheap regional fares; the surrounding streets get repeated warnings for after-dark hustle, and services are cut without notice during track works.
properties.entry: Free to enter · regional tickets a few euros
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then İZBAN to Basmane, which is also the metro interchange for the old city

properties.name: Asansör (Historical Elevator)
properties.desc: A brick lift tower built in 1907 by the Jewish banker Nesim Levi so residents of the Karataş cliff would not have to climb 155 steps. The cabin still runs, free, up 51 metres to a terrace restaurant over the gulf. Below it, Dario Moreno Street is a lane of restored Levantine houses in ochre and pink.
properties.season: Year-round — the terrace is best an hour before sunset
properties.tip: Walk up Dario Moreno Sokak first and take the lift down, then have the sunset drink at the terrace bar rather than paying for the restaurant dinner.
properties.rev: Locals and visitors both like the free ride and the view; the recurring gripe is that the terrace restaurant charges tourist prices for mediocre food and the queue at sunset can run twenty minutes.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then İZBAN to Konak and the 169 bus or a 20-min walk south along the shore

properties.name: Kemeraltı Bazaar
properties.desc: A living Ottoman bazaar following the curve of a filled-in harbour: coppersmiths, spice sacks, thirty hans, a working synagogue quarter and coffee served in courtyards under vine. It is not curated for tourists, which is why it works. Kızlarağası Han and the Havra Sokağı fish and pickle street are the two poles.
properties.season: Year-round — best Oct–May; the covered lanes trap heat in August
properties.tip: Go on a weekday morning and enter through Havra Sokağı from Anafartalar Caddesi; the tourist end near Konak is the least interesting part of the whole bazaar.
properties.rev: Repeatedly called the most authentic bazaar in Türkiye after Istanbul's, with the caveats that it is genuinely confusing to navigate, several hans are half-derelict, and pickpocketing near Konak is real.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then İZBAN train to Konak and walk 300 m inland; the metro stop is Çankaya

properties.name: Gümüldür and the Menderes coast
properties.desc: The stretch of shore between Özdere and Ahmetbeyli, backed by tangerine orchards that scent the whole coast road in December. Long sand-and-shingle beaches, unfashionable family pensions, and the ancient sites of Claros and Notion within a few kilometres. This is where İzmir families rent a summer flat rather than a boutique hotel.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for the sea; December for the mandarin harvest and empty beaches
properties.tip: Buy mandarins straight from the orchard gates on the Gümüldür–Ahmetbeyli road; the roadside stalls nearer the beach charge triple for the same fruit.
properties.rev: Turkish families rate it good value with clean shallow water; foreign visitors often find it a scrappy strip of concrete holiday blocks, and the summer traffic on the single coast road is heavy.
properties.entry: Free · beach clubs charge modestly by Çeşme standards
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 45 min south on the coast road via Gümüldür; minibuses run from Üçkuyular otogar

properties.name: Agora of Smyrna
properties.desc: A Roman civic square rebuilt by Marcus Aurelius after the earthquake of 178, sunk two storeys below the modern street grid. The basement galleries are the surprise: rows of vaulted arches, still carrying water in their original channels, with graffiti scratched by second-century citizens. Apartment blocks lean over the whole thing.
properties.season: Oct–May — the sunken court holds heat badly in July and August
properties.tip: Go down into the west basilica vaults rather than staying on the upper court; the Roman graffiti and the working water channel are down there and are easy to miss entirely.
properties.rev: Praised as an unexpected, near-empty Roman site inside a working city; complaints centre on patchy signage, closed sections behind excavation fencing and the rubbish blown in from the streets above.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then metro to Çankaya and a 10-min walk uphill through Kemeraltı's back lanes

properties.name: Alsancak and the Kordon
properties.desc: İzmir's Levantine quarter: grid streets of tall shuttered houses behind a two-kilometre grass waterfront where the whole city sits at dusk with beer and sunflower seeds. Horse carriages have gone, phaeton stands remain. Kıbrıs Şehitleri and the narrow bar lanes off it are where İzmir actually drinks and eats.
properties.season: Year-round — Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct are ideal; the Kordon is windy and grey in January
properties.tip: Cross to the Karşıyaka side on the municipal ferry at sunset for about a euro — it is the cheapest and best boat trip in the city and locals use it as a commute.
properties.rev: Consistently described as the most relaxed big-city waterfront in Türkiye, with complaints about weekend noise from the bars, thin parking and gulf water that smells in still August weather.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then İZBAN suburban train straight to Alsancak station in about 25 min

properties.name: Kadifekale
properties.desc: The acropolis of Smyrna, founded by Alexander's generals, sits on a bare hill 180 m above the gulf. The walls are Hellenistic below and Byzantine-Ottoman above, and there is a huge Roman cistern inside. What people come for is the view: the whole horseshoe of İzmir, the bay and the ferries laid out at once.
properties.season: Year-round — go at sunset any month; the hilltop is windy and exposed
properties.tip: Take the 33 bus from Konak rather than walking up through the neighbourhood, and come down before dark — the streets below are poor and unlit.
properties.rev: The panorama is universally rated the best in İzmir, but visitors consistently flag litter inside the walls, ongoing excavation fencing and a run-down approach that puts some people off.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then metro to Konak and the 33 city bus up the hill; taxis from Konak take 10 min

properties.name: Dilek Peninsula National Park
properties.tr: Dilek Yarımadası-Büyük Menderes Deltası Milli Parkı
properties.desc: A forested ridge running out into the Aegean opposite Samos, with four pebble coves on the north side — İçmeler, Aydınlık, Kavaklıburun, Karasu — reached by one road through pine and wild olive. Wild boar cross it at dusk. The far end is a military zone, which is exactly why the water is so clear.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct — swimmable Jun–Sep, but weekends in August are gridlocked
properties.tip: Arrive before nine or the park hits its vehicle quota and shuts the gate; alternatively leave the car in Güzelçamlı and take the shuttle or bicycle in.
properties.rev: Repeatedly described as the cleanest water near Kuşadası, with two constant complaints: the entrance queue on summer weekends and boar that raid unattended picnic bags.
properties.entry: Per-person park fee plus a vehicle charge — roughly ₺200–400 (≈€5–10) per car, cash easiest
properties.onward: İzmir (ADB) then 1 hr 30 via Kuşadası and Güzelçamlı; the 'Milli Park' dolmuş runs from Kuşadası in summer

properties.name: Asklepion of Pergamon
properties.desc: The Roman world's most famous healing sanctuary, where Galen trained: a colonnaded sacred way, a theatre for patient therapy, sacred springs, and a vaulted tunnel down which attendants whispered suggestions to sleeping patients on their way to the round treatment temple. Dream interpretation, mud baths and music were the prescriptions.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — flat, shadeless and hot from July
properties.tip: Walk the underground tunnel slowly and listen; the acoustics and the light shafts are the whole point, and most groups march through it in twenty seconds.
properties.rev: The tunnel and the sacred way impress most visitors, though several note that the site sits inside a military zone with photography restrictions at the gate and that separate tickets from the acropolis add up.
properties.entry: ≈₺500 (≈€11) · separate from the acropolis · covered by Museum Pass Türkiye
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 2 h north to Bergama; the sanctuary is 3 km west of the town centre by taxi

properties.name: Red Basilica
properties.desc: A colossal red-brick temple to the Egyptian gods, built by Hadrian, straddling the Selinus river on two tunnels that still carry the water. One of the round side towers has been rebuilt as a mosque and is in use. Inside the main hall the brick walls rise nineteen metres and swallows nest in the arcades.
properties.season: Year-round — spring and autumn best; the brick hall stays cool even in July
properties.tip: Walk down to the riverbank behind the building to see the two vaulted tunnels the whole temple is built over — almost nobody goes round the back.
properties.rev: The sheer scale of the brickwork surprises people; the usual grumbles are scaffolding that has been up for years, restricted access to the towers and an entry fee for a building you see in twenty minutes.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 2 h north to Bergama; the basilica is in the old town, walkable from the bazaar

properties.name: Pergamon
properties.desc: An acropolis stacked on a 300-metre crag, with the steepest theatre of the ancient world — eighty rows dropping almost vertically into the valley. The library rivalled Alexandria and gave us parchment. The Great Altar's terrace is empty because the frieze is in Berlin, which locals will tell you about within the first minute.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — the crag is fully exposed and July tops 38 °C
properties.tip: Take the cable car up but walk down the ancient road past the Temple of Demeter and the gymnasium terraces; the descent is the half of the site the coaches never see.
properties.rev: The theatre and the setting draw superlatives; complaints are about the cable-car queue at midday, the missing altar frieze, and vertigo on the theatre steps, which have no handrail.
properties.entry: ≈₺900 (≈€20) plus cable car ≈₺200 · covered by Museum Pass Türkiye
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 2 h north on the O-33 and D550 to Bergama; coaches run from İzmir otogar hourly

properties.name: Claros
properties.desc: The oracle of Apollo that rivalled Delphi, sitting in a waterlogged hollow behind the beach at Ahmetbeyli. Enormous drums of the temple's Doric columns lie where the earthquakes dropped them, half in standing water, and colossal marble feet from the cult statues survive. Below the temple are the vaulted rooms where prophecies were delivered.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — the hollow floods in winter and mosquitoes own it in high summer
properties.tip: Wear boots you do not mind soaking: the site sits below the water table and the walkways are frequently submerged, which is exactly why so few people bother with it.
properties.rev: Those who make it call it one of the most atmospheric sites in Ionia, with the standard caveats: standing water, biting insects, minimal signage and an entrance that is often unstaffed.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 50 min south to Ahmetbeyli; the site is signposted 1 km inland from the coast road

properties.name: Cave of Zeus
properties.desc: A collapsed karst chamber right beside the national park gate, filled with cold spring water that meets the sea underground, so it reads green at the edges and near-black in the middle. It is small — twenty metres across — and the shock when you get in is the whole experience. Fig roots hang down the rock.
properties.season: Jun–Sep to swim; the water stays cold all year
properties.tip: Go at opening time or after five; between eleven and four it is a queue of people photographing each other on the same ledge, and swimming is often stopped when it is busy.
properties.rev: Worth ten minutes for the colour of the water, but almost everyone says it is far smaller than the photographs suggest and mobbed in season, with slippery rock and no real changing space.
properties.entry: Small fee — check locally; usually included if you are already paying to enter the national park
properties.onward: İzmir (ADB) then 1 hr 30 to Güzelçamlı; the cave is signposted 200 m before the national park entrance gate

properties.name: Mount Yamanlar and Karagöl
properties.desc: The pine mountain behind Karşıyaka, with a small dark crater-shaped lake in a fold near the top that İzmir families have picnicked at for a century. Legend hangs Tantalus on it. From the ridge you look down on the whole gulf on one side and the Gediz plain on the other, with nothing between you and the wind.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov — snow is possible in January, and summer weekends are picnic chaos
properties.tip: Go on a weekday: on Sundays the single-lane road up is nose-to-tail and the lake shore disappears under barbecue smoke.
properties.rev: Locals value it as the nearest real forest to the city; visitors coming for the lake often say it is smaller and more littered than the photographs suggest, and the road has some rough sections.
properties.entry: Free · small parking charge at the lake
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then İZBAN to Karşıyaka and 40 min by car up the forest road; buses are infrequent

properties.name: Güzelçamlı
properties.desc: The last village before the national park gate: one long street of pensions, a Sunday market under plane trees, and grilled sardines eaten at plastic tables with the mountain behind. It is where people who want Dilek without Kuşadası prices stay, and it still shuts down properly in winter.
properties.season: May–Oct — most pensions and half the restaurants close Nov–Mar
properties.tip: The Sunday pazar is the real one for this coast — figs, thyme honey, village cheese — and it is over by two, so come early and eat gözleme at the far end.
properties.rev: Praised as calmer and cheaper than Kuşadası with genuinely good fish, though the beach in the village itself is narrow and busy and traffic backs up on park-entry mornings.
properties.onward: İzmir (ADB) then 1 hr 30; dolmuşes run every 20 minutes from Kuşadası bus station in season

properties.name: Panionion
properties.desc: The federal sanctuary where the twelve Ionian cities met, on a low hill of scrub and olive above Güzelçamlı. What survives is a rock-cut semicircular assembly place, eleven rows of seats hacked straight out of the hillside, and a view down the whole Ionian coast. There is nobody here, ever.
properties.season: Mar–May and Oct–Nov — grass and thistles swallow the seats by midsummer
properties.tip: The turning is an unmarked farm track off the Güzelçamlı road near Otomatik; set the pin before you leave the village because there is no sign and no phone signal on the hill.
properties.rev: Those who find it call it the most atmospheric empty site in Ionia; most of the complaints are simply about failing to find it, since the access track is unsigned and rutted.
properties.onward: İzmir (ADB) then 1 hr 30 to Güzelçamlı; from the village it is 3 km on a rough track best done on foot or in a high car

properties.name: Gümüşlük and Myndos
properties.desc: A fishing village at the peninsula's western tip where the ancient city of Myndos lies half underwater — you can wade the submerged causeway to Rabbit Island in knee-deep water over cut stone. Building is restricted because of the ruins, so the bay has stayed low, and the fish restaurants sit with their feet in the sea.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for wading and swimming; May and Oct for the village without the queue
properties.tip: Wade to the island barefoot before dinner and eat late, after the sunset rush; the causeway stones are sharp, so reef shoes save the evening.
properties.rev: Widely called the most attractive corner of the peninsula, with two complaints repeated everywhere: restaurant prices well above the Bodrum average and a village that is thoroughly full on August evenings.
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) about 55 minutes by road; dolmuşes run from Bodrum otogar via Turgutreis, and parking in the village is limited

properties.name: Pigeon Island
properties.desc: A rock islet joined to Kuşadası by a 350-metre causeway, ringed by a low Ottoman sea wall with a small keep in the middle. Inside there are figs, cats, a tea garden and a circular walk of ten minutes that puts the whole bay and the Greek island of Samos in front of you.
properties.season: Apr–Nov — the causeway takes spray in winter storms
properties.tip: Come an hour before sunset and walk the seaward side of the wall, not the tea-garden side; the light hits the fortress and the fishing boats come back at the same time.
properties.rev: A cheap and genuinely pleasant half hour, though visitors note the fortress interior is mostly empty and the causeway becomes a slow shuffle when a cruise ship is in.
properties.onward: İzmir (ADB) then 1 hr 15 to Kuşadası; the causeway starts at the southern end of the seafront promenade, a 10-minute walk from the port

properties.name: Didyma
properties.desc: Two complete columns nineteen metres high, and behind them a temple platform you descend into by a sloping tunnel to reach the oracle courtyard where the laurel grew. The Medusa head lying at ground level is the photograph everyone takes. The scale is closer to a cathedral than a temple and it was never finished.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — the marble throws heat back at you in midsummer
properties.tip: Go through the vaulted ramp on the north side into the inner court rather than only circling the outside; that descent is the whole point of the building.
properties.rev: Almost everyone calls it the most impressive single ruin on this coast, then notes the ring of souvenir shops and carpet touts pressed right up against the fence and a car park that fills with coaches by ten.
properties.onward: Bodrum (BJV) about 1 hr 15 by road, or İzmir (ADB) about 2 hr 30; town dolmuşes from Altınkum stop at the temple gate

properties.name: Kuşadası
properties.desc: A cruise port with an old quarter that survives behind it: Kaleiçi's grid of low stone houses, the Öküz Mehmet Pasha caravanserai of 1618 on the harbour, and a bazaar street that turns genuinely good the further uphill you climb. Two ships in port changes the town completely for six hours, then it empties.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct — August is hot, full and expensive
properties.tip: Check the cruise schedule board at the port; on a no-ship day the bazaar prices and the pressure from shop callers drop by half.
properties.rev: Handy as a base for Ephesus and Priene and praised for its seafront, but reviewers are blunt about aggressive shop touts on Barbaros Hayrettin street and the wall of cruise passengers on double-ship days.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB) about 1 hr 15 by road; regular buses from İzmir otogar and Selçuk, and a summer ferry from Samos

properties.name: Karaincir
properties.desc: A single crescent of coarse pale sand between two headlands on the south coast, sheltered from the meltemi, with water that shelves gently and a handful of low pensions behind the tamarisks. It is the beach Bodrum locals drive to on their own day off, and it is still mostly Turkish families.
properties.season: Jun–Oct — sheltered from the north wind, so it works when the north coast is choppy
properties.tip: Park at the far eastern end near the tamarisks rather than the central car park; that section has no sunbed operator and you can put a towel straight on the sand.
properties.rev: Praised for calm, clean water and low prices; the complaints are that sunbeds now cover much of the sand, the road in is narrow and the beach fills completely on summer weekends.
properties.entry: Free · sunbed hire on the organised stretch
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) about 1 hour; take the Turgutreis road then the Akyarlar turning, or the Akyarlar dolmuş from Bodrum otogar

properties.name: Miletus
properties.desc: The city that invented Western philosophy now sits in a cotton field four miles from the sea it once ruled, its harbour silted solid by the Meander. The Roman theatre is enormous and you can climb through its vaulted passages to the Byzantine castle on top. Storks nest on the İlyas Bey Mosque next door.
properties.season: Apr–May and Oct — the plain is a mosquito swamp after rain and an oven in August
properties.tip: Walk five minutes to the İlyas Bey Mosque of 1404, a perfect little Menteşe-era building with a marble portal, that most day-trippers drive straight past.
properties.rev: People find the scale of the theatre astonishing and the rest of the site confusing and waterlogged; the ground is often muddy and the small museum is frequently shut without notice.
properties.onward: Bodrum (BJV) or İzmir (ADB), then the Söke–Didim road; Miletus, Priene and Didyma are a natural one-day loop by car

properties.name: Altınkum
properties.desc: A shallow, gold-sand bay with water that stays waist-deep for fifty metres, which is why every Turkish family with small children ends up here. The promenade is fish restaurants, ice cream and British bars in equal measure. Walk west past the marina to Cengiz Topel and the beaches thin out fast.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for swimming; May and Oct for the town without the crowd
properties.tip: Skip the main strip and take the coast road west to Akbük or south to Tavşan Burnu, where the same water comes without the loudspeakers.
properties.rev: Families rate the safe shallow water highly; almost every review mentions that July and August bring package crowds, sunbed charges and traffic on the single beach road.
properties.entry: Free · sunbed and umbrella hire extra
properties.onward: Bodrum (BJV) about 1 hr 15 by road, or İzmir (ADB) 2 hr 30; frequent buses from Söke and Aydın otogar

properties.name: Yalıkavak
properties.desc: A former sponge-diving village turned superyacht marina, where hundred-metre boats moor a few streets from a whitewashed old quarter of windmills and stone lanes. The abandoned Greek village of Sandıma sits on the slope above, roofless and quiet, and the wild Küdür headland to the west has coves with nobody on them.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for the sea; May and Oct for the village and the walks
properties.tip: Walk up to Sandıma in the late afternoon — twenty minutes above the marina — then come down for dinner; it is free, empty, and the contrast with the yachts below is the point.
properties.rev: People rate the marina restaurants and the old streets, then note that prices in the yacht marina are Monaco-level and that the village beach itself is small and pebbly.
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) about 50 minutes; regular dolmuşes from Bodrum otogar take 30 minutes over the ridge

properties.name: Priene
properties.desc: A Hellenistic grid city on a terrace under a 370-metre cliff, laid out by the same planners who drew Rhodes. Five columns of the Temple of Athena stand against pine and rock, the little bouleuterion still has its stone benches on four sides, and the streets are cobbled and steep. The Meander plain stretches flat below.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov — the climb from the car park is punishing in July
properties.tip: Sit in the theatre's five marble thrones in the front row, then keep walking uphill past the temple to the west gate where nobody goes and the whole grid opens out below you.
properties.rev: Visitors love the pine shade and the emptiness compared with Ephesus, and consistently warn that the stepped approach path is a real climb and that there is no café or shade at the top.
properties.onward: İzmir (ADB) or Bodrum (BJV), then road to Söke and 15 km west to Güllübahçe; buses run Söke–Güllübahçe but drop you at the village, not the gate

properties.name: Allianoi
properties.desc: A Roman thermal spa town north of Bergama, with baths still fed by a 45 °C spring and an intact vaulted bathing hall, deliberately buried under sand and flooded by the Yortanlı dam in 2011 after a decade of legal fights. The bridge and the hot spring outflow remain visible at the reservoir edge in dry years.
properties.season: Aug–Oct when the reservoir is at its lowest and more of the site is exposed
properties.tip: Ask at the Bergama museum first — what you can actually see depends entirely on the year's water level, and in a wet spring there is nothing above the surface at all.
properties.rev: Visitors describe it as a site to mourn rather than tour: usually nothing but water and a bridge, no facilities, no signage, and a story that Turkish archaeologists still consider a scandal.
properties.entry: Free — there is no ticketed site left to enter
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 2 h to Bergama and 18 km north-east toward Paşaköy on a minor road

properties.name: Akyarlar
properties.desc: The peninsula's south-western corner, with fine pale sand, Kos sitting close enough across the strait to see cars on it, and the conical hill of Aspat — the Byzantine fortress of Strobilos — rising behind the bay. A row of low fish restaurants, a small mosque, and none of the Bodrum noise.
properties.season: Jun–Oct — the sea here stays warm latest on the peninsula
properties.tip: Climb Aspat hill from the eastern side in the last hour of light; it is a 30-minute scramble to the fortress and the view down the Kos strait is the best on this coast.
properties.rev: Regulars call it the best sand on the peninsula and the calmest village left; the recurring notes are limited shade, a long drive from Bodrum and very little to do after dinner.
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) about 1 hour via Turgutreis; dolmuşes run from Bodrum otogar through Turgutreis to Akyarlar

properties.name: House of the Virgin Mary
properties.desc: A small stone chapel in pine forest on Bülbül Dağı, identified from the visions of a German nun and endorsed by three popes. Inside it is dim, candle-smelling and takes about ninety seconds to walk through. Outside, a wall of paper prayer slips tied by Muslims and Christians alike is the more interesting sight.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — cool under the pines even when Selçuk is at 38 °C
properties.tip: Arrive before 09:00 or after 16:00; between those hours the Kuşadası cruise coaches queue the chapel entrance forty deep.
properties.rev: Pilgrims find it genuinely affecting; secular visitors often report a two-minute chapel, a stiff entry fee, a car-park charge on top and an aggressive gift shop.
properties.entry: ≈₺600 (≈€14) plus a vehicle charge · not covered by the Museum Pass
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then to Selçuk and 7 km of hairpins up Bülbül Dağı; taxis wait at the Ephesus lower gate

properties.name: Ephesus
properties.desc: Marble streets polished by two thousand years of feet run downhill from the Odeon to the Library of Celsus, whose two-storey façade still stands with its columns in place. The Great Theatre holds twenty-five thousand and the acoustics still work. The Terrace Houses, six Roman flats under a glass roof with frescoes and mosaic floors, are what most visitors skip.
properties.season: Apr–May and Oct — July and August bake the marble and there is almost no shade
properties.tip: Enter at the upper south gate and walk downhill to the lower gate, then take a taxi back to your car; doing it in reverse is an uphill slog in the heat.
properties.rev: Almost everyone calls it the best-preserved classical city they have walked, then complains about cruise-coach waves before noon and a ticket price that has climbed hard in three years.
properties.entry: ≈€40 · Terrace Houses ≈€15 extra · covered by Museum Pass Türkiye
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 50 min by road to Selçuk, or the İZBAN suburban train to Selçuk and a 3 km taxi

properties.name: Gündoğan
properties.desc: A deep north-facing bay with a long shallow beach, tangerine gardens behind it, and a headland at the western end where a cave church with Byzantine frescoes is cut into the cliff above the water. Quieter than Türkbükü across the ridge, and the fish restaurants are aimed at Turkish families rather than club crowds.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for swimming; the meltemi blows hardest across this north coast in July
properties.tip: Take a small boat or kayak from the beach to the Manastır cave on the west point — it is only reachable from the water and most people staying here never see it.
properties.rev: Regulars value the calm and the value for money compared with Türkbükü; the common gripes are strong afternoon wind, a beach that narrows in front of the hotels and thin nightlife.
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) about 40 minutes; dolmuşes from Bodrum otogar run every half hour in season

properties.name: Temple of Artemis
properties.desc: One re-erected column with a stork's nest on top, standing in a marshy field of scattered drums and frog noise. That is all that survives of a building the ancients rated above the Pyramids. The anticlimax is the point: pace the foundation outline with Ayasuluk Hill and the İsa Bey Mosque lined up behind you.
properties.season: Mar–May — the field floods after winter rain and the frogs take it over
properties.tip: It is a five-minute walk from Selçuk's centre and free, so come at sunset when the mosque and castle behind it go gold and the coaches have left.
properties.rev: Visitors are split between those disappointed by a swamp with one column and those who find the emptiness moving; everyone agrees the roadside touts selling guidebooks are persistent.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 50 min by road to Selçuk; it is signposted on the Selçuk–Ephesus road

properties.name: Basilica of St John
properties.desc: Justinian's six-domed basilica on Ayasuluk Hill was one of the largest churches in the world; now it is a cross-shaped field of re-erected columns and brick arches with a marble slab over the supposed tomb of the Evangelist. The hill also carries a Byzantine-Seljuk citadel and the best view over Selçuk's storks.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — exposed hilltop, no shade in high summer
properties.tip: Buy the combined ticket that also covers the castle at the top of the hill, which many people walk past without realising it is open.
properties.rev: Praised as quiet and uncrowded compared with Ephesus, though several note that the reconstruction is heavy-handed and the interpretation boards are faded to illegibility.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 50 min by road or İZBAN train to Selçuk; the hill is a 10-min walk from the station

properties.name: Knidos
properties.desc: A city built on the very tip of the peninsula where two seas meet, with twin harbours, a round temple terrace that once held Praxiteles' Aphrodite, and a theatre facing the strait to Kos. The wind never stops, the marble is white against blue on three sides, and the last 35 km of road is the price of admission.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — fully exposed, with no shade anywhere on site
properties.tip: Walk up to the round temple platform first thing; the afternoon boats from Datça all arrive together and that terrace is where everyone stands.
properties.rev: People rate the setting above the ruins themselves and consistently complain about the long, slow, partly rough road from Datça, the total lack of shade and the wind.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Datça and 35 km west on a slow single-track road; summer day boats from Datça harbour avoid the drive

properties.name: Türkbükü
properties.desc: The peninsula's fashionable bay, where there is barely any sand and the beach is instead a chain of wooden decks built out over the water, each belonging to a club or hotel. Boats anchor in rows, the İstanbul crowd arrives in July, and the mandarin groves behind still smell of the village it used to be.
properties.season: Jun–Sep — everything worth eating at is shut Nov–Apr
properties.tip: There is almost no free public shore here; check the daily deck minimum spend before you sit down, because a sunbed on a name platform costs more than dinner elsewhere.
properties.rev: People come for the scene and the water quality and report exactly the expected downside: high minimum spends, no real beach, and a road behind the bay that jams solid in August.
properties.entry: Free to the village · beach decks charge a daily minimum spend
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) about 35 minutes, the closest of the peninsula bays to the airport; dolmuşes run from Bodrum otogar

properties.name: Çamlık Railway Museum
properties.desc: Thirty-odd steam locomotives parked on open track in a pine hollow south of Selçuk, most of them British and German engines that worked the Ottoman lines. You can climb into cabs, walk the turntable and go through a short tunnel with a preserved train inside. Rust, oil smell and cicadas, almost no supervision.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — the metal is untouchable in August sun
properties.tip: Bring a torch: the tunnel section with the sleeping-car set is unlit and most people turn back at the entrance without seeing it.
properties.rev: Rail enthusiasts rate it one of the best open collections in the eastern Mediterranean; others report peeling paint, no English labelling and a café that is often shut.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then Selçuk and 10 km south on the Aydın road; Çamlık is signposted off the D550

properties.name: Bitez
properties.desc: A south-facing bay backed by one of the last big tangerine groves on the peninsula, with a shallow sandy shore, a shaded promenade under trees, and enough steady afternoon breeze that it became the windsurfing bay. Five kilometres from Bodrum and a completely different pace once the sun drops.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for the water; the wind is reliable Jun–Aug for boards
properties.tip: Walk the coastal path east from the bay towards Bodrum for twenty minutes to reach small unmarked rock coves that never fill up.
properties.rev: Families and windsurfers both rate it, and both mention the same things: the water is very shallow a long way out, sea grass washes up on the sand, and the strip is dominated by all-inclusive hotels.
properties.entry: Free · sunbed hire on the organised sections
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) about 40 minutes; dolmuşes from Bodrum otogar take 15 minutes and run late in season

properties.name: Lake Bafa
properties.desc: A former sea gulf cut off by the Meander's silt, now a brackish lake with granite islets carrying ruined Byzantine monasteries and the Beşparmak range rising straight out of the water behind it. Flamingos and pelicans work the shallows, and the light on those boulder mountains at dusk is the reason people stay.
properties.season: Mar–May and Oct–Nov for birds and hiking; summer is hot and hazy, swimming is poor
properties.tip: Stop at the lakeside restaurants on the old road at Kapıkırı rather than the ones on the new highway; ask for the lake's own fish, yayın or levrek, grilled over wood.
properties.rev: Photographers and birdwatchers rate it very highly; visitors expecting a swimming lake are disappointed by the salinity, the muddy shore and the highway that runs along the northern edge.
properties.entry: Free · boat trips to the islands negotiated at Kapıkırı
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) about 50 minutes, or İzmir (ADB) 2 hr 15; the D525 Milas–Söke road runs along the lake's north shore

properties.name: Theatre of Halicarnassus
properties.desc: A fourth-century BC theatre cut into the hill above Bodrum, restored enough to still be used for concerts, with thirteen thousand seats looking straight down over the white town, the castle and the bay. It is free, it is open late in summer, and almost no one climbs up here in daylight.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — the stone radiates heat in midsummer afternoons
properties.tip: Walk up for the last half hour of daylight; the whole peninsula turns orange from the top row and it is the best free view in Bodrum.
properties.rev: Rated highly by those who find it, with two consistent notes: it sits beside a busy main road so the traffic noise carries, and modern restoration has replaced a lot of the seating.
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) 45 minutes; from the harbour it is a steep 20-minute walk up Kıbrıs Şehitleri Caddesi, or a short taxi

properties.name: Pedasa
properties.desc: A Lelegian hill town above Konacık, reached by a walking track through scrub oak and thyme: cyclopean walls, a tower, rock-cut tombs and a sanctuary of Athena, all at 400 m with the whole Bodrum peninsula laid out beneath. Herodotus wrote about the priestess here who grew a beard before disasters.
properties.season: Oct–May — the hillside is tinder-dry and snake-warm in high summer
properties.tip: Start from the Gökçeler track above Konacık in the cool of the morning; it is 40 minutes up on a rough path with no water and no shade at the top.
properties.rev: Hikers rate the walk and the silence; the constant complaint is that the trail is poorly marked, easy to lose in scrub, and that the ruins themselves are modest if you are not into Carian archaeology.
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) about 35 minutes to Konacık, then the unpaved track towards Gökçeler; the last stretch is on foot

properties.name: Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
properties.desc: A rectangular pit two streets back from the harbour, a few green-marble column drums, a sarcophagus fragment and the foundation of the tomb that gave every mausoleum its name. The Knights quarried it flat and the sculpture is in London. What remains is the outline, a scale model, and a strong sense of loss.
properties.season: All year — the site is small and mostly open ground, best in spring light
properties.tip: See the model and the wall panels first, then walk to the castle and look for the green volcanic stone from the Mausoleum reused in its walls; that connection is the real story.
properties.rev: Visitors respect the history but are frank that one of the Seven Wonders is now a hole in the ground with a garden, and that the fee feels high for twenty minutes.
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) 45 minutes; the site is a 10-minute uphill walk from the harbour on Turgutreis Caddesi

properties.name: Muradiye Mosque, Manisa
properties.desc: A late Sinan mosque of 1585 with İznik tiles at their peak and a carved marble minbar, built for Murad III when Manisa was the training ground for Ottoman crown princes. The attached medrese now holds the town museum. Down the hill, the Sultan Mosque is where the Mesir paste is thrown to the crowd each spring.
properties.season: Year-round; the Mesir festival falls in late March
properties.tip: Time it for the Mesir Macunu festival in March, when paste wrapped in paper is thrown from the Sultan Mosque minaret and the whole town tries to catch it.
properties.rev: The tilework gets real praise from people who make the detour, though Manisa itself is usually described as a rebuilt modern town with the monuments marooned among concrete blocks.
properties.entry: Mosque free · museum small fee, covered by Museum Pass Türkiye
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 50 min north-east on the O-33; İZBAN suburban trains run İzmir–Manisa

properties.name: Bodrum Castle
properties.desc: The Knights of St John built it from 1402 partly out of the Mausoleum's marble, and its towers still carry the coats of arms of English, French, German and Italian knights. Inside is the Museum of Underwater Archaeology, whose Uluburun shipwreck gallery holds a Bronze Age cargo of copper ingots, ivory and gold.
properties.season: All year — the ramparts are exposed and hot Jul–Aug, superb in spring
properties.tip: Go straight to the Uluburun and Glass Wreck halls when you enter; they are ticketed separately in practice and close earlier than the castle grounds.
properties.rev: Consistently called the best museum on the Aegean coast, with the caveats that several galleries have been shut for restoration for years and the combined ticket costs more than people expect.
properties.entry: ≈€25 · Museum Pass Türkiye covers entry; some special galleries carry a surcharge
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) 45 minutes by shuttle; the castle is on the harbour in the town centre, walkable from anywhere in Bodrum

properties.name: Şirince
properties.desc: A Greek-built hill village of whitewashed stone houses with wooden overhangs, emptied in the 1923 exchange and refilled by tourism. Two abandoned churches, cobbled lanes too steep for cars, and vineyards on every slope. The fruit wine is mostly sugar and marketing; the olive oil, dried figs and village breakfast are the real reason to come.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — weekends are gridlocked from May onward
properties.tip: Park in the lower lot and walk up; the top of the village past St John the Baptist church empties out completely and has the terrace views everyone photographs from below.
properties.rev: People love the stone lanes and the breakfast, and are near-unanimous that the fruit-wine hard sell and the wall-to-wall souvenir stalls on the main street have gone too far.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then Selçuk and 8 km of switchbacks east; minibuses run from Selçuk otogar roughly hourly

properties.name: Bodrum
properties.desc: White cubic houses with bougainvillea running down to two bays either side of the castle, a gulet harbour on one and the bar street on the other. The old town keeps its shape: sponge divers' lanes, the Sunday market, Halikarnas Balıkçısı's house. It is loud in August and quietly Mediterranean in May.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct — August is heat, traffic and peak prices
properties.tip: Stay on the west bay near the castle rather than Cumhuriyet Caddesi; the bar street runs until four in the morning and the noise carries across the water.
properties.rev: Visitors love the castle, the harbour and the food, and complain consistently about August crowds, aggressive restaurant touts on the harbour front and cruise-day congestion in the bazaar.
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) 35 km, about 45 minutes by Havaş shuttle or taxi; ferries run to Kos year-round and to Datça in summer

properties.name: Weeping Rock (Niobe)
properties.desc: A weathered rock face on the lower slope of Spil Dağı that, from the right angle, resolves into a seated woman's head with water seeping down it. This is the Niobe of the myth, turned to stone weeping for her fourteen children, and it is the same rock Pausanias described nearly two thousand years ago.
properties.season: Nov–Apr, when the seep is actually running — it dries out completely in summer
properties.tip: Stand at the marked viewpoint below and slightly to the side; from directly underneath it is just a cliff, and half the visitors leave without ever seeing the face.
properties.rev: Classicists enjoy standing where Pausanias stood, but plenty of visitors say it is an ordinary rock with a good story, hard to make out, and the surroundings have been built up around it.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 50 min to Manisa; the rock is on the city's southern ring road at the foot of Spil Dağı

properties.name: Mount Sipylus (Spil Dağı)
properties.desc: A 1,500-metre limestone wall rising straight out of Manisa, protected as a national park, with black pine forest, wild horses on the upper meadows and the endemic Manisa tulip that flowers red across the slopes each spring. The road climbs to picnic terraces where the whole Gediz plain lies below you.
properties.season: Apr–May for the Manisa tulip and wild horses; Sep–Oct for clear plain views
properties.tip: Go up in the last two hours of daylight for the plain view, and in April look for the endemic tulip on the open slopes above the picnic areas rather than in the forest.
properties.rev: Locals treat it as their weekend mountain and rate the tulips and the views; visitors flag heavy weekend picnic litter, an entry charge per car and forest roads closed after snowfall.
properties.entry: Small national park vehicle fee — check locally
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 50 min north-east to Manisa on the O-33; the park road starts in the city's southern edge

properties.name: Latmos Rock Paintings
