properties.desc: On the Beşparmak massif above Lake Bafa, prehistoric painters left red ochre figures on the undersides of granite overhangs — human couples, hands, dancing groups — dated to roughly six thousand BC and unlike anything else in Anatolia. The rock itself, weathered into stacked spheres and caves, is half the experience.
properties.season: Mar–May and Oct–Nov — the granite is an oven in summer and there is no shade
properties.tip: You will not find the shelters alone; hire a guide from Kapıkırı or Gölyaka, which costs little and is the difference between seeing paintings and seeing boulders.
properties.rev: Those who go with a guide describe it as unforgettable; the complaints are all about access — unmarked paths, some sites damaged by graffiti and quarrying, and paintings that are faint unless the light is right.
properties.entry: Free · guide fee negotiated in the village, roughly ₺1000–1500 (≈€25–35) for a half day
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) about 1 hour to Çamiçi on the D525, then the Kapıkırı or Gölyaka road; walking access only beyond the villages

properties.name: Herakleia under Latmos
properties.desc: The village of Kapıkırı is built inside the ancient city: houses stand between a temple of Athena on its rock, a bouleuterion, and a Hellenistic wall that runs six kilometres up the mountain. Sarcophagi lie half submerged at the lake edge, and goats graze the agora. Granite boulders the size of houses are everywhere.
properties.season: Mar–May and Oct–Nov — perfect walking weather; July is airless among the rocks
properties.tip: Stay a night in one of the village pensions; the day-trippers leave by five and the temple rock at sunset over the lake is what you actually came for.
properties.rev: Repeatedly described as one of the most extraordinary places in western Türkiye, with honest warnings about the rough 10 km approach road, a village entry charge collected informally, and persistent pressure to buy scarves and boat trips.
properties.entry: Small village fee — check locally; the ruins themselves are open ground
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) about 1 hour; turn north off the D525 at Çamiçi and follow 10 km of narrow road to Kapıkırı

properties.name: Magnesia on the Maeander
properties.desc: A site being pulled out of the mud year by year: the stadium was fully excavated only recently and its long banks of seating now run clear for two hundred metres. Add the Temple of Artemis Leukophryene's scattered frieze blocks and a theatre still half buried. Diggers work through the summer and you can watch.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — the water table is high and parts flood in winter
properties.tip: It is on the main Söke road with a proper car park, so it makes an easy 40-minute stop between Ephesus and Priene rather than a trip of its own.
properties.rev: People are struck by the newly cleared stadium and equally struck by how much of the rest is still under earth, with muddy paths and minimal shade or explanation.
properties.onward: İzmir (ADB) about 1 hr 15; the site is directly on the Selçuk–Söke road near Ortaklar and any Söke bus passes the gate

properties.name: Datça Peninsula Road
properties.desc: Seventy-five kilometres from the Marmaris junction to Knidos along a ridge with the Gulf of Gökova on one side and the Hisarönü gulf on the other, through almond groves, beehives and the isthmus at Balıkaşıran where the two seas are 800 metres apart. The final stretch to Knidos is single-track and slow.
properties.season: Mar–Jun and Sep–Nov — February almond blossom turns the whole ridge white
properties.tip: Stop at the Balıkaşıran isthmus where both gulfs are visible from one layby, and fill the tank in Datça, because there is no fuel west of it.
properties.rev: Drivers call it one of the best roads in the country and warn about slow coaches, blind bends, goats on the tarmac and a final section to Knidos rough enough to punish a low car.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM) or Bodrum (BJV); collect the car at the airport, the peninsula road begins at the Marmaris–Muğla junction near Gökova

properties.name: Palamutbükü
properties.desc: A kilometre of white pebble on the peninsula's south coast, backed by a row of fish restaurants and almond terraces instead of hotels. The water is startlingly clear because there is no sand to stir up, and Rhodes sits on the horizon. Ovabükü and Hayıtbükü, the next coves east, are the same idea in miniature.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for swimming; May and Oct are warm but many places shut
properties.tip: Park at the west end by the fishing harbour rather than on the restaurant strip, and bring water shoes — the pebbles are large and the entry is sharp.
properties.rev: Repeat visitors praise the water clarity and the absence of concrete, and grumble about sunbed prices, restaurants fencing off most of the beach, and 25 km of bends from Datça.
properties.entry: Free — sunbeds charged by the restaurants
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Datça and 25 km over the ridge on a good but twisting road; dolmuş twice a day in summer

properties.name: Iasos
properties.desc: A city on a near-island in the Gulf of Güllük, where the ancient breakwater still shelters fishing boats and the modern village of Kıyıkışlacık uses the agora as its back garden. There is a theatre facing the water, a Roman fish market rebuilt as a small museum, and swimming straight off the ruins.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — the peninsula is exposed and hot in high summer
properties.tip: Follow the track out to the isthmus and the necropolis on the far side; the sarcophagi sit right on the shore and you can swim from the rocks below them.
properties.rev: Loved for the combination of ruins and sea and the total absence of coaches; the recurring notes are a rough 15 km access road, patchy opening hours and a village with only a couple of places to eat.
properties.entry: Small fee — check locally; the site museum keeps shorter hours than the ruins
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) about 40 minutes; turn off the Milas–Güllük road at Kıyıkışlacık and follow it 16 km to the coast

properties.name: Bayındır
properties.desc: The flower town of the Küçük Menderes valley: greenhouses and open fields of carnations, roses and seasonal cut flowers supply markets across Türkiye, and in April the roadsides are solid colour. The old centre has Ottoman houses, a covered market and a çarşı where the flower auction happens early and loudly.
properties.season: Apr–May for the flower fields and the festival; the rest of the year it is a working farm town
properties.tip: Be at the flower market by 07:00 — the auction is over by mid-morning and by lunchtime the town is just another Aegean market centre.
properties.rev: Visitors who time the April flower festival right find it genuinely colourful; outside those weeks people describe an ordinary agricultural town with little to detain them.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 55 min south-east via Torbalı; regional trains from Basmane also stop here

properties.name: Euromos
properties.desc: Sixteen Corinthian columns of a temple of Zeus standing in an olive grove fifty metres off the Milas–Söke road, several still carrying their architrave. Some shafts were never fluted because the donors stopped paying, and the inscriptions naming those donors are still legible on them. Ten minutes and one of the best-preserved temples in Anatolia.
properties.season: All year — spring poppies in the grove make it, midsummer light is flat and harsh
properties.tip: It is easy to shoot from the road and drive on; walk into the grove behind the temple instead, where the theatre and the city wall are hidden in the trees.
properties.rev: Everyone agrees it is remarkable value for a five-minute stop; the criticisms are the road noise from the adjacent highway and that the site takes almost no time to see.
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) about 30 minutes; directly on the D525 Milas–Söke road, 12 km north of Milas, any Söke bus can drop you at the gate

properties.name: Eski Datça
properties.desc: The stone village the modern town grew out of, two kilometres inland: single-storey houses in unrendered rubble stone, bougainvillea over the lanes, almond and olive trees between the walls. The poet Can Yücel lived and is buried here, which is why the cafés play a certain kind of music and the bookshop is better than it needs to be.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — February almond blossom is the local secret
properties.tip: Come for breakfast rather than dinner: the courtyard places serve almond dessert and village eggs before the day-trippers walk up from the harbour.
properties.rev: Visitors love the lanes and the shade, and note that it is small enough to see in an hour, that prices are high for what it is, and that August evenings fill it with coaches.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM) then 2.5 hours by road, or the summer Bodrum (BJV) ferry to Datça; the old village is 3 km up from the harbour

properties.name: Tire
properties.desc: An old Aydınid and Ottoman trade town with more than twenty surviving mosques, several hans and a Tuesday market that is one of the largest in the Aegean. The town still makes felt, keçe carpets and camel-hair goods by hand, and the local dish, Tire köftesi, is worth the drive on its own.
properties.season: Year-round; the Tuesday market is the reason to time it — avoid midsummer midday heat
properties.tip: Find one of the two remaining felt workshops behind the bazaar and watch keçe being beaten; ask at the Yeşil İmaret mosque and someone will point you.
properties.rev: Food-minded travellers rate the market and the köfte highly; others find the monuments scattered, poorly signed and often locked outside prayer times, with little in English anywhere.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 1 h south-east via Torbalı; regional trains from Basmane stop at Tire

properties.name: Beçin Castle
properties.desc: The Menteşe emirs' capital on a flat rock plateau above Milas: a walled castle, and outside it a whole abandoned medieval town of madrasas, baths, a mosque and Ahmet Gazi's tomb, spread over the tableland among wild olives. The cliff edge drops straight to the Milas plain.
properties.season: Mar–May and Oct–Nov — the plateau is completely exposed in summer
properties.tip: The castle is only half of it; walk 300 m beyond the walls to the Ahmet Gazi Medresesi and the Bey Hamamı, which are unfenced, free and better preserved than the fortress.
properties.rev: Visitors find it an unexpectedly large and evocative medieval site, and note the sparse signage, the long walk between scattered monuments and a site that is fully open to the sun.
properties.entry: Small fee — check locally; covered by Museum Pass Türkiye when the booth is staffed
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) about 35 minutes; 5 km south of Milas on the Ören road, signposted from the Milas ring road

properties.name: Milas
properties.desc: The old Carian capital Mylasa, now a market town with a Roman tomb called Gümüşkesen standing complete in a back street, the Firuz Bey Mosque of 1394 in blue-grey marble, and a Tuesday bazaar that fills the whole centre. Carpets from the surrounding villages are still woven and sold here.
properties.season: Mar–Jun and Sep–Nov — the Tuesday market is the reason to time a visit
properties.tip: Gümüşkesen is a fifteen-minute walk uphill from the bazaar and unstaffed; go there first while you have energy, then work back down through the market.
properties.rev: Travellers passing to the airport are surprised by how much survives, while also reporting heavy traffic through the centre, poor parking and monuments that are scattered and often locked.
properties.entry: Free · the small archaeological museum charges a nominal fee
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) is 15 minutes away, the closest town to the airport; buses run from Bodrum, Söke and Muğla to Milas otogar

properties.name: Labraunda
properties.desc: The Carian sanctuary of Zeus Labraundos, on a pine terrace at 600 m reached by fourteen kilometres of switchbacks above Milas. Two andrones — banqueting halls built by Maussollos and his brother — still stand to roof height, there is a sacred spring house, and a Sacred Way once ran all the way down to the city.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — the road ices over in winter and the site is cold
properties.tip: The last few kilometres are steep and narrow with no barrier; go up in the morning, because meeting a logging lorry on the descent in poor light is genuinely unpleasant.
properties.rev: Those who make the drive call it the most atmospheric Carian site anywhere, and every account warns about the mountain road, the lack of any facilities and a guard who may or may not be there.
properties.entry: Small fee — check locally; often unstaffed and free in practice
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) about 40 minutes to Milas, then 14 km of mountain road north; no public transport, car essential

properties.name: Alinda
properties.desc: Ada of Caria's stronghold, where she adopted Alexander, hanging above the village of Karpuzlu. A three-storey Hellenistic market building stands nearly complete with its barrel vaults intact, and the theatre looks straight out over the plain. Goats use the agora. It is one of the best-preserved Carian towns and almost nobody goes.
properties.season: Mar–May and Oct–Nov — thorny scrub and snakes make July a poor choice
properties.tip: Walk uphill through the village to the agora first, then follow the wall line to the watchtower on the ridge; the theatre is signposted but the market hall is the reason to come.
properties.rev: Visitors describe it as unfenced, unstaffed and wonderful, with the caveats that the last road is narrow and winding, there is no water on site and the grass hides loose stone.
properties.onward: İzmir (ADB) or Bodrum (BJV), then the Çine road and 25 km west to Karpuzlu; a car is effectively required

properties.name: Tralleis
properties.desc: Three colossal brick arches — the Üç Gözler, the vaults of a Roman gymnasium — standing on the terrace directly above Aydın city, visible from the whole plain. The rest of the city is trenches, foundations and a long view over fig orchards to the Meander. It takes twenty minutes and reframes the town below.
properties.season: Oct–May — the terrace is exposed and Aydın regularly tops 40 °C in summer
properties.tip: The site sits inside a military zone boundary and opening has been erratic for years; phone the Aydın museum the day before rather than driving up on spec.
properties.rev: The arches impress everyone who gets in; the repeated complaint is exactly that — access has been restricted or closed for long stretches and there is little to see beyond them.
properties.entry: Free when open — access can be restricted, check with Aydın Archaeological Museum
properties.onward: İzmir (ADB) about 1 hr 30 by motorway; from Aydın centre it is a 3 km climb north, easiest by taxi

properties.name: Ören and Ceramus
properties.desc: A quiet village on the north shore of the Gulf of Gökova with a long grey-pebble beach, and the ancient city of Ceramus scattered through the gardens behind it — a temple podium in an olive field, city walls in someone's orchard. Across the gulf the pine wall of the Datça road rises straight out of the sea.
properties.season: Jun–Sep to swim; Apr–May and Oct for the ruins and the walking
properties.tip: The ruins are not fenced or signed; ask in the village for the Zeus Chrysaoreus temple podium, which stands in a private olive grove and needs a nod from the owner.
properties.rev: Regulars value the near-total absence of tourism and the clear water; the drawbacks are a coarse pebble beach, a long winding drive from anywhere and a power station visible along the coast.
properties.onward: Bodrum–Milas (BJV) about 1 hr 15; 45 km south of Milas on a mountain road via Beçin, with a few daily minibuses

properties.name: Ödemiş
properties.desc: The market town under Bozdağ, with a Wednesday bazaar that pulls in the whole Küçük Menderes valley and a private ethnographic museum, the Yıldız Kent Arşivi, that is far better than a town this size deserves. Potatoes, chestnuts and the local kestane şekeri are the produce; Birgi is fifteen minutes away.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov — the valley floor is 38 °C in July and August
properties.tip: Come on a Wednesday for the bazaar and take the old regional train from İzmir Basmane rather than driving; it is slow, cheap and runs through the whole valley.
properties.rev: Useful as a base for Birgi and Bozdağ and liked for the bazaar, though most visitors agree the town itself is plain concrete and there is little reason to stay a second night.
properties.entry: Free · town museum a few euros
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 1 h 20 by road via Torbalı, or the regional train from İzmir Basmane in about 2 h

properties.name: Alabanda
properties.desc: Fallen columns of an Ionic temple lying in an olive grove exactly where the earthquake dropped them, drum against drum, with a bouleuterion's walls standing to head height nearby. Cotton fields run right up to the ruins and a tractor track cuts through the middle. The Romans called it a town of scorpions and luxury.
properties.season: Mar–May and Oct–Nov — the grove floods in winter and bakes in August
properties.tip: Come after olive harvest in late autumn when the ground is cleared; in spring the undergrowth is waist-high and you will walk past the temple without seeing it.
properties.rev: A quiet, unfenced pleasure for anyone who likes ruins without railings, though there is no signage, no facilities and the access lane through the village is easy to miss.
properties.onward: İzmir (ADB) or Bodrum (BJV), then the D525 to Çine and 8 km north to Doğanyurt village; park at the village and walk in

properties.name: Bin Tepe Tumuli
properties.desc: A hundred and fifty Lydian burial mounds scattered across the ridge above Lake Marmara, the largest — Alyattes's tomb, father of Croesus — 355 metres across and climbable in ten minutes. From the top the whole plain of Sardis and the lake open out, and you can see the other mounds standing like a bombing range of grass humps.
properties.season: Mar–May for green ridges and wild flowers; Oct is clear and cool
properties.tip: Drive the dirt track to the Alyattes mound rather than trying to reach the smaller ones — the burial chamber under it is usually locked but the climb and the view are the point.
properties.rev: Landscape-minded visitors find the field of mounds genuinely strange and memorable; others report unmarked farm tracks, a locked chamber entrance and nothing to see up close but grass.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 1 h 45 to Salihli and 15 km north on farm roads toward Gölmarmara

properties.name: Hisarönü Bay and Keçi Bükü
properties.desc: The long shallow inlet on the north side of the Bozburun peninsula, with Keçi Bükü at its head: a wooded islet carrying a Byzantine fort, a line of gulets on the mooring buoys and shallows that turn the water milky green. Marmaris is half an hour away and it feels like a different decade.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct — the meltemi funnels hard down the bay in July and August
properties.tip: Hire a kayak at Keçi Bükü and paddle out to the fort islet; there is no jetty, so aim for the shingle on its north side.
properties.near: Keçi Bükü, Orhaniye, Marmaris, Muğla, Türkiye
properties.rev: Sailors rate it as the best shelter on this coast, while swimmers find it weedy and shallow, with jellyfish in late summer and almost no beach.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Marmaris and 25 km west on the Bozburun road; dolmuşes run to Orhaniye but not late

properties.name: Loryma (Bozukkale)
properties.desc: A Hellenistic fortress at the tip of the peninsula, nine towers of dressed limestone still standing above a fjord-shaped inlet where Athenian and Rhodian fleets once sheltered. There is no proper road, so it is either a long walk from Söğüt or a yacht anchorage, and most days it is you and the goats.
properties.season: Apr–May and Oct — no shade, no water, and the walk is brutal in summer
properties.tip: Carry all your water: the track from Söğüt passes no spring, and the single seasonal shack at the anchorage may not be open.
properties.rev: Sailors and walkers call it one of the most atmospheric ruins on the coast, and everyone warns that the final dirt road destroys ordinary cars and that there is no shade, water or signage.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Marmaris to Söğüt by dolmuş and a 6 km walk; most people arrive by gulet or on a Bozburun day boat

properties.name: Gölcük Lake
properties.desc: A small crater-shaped lake at 1,000 m in the Bozdağ range, ringed by pine and chestnut and reflecting the ridge on still mornings. There is a walking loop of about three kilometres, a handful of wooden restaurants serving trout and gözleme, and mist that sits on the water until mid-morning in autumn.
properties.season: May–Oct — beautiful under snow in winter but the last kilometres often need chains
properties.tip: Walk the far side of the loop, away from the restaurants; that is where the reflections are and where the picnic crowd never goes.
properties.rev: A reliable escape from the valley heat and popular with İzmir families; on summer weekends the shore is wall-to-wall barbecues and litter, and the lake level drops noticeably by September.
properties.entry: Free · small parking charge in season
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 1 h 45 via Ödemiş and the Bozdağ road; no public transport to the lake itself

properties.name: Sardis
properties.desc: Croesus's capital, where coinage was invented. Two sites a kilometre apart: a marble gymnasium façade re-erected to full height beside the largest ancient synagogue known, its floor a carpet of mosaic; and up a gorge, the Temple of Artemis with two enormous standing columns under crumbling badland cliffs.
properties.season: Apr–May and Oct — the Gediz plain is punishing in July and August
properties.tip: Do both parts: many visitors stop at the roadside gymnasium and never drive the extra kilometre up to the temple, which is the better of the two.
properties.rev: The synagogue mosaics and the gymnasium façade draw real admiration; the frequent complaints are the highway noise beside the site, two separate entrance points and almost no shade or facilities.
properties.entry: ≈₺300 (≈€7) covering both sections · covered by Museum Pass Türkiye
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 1 h 45 east via Turgutlu and Salihli; trains from İzmir Basmane stop at Sart

properties.name: Sart
properties.desc: The village that grew on top of Sardis, where Roman column drums serve as garden walls and the Pactolus stream — the one whose gold made Croesus rich — runs behind the houses. Vineyards for sultana raisins stretch to the horizon and roadside stalls sell them by the kilo from August onward.
properties.season: Sep–Oct for the grape harvest; Apr–May for green hills and wild flowers
properties.tip: Walk up the Pactolus bed from the gold refinery excavation; the badland pinnacles above the stream are the landscape everyone photographs from the temple and hardly anyone walks into.
properties.rev: A pleasant half-hour after the ruins rather than a destination; visitors note there is essentially one café, no signage for the gold refinery site and dogs around the vineyard tracks.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 1 h 45 east on the D300 via Salihli; the İzmir–Uşak train calls at Sart

properties.name: Carian Trail
properties.desc: An 800-kilometre waymarked path through old Caria, looping the Bozburun and Datça peninsulas and the shores of the Gulf of Gökova. Unlike the Lycian Way it strings together ruins nobody stops at — Hydas, Bybassos, Loryma — and long stretches run on goat paths through pine and carob with the sea far below.
properties.season: Mar–May and Oct–Nov — summer is dangerously hot and water sources dry up
properties.tip: Walk the Bozburun peninsula section in April, when the cisterns still hold water and the village pensions at Selimiye and Söğüt have opened for the season.
properties.rev: Walkers rate the emptiness and the ruins highly, and repeatedly report faded waymarks, overgrown sections, unreliable water and villages where the only shop closed years ago.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM) or Bodrum (BJV), then dolmuş to Marmaris, Bozburun or Datça for the main trailheads

properties.name: Çine Valley Road
properties.desc: The road south from Çine follows the Çine Çayı — the ancient Marsyas — into a granite gorge where the river runs green between boulders the size of cars. Oleander lines the water, plane trees shade the roadside tea stops, and the rock walls close in until the Muğla plateau opens out at the top.
properties.season: Apr–Jun for full water and green; the river drops to a trickle by August
properties.tip: Pull in at one of the riverside kır lokantası between Çine and Eskiçine and ask for alabalık; they cook the trout over wood and the tables sit on platforms over the water.
properties.rev: Drivers rate it one of the better back roads in the Aegean, though it carries heavy lorry traffic to Muğla and the dam upstream has visibly cut the river's flow.
properties.onward: İzmir (ADB) or Bodrum (BJV), then the D525 south from Aydın through Çine towards Yatağan; the whole gorge is under an hour of driving

properties.name: Birgi
properties.desc: The Aydınid capital, a village of timber-framed houses with painted ceilings stepping up a wooded slope, and at its heart the 1312 Great Mosque with a carved walnut minbar and a mihrab of Seljuk tiles. The Çakırağa Mansion has murals of Istanbul and Venice painted by someone who had never seen either.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov — the mosque and mansion close for lunch, and August is airless
properties.tip: Check whether Çakırağa Mansion is open before you drive up; it has been closed for restoration in stretches and it is the single best interior in the village.
properties.rev: Widely called the best-preserved Ottoman village in the Aegean interior, with recurring complaints about erratic opening hours, restoration scaffolding and weekend coach parties from İzmir.
properties.entry: Small fee — check locally · mosque free
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 1 h 30 via Ödemiş; frequent minibuses cover the last 9 km from Ödemiş

properties.name: Bozburun
properties.desc: The last working gulet-building town: hulls the size of houses sit on the slipways at the edge of the harbour and the whole waterfront smells of pine resin and varnish. There is no beach, which is why it stayed a village of sponge divers and boatwrights with a handful of pensions on the water.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct — winter here is genuinely closed
properties.tip: Walk the shore road south past the yards towards Söğüt for the view back across the bay, and buy sponge or thyme honey directly from the harbour stalls.
properties.rev: Travellers who want quiet rate it highly and those expecting a resort are disappointed: no sand, little nightlife, and 50 km of bends from Marmaris that take well over an hour.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Marmaris and 50 km southwest; dolmuş from Marmaris otogar roughly every two hours in summer

properties.name: Bozdağ
properties.desc: A chestnut-forest village at 1,150 m on the ridge above Ödemiş, with İzmir's only ski centre on the slopes above and cold spring water everywhere. In winter there are five lifts and reliable snow; in summer it is where the valley escapes the heat, and the road over the top to Gölcük is one of the best drives in the province.
properties.season: Jan–Mar for skiing, Jun–Sep for the cool air and chestnut woods
properties.tip: The ski centre is small and gets İzmir day-trippers on weekends; go midweek, and in summer drive the ridge road towards Gölcük for the views back down over the plain.
properties.rev: Locals are fond of it as a cheap, close ski hill, but experienced skiers call the runs short and the lift infrastructure dated, and the access road ices over badly after dark.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 1 h 45 via Ödemiş and 25 km of switchbacks; winter tyres are needed Dec–Mar

properties.name: Selimiye
properties.desc: A boatbuilding village on the Bozburun peninsula that became a quiet harbour of stone houses, jasmine and fish restaurants without acquiring a single tall building. There are remains of a Hellenistic watchtower on the hill behind, and a swim platform at the end of the jetty that locals use at dawn.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct — most restaurants shut from November to March
properties.tip: Book a waterfront table the day before in August, and ask what came in that morning rather than ordering off the printed menu.
properties.rev: Visitors describe it as what Marmaris was forty years ago, and warn that prices are now Bodrum-level, there is no proper beach and the single road in is narrow.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Marmaris and 40 km of winding road; dolmuşes run Marmaris–Bozburun via Selimiye several times a day

properties.name: Salihli
properties.desc: The market town for the Sardis plain, surrounded by sultana vineyards and with thermal springs at Kurşunlu and Çamurhamamı where the water comes out around 60 °C into old domed bathhouses. September is harvest, when the whole town smells of drying grapes and the roadsides are covered in laid-out raisins.
properties.season: Sep–Oct for the raisin harvest; Nov–Mar is the proper thermal season
properties.tip: Use Salihli as your base for Sardis, Bin Tepe and Kula rather than staying in Manisa — it is closer to all three and the thermal hotels are cheap midweek.
properties.rev: Travellers use it as a functional and cheap base with good thermal baths; nobody pretends the town itself is attractive, and the older hamams are described as basic and dated.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 1 h 45 east on the D300; the İzmir–Uşak train stops at Salihli several times daily

properties.name: Nysa on the Maeander
properties.desc: A city built astride a gorge, with a 100-metre Roman tunnel-bridge carrying the torrent under the centre — you can still walk into the mouth of it. Above are a library standing two storeys high, a theatre with hunting reliefs on the stage front, and olive terraces climbing to Mount Messogis behind.
properties.season: Mar–Jun and Sep–Nov — the gorge is slippery after rain
properties.tip: Go down to the stadium end and look back up into the tunnel arch; almost everyone stops at the theatre and misses the piece of engineering that makes the site unique.
properties.rev: Visitors are impressed by the library and the tunnel and consistently note that signage is thin, the paths are overgrown in summer and the ticket office is sometimes unstaffed.
properties.onward: İzmir (ADB) about 2 hours, or Denizli (DNZ) 1 hr 30; Sultanhisar is on the Aydın–Denizli road and the İZBAN-style regional train stops there

properties.name: Kızkumu (Orhaniye's Sunken Road)
properties.desc: A 600-metre spit of red gravel lying just under the surface, so you walk out into the middle of the bay with water at your knees and the shore a long way behind you. The legend involves a princess carrying sand in her skirt; the geology involves a submerged ridge. Mountains close in on three sides.
properties.season: May–Oct — outside that the water is too cold to enjoy the walk
properties.tip: Walk it early or late: at midday the shallow water is bath-warm with no shade, and stepping off the edge of the spit drops you into six metres.
properties.rev: Families love the novelty and the safe shallow water; complaints centre on sharp gravel underfoot, access through waterfront restaurants that expect an order, and a car park full by mid-morning.
properties.entry: Free — most access is through restaurants that expect an order
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Marmaris and 20 km on the Bozburun road; dolmuş from Marmaris otogar to Orhaniye

properties.name: Sedir Island (Cleopatra Beach)
properties.desc: A small island in the Gökova gulf carrying the ruins of Kedrai — a theatre, a city wall, temple foundations — and a beach of near-spherical white ooid grains found almost nowhere else in the Mediterranean. The sand is fenced off: you may not lie on it or carry a grain away, and wardens actually check.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct — the daily boats stop running by November
properties.tip: Shower in the marked area before leaving; removing sand is prosecuted, and the beach closes to swimmers when the wardens judge the crowd too large.
properties.rev: The water and the ruins get consistent praise, but many find the sand rules heavy-handed, the island small enough for an hour, and the boats delivering everyone at once from Çamlı.
properties.entry: ≈€6 island fee plus the boat fare from Çamlı or Akyaka
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM) or Bodrum (BJV), then Çamlı harbour near Akyaka for the 20-minute boat; Marmaris day trips also run

properties.name: Turunç
properties.desc: A single crescent of coarse pale sand and very clear deep water under steep pine ridges, twenty winding kilometres south of Marmaris. It stays small because the road is a chain of hairpins, and the sea shelves fast, which makes it a swimmer's beach rather than a paddler's one.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for swimming; May and Oct are quiet and still warm enough
properties.tip: Take the hourly water taxi from Marmaris instead of driving — the road is beautiful but the village car parks fill by ten in August.
properties.rev: Regulars rate the water quality above anything near Marmaris; the recurring gripes are the hairpin road, sunbed charges on most of the sand and how little happens after dinner.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), 90 min to Marmaris, then 20 km of hairpins or the water taxi from the harbour

properties.name: Amos
properties.desc: A small Rhodian-period town on the headland above Kumlubük, with a theatre cut into the slope and its seats still facing the bay. There is a stretch of polygonal wall, a temple terrace and inscriptions about land leases; a ten-minute path from the road gets you there and you usually have it to yourself.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov — no shade, and the path is slippery after rain
properties.tip: Climb to the top row of the theatre and sit down — the sea fills the whole stage opening, which is the entire reason to come.
properties.rev: Almost everyone calls it the best-value ruin near Marmaris precisely because nobody is there, while noting the site is small, unlabelled and reached by a rough track that ordinary hire cars manage slowly.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM) then Marmaris; from Turunç take the Kumlubük road and look for the sign above the bay

properties.name: Marmaris
properties.desc: A yacht town wrapped around a bay so enclosed the water stays flat, with pine hills dropping straight into it and a small castle on the knoll above the old quarter. The marina end is superyachts and gelato; ten minutes west the back lanes still have stone houses, a bazaar and charcoal fish grills.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct — July and August are hot, packed and loud until 4am
properties.tip: Skip the seafront strip and eat in the lanes behind the castle, then take the water taxi to Turunç rather than swimming off the town beach.
properties.rev: Visitors like the sheltered bay, the boat trips and the value, and complain in the same breath about the wall of bars on Bar Street, restaurant touts and a town beach that is more marina than sand.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM) airport, then about 90 minutes by road or the Havaş bus; Bodrum (BJV) is a longer 2.5-hour drive

properties.name: Marmaris Castle
properties.desc: A small Ottoman fortress rebuilt by Süleyman the Magnificent before the siege of Rhodes, sitting on the rock the old town climbs. Inside are seven rooms of amphorae, ship models and Carian finds around a courtyard of bougainvillea; the real value is the wall-walk, which looks down on the harbour, the tiled roofs and the whole bay.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov — the courtyard bakes at midday in summer
properties.tip: Come in the last hour before closing, when the light hits the bay and the cruise groups have gone back down the hill.
properties.rev: People find the museum itself modest and over quickly, but almost everyone says the ramparts and the walk up through the old lanes justify the small ticket.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then 90 minutes to Marmaris; the castle is a five-minute walk uphill from the marina

properties.name: Marmaris National Park
properties.desc: Thirty thousand hectares of red pine and sweetgum wrapping the peninsulas either side of Marmaris, with forest roads climbing to viewpoints over Hisarönü and Gökova. Wild boar and jackals are common, tortoises cross the tracks, and these pine forests are why Muğla supplies most of the country's pine honey.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov — high fire risk closes forest roads in July and August
properties.tip: Drive up to the Cennet Adası viewpoint above İçmeler at the end of the day, and check first, because the forestry barriers close on high-fire-risk days.
properties.rev: Walkers praise the empty forest tracks and the smell of pine after rain, and report unsigned junctions, no water on the trails and closures after summer fires.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Marmaris; a car is essential — the trailheads are 10–30 km from town with no bus

properties.name: Akyaka
properties.desc: A village of white timber-fronted houses in the local Nail Çakırhan style at the head of the Gökova gulf, where a cold spring river meets the sea. Pine ridges rise straight behind it, the wind funnels down the gulf every afternoon, and a Cittaslow charter keeps the buildings low.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct — the meltemi turns July and August into a kitesurfing season
properties.tip: Take a flat-bottomed boat up the Azmak river at dusk to watch the springs boiling up through the weed and the kingfishers working; it beats the beach comfortably.
properties.rev: Visitors love the river, the architecture and the fish restaurants, and complain about the relentless afternoon wind, a small crowded beach and August weekend traffic from İzmir.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM) about 90 minutes, or Bodrum (BJV) about the same; Muğla–Marmaris buses stop at the Akyaka junction on the ridge

properties.name: Kuyucak Lavender Fields
properties.desc: A farming district in the upper Meander valley where growers have put lavender in among the figs and olives on the slopes towards Başaran and Pamukören. In late June the terraces go purple in stripes against grey olive, the air is loud with bees, and there is no ticket booth and no coach park.
properties.season: Late Jun–mid Jul for the flower; the rest of the year it is a working fig district
properties.tip: This is not the famous lavender village of the same name in Isparta; here the fields are scattered on private land, so ask at a village tea house before walking into a plot.
properties.rev: Those who come for the purple photographs are sometimes disappointed to find the plantings smaller and more scattered than in Isparta, but nobody complains about crowds or fees.
properties.onward: İzmir (ADB) about 2 hours or Denizli (DNZ) 1 hour; Kuyucak sits on the Aydın–Denizli road and the regional train stops in the town

properties.name: Alaşehir (Philadelphia)
properties.desc: The last of the Seven Churches of Revelation, and the last Byzantine city in Anatolia to fall. What survives is three huge brick piers of the sixth-century Church of St John, standing in a residential back street with frescoes still faintly visible under the arches. The surrounding hills are solid vineyard.
properties.season: Sep–Oct for the grape harvest; Apr–May for green hills — July and August are over 38 °C
properties.tip: The church piers are in a side street off the main road with one small sign; ask for Beş Eyvanlı Kilise and a local will point you, because the maps app frequently sends people wrong.
properties.rev: Pilgrims following the Seven Churches find it moving; independent travellers usually say there are twenty minutes of ruins in an unremarkable town and little else to justify the drive.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 2 h east via Salihli on the D300; the İzmir–Denizli regional train also calls here

properties.name: Kula Volcanic Geopark
properties.desc: Around eighty cinder cones and black basalt flows spread across the plateau east of Manisa, the youngest only a few thousand years old. The ancients called it Katakekaumene, the burnt land. Divlit cone can be climbed in half an hour, and near Sindel are human footprints pressed into volcanic ash perhaps twelve thousand years ago.
properties.season: Apr–May and Oct — the black rock radiates heat and July–Aug is brutal out there
properties.tip: The fossil footprints are fenced and easy to drive past; get the geopark map from Kula's visitor office first, because none of the cones are signposted from the main road.
properties.rev: Geology travellers rate it the most accessible volcanic field in Türkiye; everyone else notes bad tracks, no facilities, almost no interpretation on the ground and cones that look like slag heaps up close.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 2 h 15 east on the D300 via Salihli to Kula; a car is essential on the plateau

properties.name: Sultaniye Hot Springs
properties.desc: Sulphur water at around 39 °C rising on the south-west shore of Lake Köyceğiz, fed into an open pool and a domed Ottoman bath beside a small shrine. The mud pit next door is the same idea as Dalyan's with far fewer people, and you rinse off in the lake afterwards.
properties.season: Oct–May is the sweet spot — 39 °C water in August is unpleasant
properties.tip: Arrive by boat from Köyceğiz in the morning ahead of the Dalyan day-trip flotilla, and bring an old swimsuit, because the sulphur stains fabric permanently.
properties.rev: Bathers report the water genuinely helps aching joints, and warn about the powerful sulphur smell, basic changing rooms and midday crowds off the tour boats.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Köyceğiz; boats run from the town quay, or drive 25 km round the west shore on a partly unpaved road

properties.name: Karacasu
properties.desc: A hill town of tiled roofs and timber-framed houses that has made red earthenware for centuries; the potters' quarter still turns and fires by hand, and the local speciality is a wide unglazed casserole. Add the Sunday market, a couple of old coffee houses and the fact that Aphrodisias is fifteen minutes up the road.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — winter is cold and grey up here
properties.tip: Ask for the çömlekçiler mahallesi rather than the shops on the main road; the workshops sell the same pots at a third of the price and will fire a piece while you wait.
properties.rev: Travellers who stop on the way to Aphrodisias are surprised by how intact the old town is; the recurring gripe is that several workshops are closed on Mondays and the town has little accommodation.
properties.onward: Denizli Çardak (DNZ) about 1 hr 45, or İzmir (ADB) 2 hr 30; the town is on the road between the Aydın–Denizli motorway and Aphrodisias

properties.name: İztuzu Beach
properties.desc: A four-and-a-half kilometre sandbar separating the Dalyan delta from the open sea, river on one side and Mediterranean on the other. It is a loggerhead nesting beach, so it closes at eight in the evening, umbrellas are restricted to marked zones, and nothing has ever been built on it.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for swimming; May and Oct are quiet with the turtle rules still in force
properties.tip: Arrive by river boat at the far end rather than driving to the road entrance — the eastern half has the same sand and a fraction of the people.
properties.rev: Nearly everyone calls it the best undeveloped beach on the coast, then mentions the eight o'clock closure, the scarcity of shade and the trek from car park to water.
properties.entry: Free — small parking fee at the road entrance
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM) 30 minutes to Dalyan, then the river boat or 13 km of road around the delta; a summer dolmuş runs

properties.name: Kaunos
properties.desc: A Carian city that died when its harbour silted into marsh, leaving a theatre cut into the hillside, a Roman bath, a temple terrace and a Byzantine basilica standing above the reeds. The famous temple-façade rock tombs are half a kilometre downstream in the cliff, and are best seen from the water.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov — exposed site, and the marsh breeds mosquitoes in summer
properties.tip: Climb to the acropolis above the theatre for the view over the delta to İztuzu; hardly anyone goes up, and it is the only place the geography makes sense.
properties.rev: Most people rate the setting and the emptiness highly; the repeated complaints are a steep unshaded climb, mosquitoes near the marsh and rock tombs you cannot enter.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Dalyan; take the rowing ferry across the river and walk 20 minutes, or drive round via Çandır

properties.name: Dalyan
properties.desc: A river town where flat-bottomed boats thread reed channels between lake and sea, with the Lycian rock tombs of Kaunos carved into the cliff directly opposite the restaurant terraces. Loggerhead turtles come up the river to the fish weirs, and because the whole delta is protected, no hotel rises more than a few floors.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct — July and August are hot and the boat queues long
properties.tip: Use the little co-operative rowing ferry across to the tombs and the Kaunos path instead of booking a boat tour; it runs all day for the price of a coffee.
properties.rev: Visitors love the river, the tombs and the turtles, and complain about identical boat tours sold by every stall, mosquitoes at dusk and a main street that is now solid restaurants.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), 25 minutes by road — the shortest airport hop on this coast; dolmuş from Ortaca every half hour

properties.name: Kula Old Town
properties.desc: Some seven hundred timber-framed Ottoman houses on narrow lanes, many with painted ceilings and cumba bays overhanging the street, built by a town that grew rich on carpets and tanning. Restoration is patchy, so you walk past a perfect façade and then a collapsed one. Kula carpets are still woven here.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — the plateau hits 40 °C in summer and freezes in January
properties.tip: Walk the lanes around the Kurşunlu Mosque on a weekday morning when doors are open and someone will usually invite you in to see a painted ceiling.
properties.rev: Those who like unrestored Ottoman towns find it more honest than Şirince or Safranbolu; others are put off by the number of derelict houses, few places to eat and almost no tourist infrastructure.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then 2 h 15 east on the D300; intercity coaches on the İzmir–Uşak route stop in Kula

properties.name: Lake Köyceğiz
properties.desc: A large brackish lake joined to the sea by the Dalyan channel and ringed by sweetgum forest, the liquidambar that grows at this scale nowhere else. The water is warm, shallow and faintly sulphurous at the south end, and the lakefront at Köyceğiz town is a mile of plane trees and almost empty promenade.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov — mosquitoes are serious on summer evenings
properties.tip: Take the public boat from Köyceğiz town down the channel to Dalyan rather than a tour: the same route, a third of the price, and it calls at Sultaniye.
properties.rev: People find the town refreshingly untouristed and the lake beautiful at dawn; the standard complaints are mosquitoes, a muddy lake bottom and boatmen quoting three different prices.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), 45 minutes by road; all Marmaris–Fethiye buses stop at Köyceğiz otogar, five minutes from the lakefront

properties.name: Demirci
properties.desc: A highland town at 850 m in the far north of the province, cut off from the coast by pine ridges, known for hand-knotted Demirci carpets and for the coldest winters in Manisa. Old timber houses survive around the çarşı, there is a Byzantine castle on the hill, and the plateau above has springs and thin summer air.
properties.season: May–Oct — the road over the ridges is snowbound in stretches from December to March
properties.tip: Ask at the carpet cooperative rather than the shops on the main street; the co-op still has weavers working and will show you looms without a sales pitch.
properties.rev: Visitors who get there value the genuinely untouristed feel and the carpet workshops, while noting the long winding approach road, minimal accommodation and shops that shut early.
properties.onward: İzmir Adnan Menderes (ADB), then about 3 h north-east via Akhisar and Gördes; coaches run from Manisa and Akhisar

properties.name: Aphrodisias
properties.desc: A marble city in a poplar-shaded valley, quarried from the hillside above it, so the carving is everywhere: the stadium seats thirty thousand and is the best preserved anywhere, the Tetrapylon stands re-erected, and the Sebasteion reliefs in the museum show Claudius wrestling Britannia. Sheep still graze between the fallen column drums.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — winter mornings are foggy and the valley floods
properties.tip: Do the museum first so you recognise where the Sebasteion panels came from, then walk the loop anticlockwise to reach the stadium before the coaches from Pamukkale arrive at eleven.
properties.rev: Repeat visitors rate it above Ephesus for atmosphere because there is space to breathe, though the site is large, shadeless in the middle hours and the last stretch of road from the Denizli highway is slow.
properties.onward: Denizli Çardak (DNZ) or İzmir (ADB), then roughly 2 hours by road via Karacasu; there is no useful bus, so hire a car

properties.name: Yuvarlakçay
properties.desc: A spring-fed stream north-east of Köyceğiz running under plane trees so dense the water stays green and cold through August. Trout restaurants sit on platforms over the current, otters live in the banks, and villagers camped out for months to stop a hydro plant being built on it.
properties.season: Jun–Sep — the shade and the cold water are the whole point; winter is muddy
properties.tip: Go on a weekday: at summer weekends every platform table is booked by families from Muğla and Denizli, and the road in is single lane.
properties.rev: Visitors describe it as the coolest place in the province in August, and note that the restaurants are interchangeable and pricey, the parking chaotic and the water genuinely cold.
properties.entry: Free — the restaurants expect an order
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Köyceğiz and 12 km east on the Beyobası road; no bus, so drive or take a taxi

properties.name: Buldan
properties.desc: A weaving town on a wooded slope above the Meander, with several hundred restored timber and stone houses on stepped lanes, and looms still working behind shop fronts. The cloth — loose crinkled cotton scarves and shawls — is the local trade, and above the town the Süleymanlı highland has a lake and cool pine.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — the old town is steep and icy in winter
properties.tip: Go up to Süleymanlı Yaylası for lunch after the old town; it is fifteen minutes of hairpins and around ten degrees cooler than the valley in summer.
properties.rev: Visitors like the restored streets and cheap, genuine textiles; the recurring notes are that many houses are still derelict, parking is impossible in the old core and much of the town shuts on Sunday.
properties.onward: Denizli Çardak (DNZ) about 1 hr 15; Buldan is 45 minutes north-west of Denizli off the Aydın motorway, with regular buses from Denizli otogar

properties.name: Babadağ
properties.desc: A textile town clinging to a mountainside at 1,100 m, its houses stacked so steeply that one street's roofs are the next street's terraces. It is cold, quiet and unvisited, with plane-tree squares, spring water taps everywhere and a view straight down onto the Denizli plain and its lights at night.
properties.season: May–Oct — the road up is snowbound in parts of winter
properties.tip: Do not confuse it with Babadağ above Fethiye, which is the paragliding one; this Babadağ is a working town two hours away in the wrong direction if you booked a flight.
properties.rev: Those who make the climb describe an unusually intact hill town with real daily life and almost no tourism, alongside warnings about the narrow hairpin road and very limited places to eat or sleep.
properties.onward: Denizli Çardak (DNZ) about 1 hr 15; 35 km south-west of Denizli on a steep mountain road, with a few daily minibuses from Denizli otogar

properties.name: Twelve Islands
properties.desc: The archipelago in the Gulf of Göcek: Tersane with its abandoned Greek village and derelict shipyard, Yassıca with a sandbar you can walk across, Domuz with its private jetties, and Bedri Rahmi bay, where the painter left a fish on a rock in 1973. Every one of them has clear deep water.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct — August fills the anchorages and the meltemi builds after noon
properties.tip: Ask the skipper to reach Bedri Rahmi's painted rock before eleven; after that four gulets moor in front of it and the fish is invisible from the water.
properties.near: Tersane Adası, Göcek, Fethiye, Muğla, Türkiye
properties.rev: Day-trippers rate the water and the empty ruins highly, and complain that standard tours allow twenty minutes per stop, that the included lunch is mediocre and that August anchorages are crowded.
properties.entry: Free — you pay for the boat
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), 20 minutes to Göcek; boats leave the town quay around 10am, or charter a small boat with a skipper

properties.name: Göcek
properties.desc: A one-street town at the head of a gulf so sheltered that six marinas fit around it, with pine mountains coming down to the water. There is no beach worth the name and that is deliberate: Göcek exists for the boats, the chandleries and the twelve islands scattered across the gulf in front of it.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct — the gulet season either side of the August peak
properties.tip: You do not need to charter: the public taxi boats from the town quay run a fixed circuit of the bays each morning for a fraction of the day-tour price.
properties.rev: Sailors and repeat visitors love the anchorages and the low-key main street; the recurring complaints are marina prices, the absence of a real beach and how completely it empties in winter.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM) is 20 minutes away, the shortest transfer on this coast; Fethiye is 25 km on through the tunnel

properties.name: Tripolis on the Meander
properties.desc: A city on the river frontier between Lydia, Caria and Phrygia, excavated only in the last fifteen years and already showing a colonnaded street, a bath-basilica and a remarkable early Byzantine house with painted walls and its mosaic floors lifted and relaid. Cotton fields run to the edge of the trenches.
properties.season: Mar–May and Oct–Nov — flat, treeless and 40 °C in high summer
properties.tip: It is signposted off the Denizli–Sarayköy road at Yenicekent and free; ask the guard to unlock the covered house with the wall paintings, which is not always open by default.
properties.rev: Archaeology-minded visitors find the new digs genuinely exciting; casual visitors report an active building site with fencing, few explanatory panels and irregular opening.
properties.entry: Free at present — a ticket booth has been built, so expect a small fee
properties.onward: Denizli Çardak (DNZ) about 1 hour; on the Denizli–Buldan road at Yenicekent, 40 km from Denizli, car recommended

properties.name: Simav and Eynal Springs
properties.desc: A market town under Şaphane mountain with water coming out of the ground at Eynal, three kilometres away, hot enough that the town heats its buildings with it. The baths are plain municipal concrete rather than spas, and Simav's lake and the beech forests on Şaphane are what you do between soaks.
properties.season: Oct–Apr for the springs; Jun–Sep for the mountain and the lake
properties.tip: Ask the temperature of a pool before you get in — some of the Eynal baths run far hotter than visitors expect and there is nobody supervising.
properties.rev: Turkish spa-goers rate the water strength highly, and everyone notes the facilities are basic and dated, the town has little else for visitors, and almost nobody speaks English.
properties.onward: Kütahya, then 130 km west by minibus; Balıkesir or İzmir (ADB) are the nearest useful airports, roughly 3 hours away

properties.name: Güney Waterfall
properties.desc: Water dropping about thirty metres over a mossy travertine lip into a green plunge pool, with a stepped path that takes you behind the curtain into the hollow under the rock. The gorge below is thick with fig and plane, and the spray keeps the whole amphitheatre cold even in August.
properties.season: Mar–Jun for full flow; irrigation draws it down badly by late summer
properties.tip: Take the lower path that ducks behind the fall rather than only viewing from the terrace café; the steps are wet and unrailed in places, so proper shoes matter.
properties.rev: Locals treat it as a summer picnic spot and rate it; travellers report litter around the picnic tables, a much reduced flow in late summer and a slippery unfenced descent.
properties.entry: Free · small parking charge in season
properties.onward: Denizli Çardak (DNZ) about 1 hour; Güney is roughly 70 km north of Denizli via Çal, car needed as buses are infrequent

properties.name: Gemiler Island
properties.desc: An island covered end to end with a 5th–6th century Christian settlement: four basilicas, cisterns, tombs and a vaulted processional way climbing to a church on the summit. Some argue it was the original burial place of St Nicholas. You land at a jetty, pay a small fee and walk up through the whole thing.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct — no shade, and the boats stop in winter
properties.tip: The vaulted covered walkway on the north side is what most day-trippers miss, because it starts behind the second basilica rather than at the jetty.
properties.rev: Visitors find it far more substantial than expected, and warn about sharp loose stone underfoot, no shade or water on the island, and boat tours that allow barely an hour ashore.
properties.entry: ≈€5 landing fee plus the boat from Ölüdeniz or Karacaören
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Fethiye; boats go from Ölüdeniz and from the Gemiler beach road below Kayaköy

properties.name: Kayaköy
properties.desc: Around 350 roofless stone houses on a hillside, emptied in the 1923 population exchange when the Greek-speaking Orthodox inhabitants left and nobody moved in. Two basilicas keep fragments of painted plaster and pebble mosaic floors, the lanes are cobbled and stepped, and the silence at the top of the village is the point.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov — the hillside is punishing in July and August
properties.tip: Walk in from the top gate and come down through the village, then take the old mule path over the ridge to Ölüdeniz — about two hours, downhill at the end.
properties.rev: Most people find it genuinely moving and quiet, and note the loose cobbles, the complete absence of shade and a ticket that surprises those who remember when it was free.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Fethiye and a 20-minute dolmuş from the Ölüdeniz stand; the last one back leaves early evening

properties.name: Laodicea on the Lycus
properties.desc: One of the seven churches of Revelation, and now the largest active excavation in the region: a re-erected colonnaded street with the water pipes still in the pavement, two theatres cut into the hillside, and a fourth-century basilica under a modern shelter with its opus sectile floor intact.
properties.season: Mar–May and Oct–Nov — no shade at all on the plateau in summer
properties.tip: Go for the covered Church of Laodicea first thing; the shelter is locked outside main hours and the mosaic floor is the single best thing on site.
properties.rev: Biblical-tour groups and archaeology enthusiasts both rate it highly, while general visitors find it flat, hot and hard to read, and note the on-site café is minimal.
properties.onward: Denizli Çardak (DNZ) about 50 minutes; the site is 6 km north of Denizli centre on the Pamukkale road, easiest by taxi or car

properties.name: Tomb of Amyntas
properties.desc: A temple façade cut into the cliff above Fethiye in the 4th century BC: two Ionic columns, a pediment and a false door with iron studs rendered in stone, reached by a long flight of steps from the town. A Greek inscription names Amyntas son of Hermapias, and the whole bay opens out from the platform.
properties.season: Year-round; avoid the climb between noon and four in summer
properties.tip: Go up for sunset, when the rock turns orange and the tomb is floodlit from below, and pay at the kiosk rather than following the goat paths locals use.
properties.rev: Visitors call the façade and the view worth the steps, while noting that you cannot go inside, the site is small for the fee, and the staircase is steep with no handrail in places.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM) then Fethiye; the steps start a 15-minute walk uphill from the harbour, signposted off Kaya Caddesi

properties.name: Kabak Bay and Faralya
properties.desc: The last habitable notch on this coast before the cliffs take over. Faralya sits on the ridge with the Lycian Way running through it; Kabak is the bay 400 metres below, reached by a shuttle or a steep 45-minute path. Treehouse camps, no hotels, and no road down onto the beach itself.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct — most camps close from November to March
properties.tip: Do not attempt the descent to Kabak in flip-flops or after dark: the tractor shuttles stop in the evening and the path is loose scree in places.
properties.rev: Walkers and long-stayers rate the quiet and the star-filled nights, while noting basic plumbing, patchy electricity, cash-only camps and 25 km of continuous bends on the road in.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Fethiye and the Ölüdeniz–Faralya dolmuş, roughly every two hours in summer and twice a day in winter

properties.name: Fethiye
properties.desc: A harbour town rebuilt after the 1957 earthquake, so the fabric is plain — the setting is not. A broad bay full of islands, Lycian sarcophagi standing between apartment blocks, rock tombs above the roofline, and a fish market where you buy the fish and the surrounding restaurants cook it for a fixed price.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov — the town works year-round, unlike Ölüdeniz
properties.tip: At the fish market, choose from the stalls in the middle and hand it to any of the restaurants around them; the cooking charge per head is posted on the wall.
properties.rev: Long-stayers rate the market, the marina walk and the year-round life; complaints focus on a scruffy town beach at Çalış, heavy coast-road traffic and persistent timeshare touts.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), 50 minutes by road with a Havaş bus meeting most flights; long-distance buses run to İzmir and Antalya

properties.name: Pamukkale
properties.desc: A white calcite hillside 160 metres high, built up over millennia by hot springs depositing lime, with terraced pools you walk through barefoot in warm shin-deep water. Only a strip of the terraces is open and the flow is rotated between them, so half the cascade is usually dry chalk rather than blue basins.
properties.season: Apr–May and Oct — winter is cold on wet bare feet, August is a queue in 38 °C
properties.tip: Enter at the lower south gate and walk up the travertines against the flow at sunrise, or arrive after four for the sunset light; midday is when every tour bus from the coast unloads.
properties.rev: The colour genuinely delivers at the right hour, but visitors regularly report dry terraces, compulsory bare feet on sharp calcite, drone bans and a ticket price that has risen sharply.
properties.entry: ≈€35 combined with Hierapolis · Antique Pool ≈€25 extra · Museum Pass covers the site but not the pool
properties.onward: Denizli Çardak (DNZ) about 1 hour by road, or the İzmir–Denizli train then a 20-minute dolmuş from Denizli otogar

properties.name: Hierapolis
properties.desc: The Roman spa city on top of the travertines, and much larger than people expect: a theatre with its stage building restored to full height and carved friezes of Apollo, a colonnaded main street a kilometre long, and a necropolis of some twelve hundred tombs spread over the ridge to the north.
properties.season: Apr–May and Oct — the plateau is shadeless and brutal Jul–Aug
properties.tip: Walk north past the Martyrium of St Philip to the necropolis; it is twenty minutes from the crowds and you will usually have twelve hundred tombs to yourself.
properties.rev: Often the surprise of the trip for people who came only for the white terraces; the standard complaints are the distances between monuments, no shade, and a museum in the Roman baths that closes earlier than the site.
properties.entry: ≈€35 combined with Pamukkale · covered by Museum Pass Türkiye
properties.onward: Denizli Çardak (DNZ) about 1 hour; dolmuşes run from Denizli otogar to Pamukkale village every 20 minutes and the north gate is a taxi ride from there

properties.name: Butterfly Valley
properties.desc: A steep-sided gorge dropping to a shingle beach, reachable only by boat from Ölüdeniz or a rope-assisted scramble down from Faralya. Jersey tiger moths breed here in summer, there is a waterfall an hour up the valley bed, and the accommodation at the bottom is bungalows and hammocks rather than hotels.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for the moths and the boats; the descent path is dangerous when wet
properties.tip: Take the last boat back or stay the night — day-trippers get ninety minutes, and the valley only becomes itself after the four o'clock boat leaves.
properties.rev: People love the beach once the boats leave, and repeatedly warn that the cliff path from Faralya has killed walkers, that facilities are basic and that the moths are strictly seasonal.
properties.entry: ≈€10 boat return from Ölüdeniz plus a small valley fee
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Fethiye and Ölüdeniz; boats leave the Belcekız beach jetty several times a day in season

properties.name: Ölüdeniz
properties.desc: The lagoon everyone has seen on a poster: a hooked spit of white shingle enclosing water that goes from clear to turquoise to deep blue within twenty metres, with Babadağ rising 1,900 metres directly behind. The lagoon is a protected nature park with nothing built on it; the resort strip sits round the corner on Belcekız beach.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct — August is very hot and the beach is shoulder to shoulder
properties.tip: Pay the small nature-park fee and go through to the lagoon proper instead of staying on the free Belcekız side: calmer water, and the paragliders land on the other beach.
properties.rev: The colour of the water gets universal praise; the complaints are relentless — sunbed prices, crowds by ten in the morning, sharp shingle underfoot and a resort strip with no charm.
properties.entry: ≈₺150 (≈€3.50) for the lagoon nature park; Belcekız beach is free
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Fethiye and a 25-minute dolmuş that runs every few minutes in season

properties.name: Lycian Way (Western Half)
properties.desc: The first 200 kilometres of Türkiye's original long-distance path, from Ovacık above Ölüdeniz along the cliffs through Faralya and Kabak to Sidyma and the Xanthos valley. It is the hardest and most spectacular section: sea on one side, the Boncuk range on the other, and villages where the pension is somebody's spare room.
properties.season: Mar–May and Oct–Nov — summer on the exposed cliffs is dangerous
properties.tip: Carry three litres per person: the springs marked on older maps are unreliable after June, and several villages on this stretch no longer have a shop.
properties.rev: Walkers rate the coastal views as the best in the country, and consistently report vague waymarking after storms, long waterless stretches and ankle-turning limestone.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Fethiye and a dolmuş to Ovacık for the western trailhead; luggage transfer companies operate along the route

properties.name: Akhan Caravanserai
properties.desc: A Seljuk han of 1253 in white marble on the old road east out of Denizli, with a carved portal, an open courtyard and a covered hall of pointed arches behind it. Lions and rosettes are cut into the doorway. It is small, complete, free, and sits on a roundabout that almost everyone drives past.
properties.season: All year — the covered hall is cool in summer and dry in winter
properties.tip: The gate keeper's hours are loose; if the outer door is shut, walk round to the eastern side where the courtyard wall is low enough to see the whole plan.
properties.rev: People are pleased to find a genuinely intact Seljuk han for nothing, and equally quick to say it takes twenty minutes, sits beside a busy road and is occasionally locked without warning.
properties.onward: Denizli Çardak (DNZ) about 40 minutes; 7 km east of Denizli centre on the old Afyon road, any Honaz-bound dolmuş passes it

properties.name: Babadağ
properties.desc: The 1,969-metre mountain behind Ölüdeniz and one of the most reliable paragliding sites anywhere: the takeoff ramps sit at roughly 1,700 and 1,965 metres and the glide down over the lagoon lasts half an hour. A cable car now runs to the top, so you can take the view and the summit terrace without jumping off anything.
properties.season: Apr–Oct for flying; the cable car runs most of the year but wind closes it
properties.tip: Book the first flight of the morning — the air is smoothest before ten, and by afternoon the thermals turn it rough enough that queasy passengers regret it.
properties.rev: Flyers call it the highlight of the trip, with common warnings about wind cancellations, hard sell on video packages and a bumpy jeep ride up if you fly rather than ride the cable car.
properties.entry: Cable car ≈€25 return; tandem flights ≈€90–130 depending on the ramp
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Fethiye and the Ölüdeniz dolmuş; the cable car base station is at the inland end of the Ölüdeniz valley

properties.name: Blaundus
properties.desc: A Hellenistic city on a spur almost entirely surrounded by canyon, so the only approach is a narrow neck with the city gate still standing across it. Inside are a temple of Demeter, a stadium, rock-cut tombs in the cliff walls and a Byzantine church, with farmland worked in between the ruins.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — the plateau hits 40 °C in July and freezes in January
properties.tip: Walk out to the far end of the spur past the last field: the canyon drops away on three sides, and that is the view the city was built for.
properties.rev: The handful of visitors call it one of the most dramatically sited ruins in the country, and report no ticket office, no signage, no shade and a village road that needs care after rain.
properties.onward: Uşak (USQ) or the train to Uşak, then 40 km south via Ulubey to Sülümenli; a car is essential

properties.name: Cadyanda
properties.desc: A Lycian hill city at 1,000 metres above Üzümlü, set in pine forest with a stadium, a theatre, baths and a paved road still showing cart ruts. The loop path runs under trees, which makes it the one Lycian site you can walk at midday in July, and the view drops all the way to Fethiye bay.
properties.season: May–Oct; the access road can be icy in winter
properties.tip: Follow the marked forest loop anticlockwise so you reach the stadium first — most people turn back at the baths and never see the best-preserved part.
properties.rev: Walkers like the shade and the emptiness; the recurring complaints are a steep narrow access road, minimal signage on site and a ticket booth that is often unstaffed.
properties.entry: Small fee — check locally · Museum Pass usually accepted
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Fethiye and 20 km northeast to Üzümlü, then 4 km of steep forest road to the gate

properties.name: Pinara
properties.desc: A Lycian city under a vertical cliff honeycombed with hundreds of rectangular tomb openings, cut so high they can only have been reached on ropes. Below, oaks grow through a theatre that still has its stage building, and the Royal Tomb carries a relief of a walled city. Cattle graze between the ruins.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov — the access track is bad after winter rain
properties.tip: The last two kilometres are steep gravel switchbacks, so leave a low car in the village and walk up, and allow two hours because the site is spread through woodland.
properties.rev: Those who make it call it the most atmospheric site in Lycia because they were alone; the consistent warnings are the rough access road, overgrown paths, snakes in summer and no facilities at all.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Fethiye and 45 km south on the D400 to Minare village; a high-clearance car helps on the final climb

properties.name: Colossae
properties.desc: A grass-covered mound in a field below Honaz, with a theatre hollow you can trace by eye and potsherds turning up in the ploughed earth. Paul wrote a letter to the people who lived here and essentially nothing has been dug. What you get is the shape of a city and Mount Honaz filling the sky behind it.
properties.season: Mar–May and Oct–Nov — the track is mud after rain
properties.tip: Climb the höyük for the view rather than expecting ruins; the visible cut of the theatre is on the north slope facing the Lycus, and it is easiest to find in the low light of early morning.
properties.rev: Pilgrims come for the name and often leave disappointed because there is literally nothing built to see; those who treat it as a walk in a field with a good view are the ones who enjoy it.
properties.onward: Denizli Çardak (DNZ) about 45 minutes; 3 km north-west of Honaz town on a signposted farm road, car needed

properties.name: Mount Honaz
properties.desc: At 2,571 m the highest peak in the Aegean region, rising straight off the Lycus plain in one 2,000-metre wall. A national park road climbs through black pine and cedar to alpine meadow, and from the ridge you see Pamukkale's white scar, Lake Acıgöl and, on a clear day, the Bey mountains.
properties.season: Jun–Oct for the summit; snow closes the upper road roughly Dec–Apr
properties.tip: Start from Karateke picnic area rather than Honaz town — it cuts about 700 m of climbing — and carry all your water, because the springs on the ridge dry up by July.
properties.rev: Hikers rate the summit view as one of the best in western Türkiye and warn that the ascent is long, unmarked in places, and that the forest road is rough and gated in winter.
properties.entry: Small national park fee — check locally; usually charged per vehicle at the forest gate
properties.onward: Denizli Çardak (DNZ) about 45 minutes to Honaz, then a forest road up to the park; four-wheel drive is helpful above the picnic areas

properties.name: Letoon
properties.desc: The federal sanctuary of the Lycian League: three temples side by side to Leto, Apollo and Artemis on a plain where the water table has risen so far that half the site is now a pond full of frogs and terrapins. The trilingual stele found here, in Lycian, Greek and Aramaic, is how the Lycian language was cracked.
properties.season: Mar–Jun and Sep–Nov — the flooded section is deepest after winter rain
properties.tip: Come late in the afternoon when the columns reflect in the standing water; that reflection is the photograph and it does not work at midday.
properties.rev: People find it small but unusually atmospheric, and note the flooding, the mosquitoes, the modest theatre and the fact that the famous stele is in Fethiye museum rather than on site.
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Fethiye and about an hour southeast via Eşen to Kumluova; no useful bus, so drive

properties.name: Ulubey Canyon
properties.desc: A canyon system cut into the Uşak plateau by the Banaz stream, running for tens of kilometres through soft rock. A glass viewing terrace hangs off the rim, poplars and walnut line the river 150 metres below, and a footpath drops to the water where kingfishers work the shallows.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov — the descent path is slippery in winter and airless in August
properties.tip: The glass terrace is the postcard, but the path down from the rim to the riverbed is where the canyon actually feels big; allow two hours for the climb back.
properties.rev: People rate the terrace and the scale of the gorge, and complain about a fee for what is essentially a viewpoint, litter at the picnic areas and weekend crowds from Uşak.
properties.entry: ≈₺100 (≈€2.50) per car for the nature park
properties.onward: Uşak (USQ) or the İzmir–Afyon train to Uşak, then 25 km south to Ulubey; minibuses run but not as far as the terrace

properties.name: Uşak Archaeological Museum
properties.desc: A small provincial museum holding the Karun Treasure: Lydian gold looted from tumuli near Güre in the 1960s, sold to the Met, and returned in 1993 after a long court fight. The winged seahorse brooch was then stolen by the museum's own director and replaced with a fake, and only came back from Germany in 2012.
properties.season: Year-round; closed Mondays
properties.tip: Ask specifically for the seahorse brooch and the wall paintings lifted from the Aktepe tumulus — both are easy to walk past in a room full of small gold objects.
properties.rev: Visitors find the treasure remarkable and the museum itself small and quickly seen, with limited English labelling and a story the displays badly underplay.
properties.onward: Uşak is on the İzmir–Afyon rail line and has a small airport (USQ) with Istanbul flights; the museum is central

properties.name: Saklıkent Gorge
properties.desc: An eighteen-kilometre slot cut through the Akdağ massif, entered on a boardwalk pinned to the wall above the river. Where the boardwalk ends you wade an icy blue torrent coming straight out of the mountain, then walk upstream between walls two hundred metres high that narrow to a few metres apart.
properties.season: May–Oct; snowmelt flood closes the gorge from November to April
properties.tip: Rent the rubber shoes at the entrance and go early — by midday the first ford is a queue, and the water is genuinely too cold to stand in for long.
properties.rev: Most people call the first kilometre spectacular and then complain about the cold water, the crowded boardwalk, the stalls at the entrance and tour buses arriving in convoy from Fethiye.
properties.entry: ≈₺200 (≈€5) national park entry; not covered by the Museum Pass
properties.onward: Dalaman (DLM), then Fethiye and 45 km east via Kemer; day tours usually combine it with Tlos

properties.name: Tlos
