properties.desc: A volcanic crater on the Karapınar steppe with a second, smaller cone rising out of the middle of it — a maar within a maar, once ringed by red salt water that photographed like a wound in the plain. Groundwater extraction has dried much of it; what remains is white salt crust, rust-coloured scoria and total silence.
properties.season: Mar–May and Oct–Nov — summer heat and glare are punishing
properties.tip: Do not expect the postcard water; go for the geology and the light, and stop at the viewpoint layby on the Karapınar–Ereğli road rather than driving down to the rim.
properties.rev: Still striking, but almost every recent report leads with disappointment that the lake has essentially dried up, and there are no facilities, shade or signage at the viewpoint.
properties.onward: Konya (KYA) airport, then 100 km east on the D330 towards Ereğli; the crater is signposted just off the highway past Karapınar.

properties.name: Ilgaz Mountain National Park
properties.desc: The range that separates the Anatolian plateau from the Black Sea, rising to 2,587 m with fir and pine forest on the northern slopes and a small, cheap ski centre at Yıldıztepe. In summer the meadows above the treeline are full of wildflowers and the ridge walk gives you the plateau on one side and the sea haze on the other.
properties.season: Dec–Mar for skiing; Jun–Sep for the meadows and ridge walks
properties.tip: Ski here midweek — it is a fraction of Uludağ's price with short lifts and no queues, but weekends bring Ankara and Kastamonu day crowds all at once.
properties.rev: Well liked for value and forest scenery, with recurring complaints about short and dated lifts, thin snow in mild winters, and basic hotel food at the ski centre.
properties.entry: Small national park vehicle fee · ski passes charged separately
properties.onward: Ankara Esenboğa (ESB) airport, then 190 km north via Çankırı on the D765 towards Kastamonu; the ski centre is signed off the pass.

properties.name: Kaman-Kalehöyük
properties.desc: A mound dug by Japanese archaeologists since 1986, its four superimposed levels running from the Early Bronze Age through Hittite and Phrygian to Ottoman — one of the cleanest stratigraphies in Anatolia. The site museum is buried into the hillside, and a Japanese garden with a teahouse sits next to it.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; the garden is at its best in late spring
properties.tip: Come on a summer weekday during the dig season and you can watch the excavation from the viewing path, which is the only time the trenches are open.
properties.rev: Praised for a genuinely good small museum and an unexpectedly serene Japanese garden; the caveats are that the mound itself is bare earth outside the dig season, opening hours are short, and it is well off any normal route.
properties.onward: Ankara (ESB) airport, then 100 km southeast via Kaman; buses run Ankara–Kaman, then a taxi to Çağırkan

properties.name: Ereğli
properties.desc: A working plains town at the foot of the Taurus that most people use as a base for İvriz and Karadağ. Its own draws are quiet: a good small archaeological museum, the Akhüyük thermal mud pools, and a reputation across Türkiye for its cherries. The Taurus wall standing behind the flat wheat gives the place its horizon.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — cherry season is late May into June
properties.tip: Use it as a bed rather than a destination: İvriz, the obruks and Binbir Kilise are all within an hour, and Ereğli has the only decent hotels among them.
properties.rev: Practical and friendly rather than pretty; travellers mention limited evening options, a dusty industrial edge, and that the museum keeps short hours.
properties.onward: Konya (KYA) airport, then 150 km east on the D330; Ereğli is also a stop on the Konya–Adana rail line and on all intercity buses.

properties.name: Ağzıkara Han
properties.desc: A Seljuk caravanserai of 1231 on the old Konya–Kayseri road, with a carved portal, an open summer courtyard and a vaulted winter hall where camels and merchants slept in the same space. A small mosque stands on piers in the middle of the yard. Traffic on the modern highway roars past outside.
properties.season: Year-round; the covered hall is cold and unheated in midwinter
properties.tip: It sits right on the Aksaray–Nevşehir highway, so it costs you ten minutes on the drive between Cappadocia and Ihlara — most people never notice it.
properties.rev: Visitors find it atmospheric and almost always empty, with the usual caveats: restoration has left some walls looking new, the caretaker's hours are informal, and there is nothing to do there beyond half an hour of looking.
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) airport, then 15 km east of Aksaray directly on the D300 highway

properties.name: Cacabey Madrasa
properties.desc: A 1272 Seljuk madrasa built as an astronomical observatory, with a shaft in the courtyard floor used for star sightings and planetary symbols carved on the portal. It has served as a mosque since the Ottoman period, so you take your shoes off to see the vaulting and the blue-tiled eyvan.
properties.season: Year-round; visit outside the five prayer times
properties.tip: Look for the observation well in the middle of the floor and the tomb chamber on the left — the caretaker will explain the astronomy if you ask, and nobody volunteers it.
properties.rev: Visitors find the observatory story fascinating and the building small but genuine; the drawbacks are that it functions as a working mosque with restricted hours, the interior is heavily replastered, and Kırşehir itself sees very few travellers.
properties.onward: Ankara (ESB) airport 190 km or Kayseri (ASR) 150 km; the madrasa is on the main square in Kırşehir

properties.name: Mount Hasan
properties.desc: The 3,268-metre twin-peaked volcano that supplied the tuff all of Cappadocia is carved from, and possibly the mountain painted on a wall at Çatalhöyük 8,000 years ago. The walk from Karbeyaz plateau to the summit takes six hours through scree and old lava, with Tuz Gölü glinting to the north.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for the summit; snow lies on the cone into May and returns in October
properties.tip: Start from the Helvadere side before 05:00 — the ridge above 2,800 m is loose volcanic scree and the wind picks up hard by early afternoon.
properties.rev: Climbers call it a straightforward but long scree slog with a huge view; the warnings are consistent — no water above the plateau, fast weather changes, an unmaintained upper path and a rough track to the trailhead.
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) or Kayseri (ASR) airport, then Aksaray and 30 km south to Helvadere; a car is essential

properties.name: İvriz Rock Relief
properties.desc: A four-metre Neo-Hittite god of grain and wine holds out barley ears and a bunch of grapes to a small, praying king, carved into the rock beside a spring that still gushes into a poplar valley below the Taurus. The eighth-century BC hieroglyphs name Warpalawas of Tuwana. The water, the fig trees and the carving all belong to the same place.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct — the spring valley is a cool refuge in high summer
properties.tip: Go in the morning; by afternoon the relief is in flat shade and the carved detail on the god's robe disappears entirely.
properties.rev: Consistently described as one of Anatolia's most beautiful reliefs in one of its prettiest settings, spoiled a little by picnic litter, loud weekend crowds and a scruffy car park.
properties.onward: Konya (KYA) airport, then 150 km southeast to Ereğli and 17 km south towards Halkapınar; also reachable from Ereğli by taxi.

properties.name: Nora (Viranşehir) and Helvadere
properties.desc: The Hellenistic fortress where Eumenes of Cardia held out against Antigonus for a year in 320 BC, now a scatter of Byzantine chapels, cisterns and walls on a spur above Helvadere village. The trout restaurants by the reservoir below and the Hasan Dağı trailhead make it a good half-day.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; the site is exposed and the track muddy after rain
properties.tip: Ask in Helvadere for the Viranşehir track rather than trusting the map — the last kilometre is a farm road and the ruins are unsigned from the village.
properties.rev: Rewarding for people who like empty ruins and a view of Hasan Dağı; everyone else reports there is very little standing, no information boards, no ticket office and a rough approach that a low car will not enjoy.
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) or Kayseri (ASR) airport, then Aksaray and 30 km south to Helvadere; car only

properties.name: Aşıklı Höyük
properties.desc: A 10,000-year-old aceramic Neolithic mound on the Melendiz stream, older than Çatalhöyük, where people entered their mud-brick houses through the roof and buried their dead under the floors. Experimental reconstructions stand next to the excavation so you can see how the packed settlement actually worked.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; excavation season runs in summer, when you may see work in progress
properties.tip: Go on a weekday in July or August and there is a decent chance an archaeologist on site will show you the trench and the roof-entry houses.
properties.rev: Archaeology travellers find it genuinely important and free, while everyone else warns it is a low brown mound with minimal interpretation, no facilities, no shade, and a bumpy access track off the Ihlara road.
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) or Kayseri (ASR) airport, then the Aksaray–Ihlara road; 25 km southeast of Aksaray, car only

properties.name: Selime Monastery
properties.desc: The largest rock-cut complex in Cappadocia, at the north mouth of the Ihlara canyon: a basilica-sized cathedral hall with columns hewn from the rock, a kitchen with a soaring chimney, stables with feed troughs, and rooms opening onto sheer drops. The cone-topped village below is half cave, half stone.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; the polished rock ramps are lethal when wet or icy
properties.tip: Wear grippy shoes — the entry ramp is worn smooth and steep, and it is the single most common place people fall in Cappadocia.
properties.rev: Frequently the surprise favourite of an Ihlara day and vast enough to lose people in, though visitors flag the slippery unprotected ramps, no railings above long drops, and tour groups given only twenty minutes for a site that deserves an hour.
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) or Nevşehir (NAV) airport, then via Aksaray to the top of the Ihlara valley; part of every Green Tour

properties.name: Ihlara Valley
properties.desc: A 14 km canyon cut 100 metres into the plateau by the Melendiz river, green with poplars and willows where everything above is bare steppe. Around forty rock churches open off the walls — Yılanlı with its snake-punished sinners, Kokar with a hand of God on the ceiling. A staircase of 382 steps drops you in.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; the canyon floor stays cool when the plateau is at 35 °C
properties.tip: Start at Ihlara village and walk downstream to Belisırma, then arrange a taxi back — the standard tour drops everyone at the mid-valley stair and sees a third of it.
properties.rev: Rated the best walk in Cappadocia for shade and water, with recurring complaints about the 382-step descent on the return, several churches locked or fenced, and the riverside restaurant platforms at Belisırma charging tourist prices for ordinary trout.
properties.entry: ≈€10 for the valley · covered by Museum Pass Türkiye
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) or Nevşehir (NAV) airport, then 100 km southwest via Aksaray; buses run Aksaray–Ihlara, but a car is far easier

properties.name: Güzelyurt (Gelveri)
properties.desc: A Greek town of cut-stone houses stacked above the Manastır valley, where the 4th-century church of St Gregory of Nazianzus became a mosque in 1924 and kept its Byzantine bones. A monastery valley runs below with dozens of rock chapels, and the Sivişli church still has its frescoes.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; snow closes the higher lanes in January
properties.tip: Ask at the Kilise Camii for the key to the Sivişli church down the valley — it is kept in the village and not advertised anywhere.
properties.rev: Travellers rate it the most intact Greek-Cappadocian town after Sinasos and pleasantly untouristed, but note that half the churches need a key from someone who has gone to lunch and there are only a handful of places to eat.
properties.entry: Village free · Kilise Camii and monastery valley ≈₺150 (€3.50)
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) or Kayseri (ASR) airport, then via Aksaray; 12 km from Ihlara, best combined with it by car

properties.name: Lake Seyfe
properties.desc: A shallow soda lake on the steppe east of Kırşehir, a Ramsar site where flamingos breed and thousands of waders stop on migration. There is no infrastructure beyond a track around the reedbeds and a hide — you park, walk to the shore, and listen to steppe larks with nobody else in sight.
properties.season: Apr–May and Sep–Oct for migration; the lake can dry out entirely by late summer
properties.tip: Approach from the Seyfe village side in the morning with the sun behind you — the western shore turns the birds into silhouettes all day.
properties.rev: Birders value the flamingo colony and the absolute quiet, while every account notes falling water levels from irrigation, a lake that is sometimes just a salt crust in August, rough tracks and no facilities whatsoever.
properties.onward: Ankara (ESB) or Kayseri (ASR) airport, then Kırşehir and 30 km east towards Mucur; car essential

properties.name: Narlıgöl Crater Lake
properties.desc: A maar lake in a volcanic crater on the Melendiz range, green-blue and about 500 metres across, with hot springs bubbling up at the edge and a small thermal bath built over them. The rim road gives you the whole bowl at once; the water is sulphurous and warm where the springs enter.
properties.season: Year-round; the thermal pools are best in Oct–Apr when the air is cold
properties.tip: The spring water on the north shore runs at around 45 °C — go in the late afternoon on a winter day, when locals rather than tourists are in the pools.
properties.rev: Visitors like the strangeness of a warm lake in bare steppe and the near-total absence of foreigners; the complaints are basic and rundown bath facilities, a strong sulphur smell, litter on the shore and an unsigned turn-off.
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) or Kayseri (ASR) airport, then the Niğde–Aksaray back road via Çiftlik; car only

properties.name: Hacı Bektaş Veli Complex
properties.desc: The spiritual centre of Anatolian Alevism and Bektashi Sufism: three courtyards, a kitchen with the cauldron that fed dervishes, and the tomb of Hacı Bektaş Veli under a fluted dome. Pilgrims touch the threshold stone rather than step on it. The atmosphere is devotional, not archaeological.
properties.season: Year-round; the August 16–18 commemoration fills the town completely
properties.tip: Come outside the August festival if you want the tomb quiet, and note that visitors are expected not to tread on the marble threshold at the inner gate.
properties.rev: Turkish visitors describe it as moving and quietly maintained; foreign visitors report almost no English signage, a museum layout that assumes you know the tradition, and a bleak 45 km drive across steppe to reach it.
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) airport, then 45 km northwest by road; buses from Nevşehir otogar run several times a day

properties.name: Tyana (Kemerhisar)
properties.desc: The chief city of southern Cappadocia and home of Apollonius of Tyana, now a Roman aqueduct marching across a village at the edge of Kemerhisar, plus a spring-fed pool the Romans built and a mosaic-floored basilica under excavation. Locals still water fields from the same source.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; Bor plain summers are hot and shadeless
properties.tip: The Roman pool by the spring is on the far side of the village from the aqueduct arches — most visitors photograph the arches and drive off without finding it.
properties.rev: Ancient-history travellers enjoy piecing the city together, though reports agree it is thoroughly built over by the modern village, the excavation areas are fenced and often closed, and there is no visitor centre of any kind.
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) or Adana (ADA) airport, then Niğde and 20 km southwest via Bor; dolmuş from Niğde to Kemerhisar

properties.name: Church of St Jean, Gülşehir
properties.desc: A two-storey rock church whose upper chapel was cleaned of soot in 1995, revealing 1212-dated frescoes in reds and blues so fresh they look wrong — a Last Judgment, a whale swallowing Jonah, Christ on a ladder. It is the most vivid painted interior in Cappadocia and almost nobody stops here.
properties.season: Year-round; the interior is dim on overcast days
properties.tip: The lower level is unpainted and easy to mistake for the whole church — the stair to the frescoed upper chapel is around the outside to the right.
properties.rev: Those who find it call the colour better than anything at Göreme and the solitude remarkable; the complaints are erratic opening hours, a caretaker who sometimes is not there, and no signage at all from the main road.
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) airport, then 20 km north on the Kırşehir road; dolmuş from Nevşehir, then a short walk

properties.name: Devrent Valley
properties.desc: A small lunar bowl between Zelve and Avanos with no churches and nothing carved — just eroded pale rock that reads as camels, seals and hooded figures depending on where you stand. It takes twenty minutes to walk and works best in flat morning light when the shapes have edges.
properties.season: Year-round; best in the first hour after sunrise
properties.tip: The camel rock everyone photographs is on the right of the road, but the better ground is the unmarked path uphill on the left, where nobody goes.
properties.rev: Fine as a fifteen-minute stop and free, but frequently described as the weakest item on the standard Red Tour — coaches unload, everyone shoots the camel, and the souvenir stalls outnumber the formations.
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) airport, then the Avanos–Ürgüp road; it is a roadside stop 5 km from Zelve

properties.name: Nevşehir Castle
properties.desc: A Seljuk fortress on the rock above the provincial capital, mostly walls and a keep, with the whole city and the Kaymaklı-scale underground complex of Kayaşehir beneath it — found in 2013 during a demolition and thought to be the largest in the region. The castle itself takes twenty minutes.
properties.season: Year-round; the ramparts are windy and exposed all winter
properties.tip: Combine it with the Kurşunlu Mosque complex and the Damat İbrahim Paşa library below — the castle alone does not justify the drive into Nevşehir.
properties.rev: Locals use it as a viewpoint and it is free, but travellers report a heavily rebuilt structure with little original fabric, the Kayaşehir underground city still not properly open to visitors, and a city that most people only pass through.
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) airport 25 km, or Kayseri (ASR) 100 km; all regional dolmuş routes pass the Nevşehir otogar

properties.name: Derinkuyu Underground City
properties.desc: Eighteen storeys cut into the tuff, eight of them open, going down 60 metres to a cruciform church and a 55-metre ventilation shaft that still draws cool air. Half-tonne millstone doors could be rolled shut from inside at each level. Thousands of people and their livestock sheltered here from raids.
properties.season: Year-round; a constant 13 °C makes it the best stop on a 35 °C July day
properties.tip: Go at opening or after 16:00 — mid-morning the single stooped staircase becomes two-way traffic and you queue underground, which is where claustrophobia usually starts.
properties.rev: Staggering as an engineering feat, but the reports are consistent: long crouched passages, genuine bottlenecks when two groups meet, poor air in peak season, and a visit that lasts about 45 minutes for a rising ticket price.
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) airport 30 km, then the Niğde road; dolmuş from Nevşehir otogar every 30 minutes

properties.name: Kaymaklı Underground City
properties.desc: Wider and lower than Derinkuyu, built around a central ventilation shaft with rooms fanning out from it — stables on the first level, a chapel, then kitchens with blackened ceilings and basalt blocks for grinding copper ore. Villagers above still use the top-level cellars for storage.
properties.season: Year-round; steady 13 °C, welcome in July and August
properties.tip: Follow the red arrows down and blue arrows up religiously — people who improvise end up crawling against the flow in a 1.2-metre-high tunnel.
properties.rev: Generally described as easier and less claustrophobic than Derinkuyu with lower ceilings but shorter passages; complaints centre on tight two-way traffic at peak times, hawkers at the entrance, and guides rushing groups through in half an hour.
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) airport 20 km on the Niğde road; frequent dolmuş from Nevşehir, 20 km short of Derinkuyu

properties.name: Gümüşler Monastery
properties.desc: A rock-cut monastery around a courtyard sunk into the cliff, unknown until 1963 and therefore never vandalised. Its main church holds the only smiling Virgin in Byzantine art, still in original colour, plus a rare secular fresco of hunting scenes. There are grain pits, a crypt and a rock-cut tomb in the floor.
properties.season: Year-round; interiors are dim, so go on a bright day and skip early morning
properties.tip: Look up in the west chapel for the hunting fresco with a griffin — the caretaker will point out the smiling Virgin, but almost nobody is shown the secular painting.
properties.rev: Consistently called the best-preserved frescoes in Cappadocia with a fraction of the visitors, though people note it is a plain suburb of Niğde, signage is thin, and the site takes only forty minutes once you have driven out here.
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) airport 130 km, or Adana (ADA); 10 km northeast of Niğde, dolmuş from the town centre

properties.name: Yozgat Çamlığı National Park
properties.desc: Türkiye's first national park, declared in 1958, and one of its smallest — a surviving stand of old black pine on a ridge above Yozgat that was once the town's private hunting wood. Some trees are over 500 years old. It is a park in the municipal sense as much as the wild one, but the pines are the real survivors of a forest that used to cover the plateau.
properties.season: May–Oct for walking; Dec–Feb for snow under the pines
properties.tip: Go on a weekday: at weekends the picnic areas fill with Yozgat families and the mangal smoke sits under the trees all afternoon.
properties.rev: Pleasant, shady and historically interesting as the country's first park, but visitors note it is small, heavily used for picnics, and littered after busy weekends.
properties.onward: Ankara Esenboğa (ESB) airport, then 220 km east on the D200; the park entrance is 5 km south of Yozgat town.

properties.name: Pigeon Valley
properties.desc: The 4 km link between Göreme and Uçhisar, its cliffs drilled with thousands of hand-cut pigeon holes, many with painted red-ochre borders to guide the birds home. Farmers collected the droppings for the vineyards for centuries. The path ends climbing to Uçhisar castle with the whole plateau behind you.
properties.season: Mar–Jun and Sep–Nov; parts flood briefly after spring storms
properties.tip: Walk it uphill from Göreme to Uçhisar in the late afternoon and take the dolmuş back — the reverse leaves you climbing into the sun.
properties.rev: An easy, shaded, genuinely quiet walk by Cappadocian standards; the complaints are the evil-eye tree viewpoint being a tour-bus scrum, litter near the Göreme end, and a couple of short scrambles that surprise people in the wrong shoes.
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) or Nevşehir (NAV) airport, then Göreme; dolmuş from Uçhisar back to Göreme runs roughly hourly

properties.name: Uçhisar
properties.desc: A single tuff outcrop riddled with rooms, tunnels and tombs, rising above a village of cave houses at the highest point in Cappadocia. From the top you see Erciyes, Hasan Dağı and every valley at once. The lanes below still have collapsed dwellings that people moved out of in the 1960s.
properties.season: Year-round; the summit platform is exposed and brutal in a winter wind
properties.tip: Climb at sunrise when the balloons launch below you rather than at sunset, when the small platform is standing-room only.
properties.rev: The view is the best in the region by common consent; the recurring complaints are steep worn steps with poor railings, a genuine crush at sunset, and a village that has gone almost entirely over to boutique cave hotels.
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) airport 10 km, or Kayseri (ASR) 70 km; dolmuş from Göreme takes 10 minutes

properties.name: Love Valley
properties.desc: A flat-bottomed corridor of the tallest, most improbably shaped fairy chimneys in Cappadocia, some over 30 metres with basalt caps. The floor is sandy and easy walking between vineyards; at dawn balloons drift right down the length of it. The name is a joke everyone gets immediately.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; snow in the valley in Jan–Feb photographs beautifully
properties.tip: Walk in from the Göreme–Uçhisar road at the bottom instead of stopping at the paid roadside viewpoint — the chimneys only work from below.
properties.rev: Universally photographed and genuinely striking, though people report the top viewpoint is now a fenced car park with an entry charge, quad bikes churn the sand, and there is no shade at all after 11:00.
properties.entry: Free from the valley floor · roadside viewpoint car park ≈₺100 (€2.50)
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) airport, then Göreme; the lower entrance is 2 km on foot from the village along the Uçhisar road

properties.name: Zemi Valley
properties.desc: The longest of the Göreme valleys, running southwest towards Uçhisar with a seasonal stream, poplars and no road access for most of its length. El Nazar Church stands alone in a cone near the entrance with 10th-century frescoes; the Sakli (Hidden) Church nearby was only found in 1957.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; stream crossings after snowmelt in March
properties.tip: El Nazar has its own caretaker and closes early — call in on the way out of Göreme rather than at the end of the walk.
properties.rev: People come out of Zemi saying it feels like Cappadocia before tourism, then note the churches are often locked, the path braids into dead ends among the orchards, and phone signal disappears halfway along.
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) airport, then Göreme; the valley starts below the Open-Air Museum road, 10 minutes on foot

properties.name: Cappadocia Hot-Air Ballooning
properties.desc: Around a hundred balloons lift from the Göreme valleys before dawn, drifting low enough into Love and Rose valleys that the basket brushes the tuff, then climbing for the sunrise over the whole plateau. Flights last an hour, take off in the dark, and are strictly weather-dependent.
properties.season: Flies year-round; Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct have the highest launch rate, winter the most cancellations
properties.tip: Book for your first morning, not your last — roughly one in four winter mornings is grounded for wind and you want spare days to rerun it.
properties.rev: Almost everyone calls it worth the money once, then reports the same friction: 04:30 pickups, cancellations with slow refunds, crowded 24-person baskets on the cheap tickets, and prices that have roughly doubled since 2019.
properties.entry: ≈€180–350 per person depending on basket size and season
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) or Nevşehir (NAV) airport, then Göreme; operators collect from every cave hotel in the dark

properties.name: Göreme Open-Air Museum
properties.desc: Eleven rock-cut chapels and a monastic refectory packed into one hillside bowl, the whole thing carved out of soft tuff. The Dark Church still carries deep blue 11th-century frescoes because centuries of pigeon droppings sealed it from daylight. Tokalı Church, the largest and best painted, sits across the road on the same ticket.
properties.season: Apr–May and Oct; January snow on the cones is worth the cold and the slippery stairs
properties.tip: Do the Dark Church first at opening, then Tokalı across the road — most groups skip Tokalı entirely because it is outside the fence.
properties.rev: Visitors rate the frescoes among the best Byzantine painting anywhere, but complain about the queue and no-photo rule in the Dark Church, the constant tour-group shuffle on narrow stairs, and a ticket price that has roughly doubled in three years.
properties.entry: ≈€20 · Dark Church ≈€8 extra · covered by Museum Pass Türkiye
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) or Nevşehir (NAV) airport, then shuttle to Göreme; the museum is a 15-minute uphill walk from the village

properties.name: Zelve Open-Air Museum
properties.desc: Three converging valleys of cave dwellings lived in until 1952, when erosion made them unsafe and the village moved down the road. You walk through kitchens with soot on the ceilings, a rock-cut mosque with its minbar, a mill, and the Üzümlü and Balıklı churches, all on the same terrain the residents used.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; no shade anywhere in the three valleys
properties.tip: Take a torch and use the 30-metre unlit tunnel linking valleys one and two — most visitors turn back at the barrier and walk the long way round.
properties.rev: Often called more atmospheric than Göreme because you can actually go inside the rooms; the frequent complaints are steep loose scrambles, several sections fenced off after rockfalls, and zero shade or water once you are in.
properties.entry: ≈€10 · joint ticket with Paşabağ · covered by Museum Pass Türkiye
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) or Kayseri (ASR) airport, then the Avanos–Ürgüp road; a car or the Red Tour is the practical way in

properties.name: Paşabağ (Monks Valley)
properties.desc: The multi-headed fairy chimneys, some with two and three basalt caps on one stem, standing in an old vineyard. One cone is hollowed into a hermitage chapel for Simeon Stylites, reached by a steep internal stair with windows cut at the top where the hermit watched the valley.
properties.season: Year-round; low winter sun gives the cones the strongest shadows
properties.tip: Squeeze up the stair inside the St Simeon chimney — it is unmarked, easy to walk past, and the only chimney interior here you can enter.
properties.rev: The most photogenic chimneys in Cappadocia and mercifully flat to walk, undercut by a large souvenir bazaar at the entrance, coach parties every fifteen minutes, and a ticket that now covers Zelve whether you want it or not.
properties.entry: ≈€10 · joint ticket with Zelve · covered by Museum Pass Türkiye
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) airport, then the Avanos road; 5 km from Avanos, usually visited on the Red Tour

properties.name: Çavuşin
properties.desc: Half-abandoned cliff village whose old rock houses were evacuated after a rockfall, leaving open rooms hanging above the new settlement. The Church of St John the Baptist, one of the oldest in Cappadocia, sits at the top of an iron stair; the Nicephorus Phocas church by the road has vivid 10th-century soldiers.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; the stair to the basilica is dangerous when icy
properties.tip: The Nicephorus Phocas church at the foot of the cliff is a separate ticket and takes ten minutes — most people drive past it to Paşabağ.
properties.rev: Praised as the best trailhead in Cappadocia and pleasantly ruinous, but the collapsed village is genuinely unstable, the upper basilica is often roped off, and the coach car park below fills with carpet touts by mid-morning.
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) airport, then the Göreme–Avanos road; dolmuş from Göreme takes 10 minutes

properties.name: Özkonak Underground City
properties.desc: Found in 1972 by a farmer wondering where his irrigation water went, this one has a defensive trick the famous two lack: holes above the tunnels for pouring hot oil on anyone who forced a door. Four of ten levels are open, and on most days you will have them to yourself.
properties.season: Year-round; cool inside, and the Avanos road is clear in winter
properties.tip: There is no ticket queue and no tour schedule here — the caretaker walks you down and explains the oil holes, which no guide bothers with at Derinkuyu.
properties.rev: Visitors who make the detour rate it the best-value underground city precisely because it is empty, while warning that the open section is small, lighting is patchy, and it is a 15 km dead-end drive north of Avanos with no public transport.
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) airport, then Avanos and 15 km north on the Özkonak road; you need a car or a taxi

properties.name: Avanos
properties.desc: The pottery town on the Kızılırmak, where the red clay from the riverbed has been thrown on kick-wheels since Hittite times. Workshops line the old streets below the Ottoman houses, and any of them will sit you at a wheel for half an hour. The river is the widest thing you will see in Cappadocia.
properties.season: Apr–Oct for the river terraces; workshops are open all year
properties.tip: Skip the coach-stop showrooms on the main road and walk up into the back lanes, where families still fire their own kilns and prices are a third of the ones on the tour circuit.
properties.rev: Most people enjoy the wheel session and the riverside evening; the persistent complaints are hard-sell showrooms attached to tours, wildly inflated ceramic prices, and the hair museum in Chez Galip being either the highlight or deeply unpleasant, depending on the visitor.
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) airport 18 km or Kayseri (ASR) 65 km; frequent dolmuş from Ürgüp and Göreme

properties.name: Rose Valley (Güllüdere)
properties.desc: Pink and cream tuff folded into fins that go coral in the last hour of light. The 4 km path from Çavuşin passes apricot terraces, painted dovecotes and two rock churches — Haçlı, with a carved cross in its ceiling, and Üç Haçlı, where a caretaker unlocks the door for a coin.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; midsummer afternoons are shadeless and over 33 °C
properties.tip: Start at Çavuşin and walk up rather than driving to the Kızılçukur sunset terrace, which fills with minibuses by 18:00.
properties.rev: Walkers call this the best two hours in Cappadocia; the standard gripes are unsigned trail forks, informal fees collected at the churches, and dust from ATV tours cutting through the same gullies.
properties.entry: Free — ≈₺100 (€2.50) collected informally at the rock churches
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) or Kayseri (ASR) airport, then Göreme; taxi or dolmuş to Çavuşin and walk back

properties.name: Meskendir Valley
properties.desc: A narrow green cut between Göreme and Ortahisar where the path runs under rock arches and through short unlit tunnels cut by farmers. Apricot and mulberry trees close overhead, dovecotes line the walls, and you can walk an hour on a weekday without meeting anyone.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; the tunnels stay cool even in July
properties.tip: Bring a torch for the two tunnels and link it with Kızılçukur at the top for a proper half-day loop back to Göreme.
properties.rev: Repeatedly named the quietest of the Göreme valleys, with the caveat that the trail is badly signed where it crosses the campsite road and vanishes entirely in one overgrown stretch after rain.
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) airport, then Göreme; the trailhead is by the campsite on the Ortahisar road

properties.name: Ortahisar
properties.desc: Uçhisar's overlooked sibling: an 86-metre rock citadel over a square where old men still play okey, and a warren of cold-storage caves that hold Turkey's lemons and potatoes through winter. Stone Ottoman houses and a small ethnography museum sit below. Far fewer hotels, and prices to match.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; the citadel closes in high wind
properties.tip: Ask at the square about the citrus storage caves — the refrigeration trade, not tourism, is what keeps this village going.
properties.rev: Travellers who base here say it is the authentic version of Göreme with real village life; the trade-offs are fewer restaurants, an early-closing citadel with a rickety metal stair, and almost no evening transport.
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) airport, then 15 km by road; dolmuş from Ürgüp or Göreme every 30–60 minutes

properties.name: Red Valley (Kızılçukur)
properties.desc: The darker twin of Rose Valley, its iron-stained rock running from rust to violet as the sun drops. Narrow slots squeeze between walls barely shoulder-width, and the Üzümlü church hides grapevine frescoes above a vineyard. Locals still keep pigeon houses cut into the cliffs for fertiliser.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; the clay path turns to slick paste after rain
properties.tip: The two valleys interlock — take the marked link path near the vineyard and you can loop Red and Rose in one three-hour walk.
properties.rev: Hikers love the colour and the emptiness at midday, then find the sunset viewpoint commercialised with a paid terrace, loud music and coach parties; the trail itself is unmarked in places and easy to lose.
properties.entry: Free · terrace cafés charge ≈₺150 (€3.50) for the sunset spot
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) airport, then Göreme or Ortahisar; the trailhead is a 20-minute walk from Ortahisar village

properties.name: Mustafapaşa (Sinasos)
properties.desc: The best-preserved Greek village in Cappadocia, emptied by the 1924 population exchange. Carved stone doorways with Greek inscriptions, the Ayios Vasilios and Constantine-Helena churches, and a main square that still looks like 1910. Students from the local faculty keep it from being a museum piece.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; very quiet and half-shut in midwinter
properties.tip: Walk the 3 km down to the Gomeda valley behind the village — a rock-cut church, an old chapel and nobody else on the path.
properties.rev: Visitors consistently call it the calmest place in the region and the stonework genuinely rare, while noting that several churches are locked with no visible keyholder, restoration has left scaffolding up for years, and there is little to do after dark.
properties.entry: Village free · churches ≈₺100 (€2.50) each when open
properties.onward: Nevşehir (NAV) airport, then 6 km south of Ürgüp; dolmuş from Ürgüp runs about every hour

properties.name: Ürgüp
properties.desc: The region's proper town rather than a tourist village: a working market, Greek and Ottoman stone houses on the Esbelli hill, and the Üç Güzeller chimneys on the edge of it. This is Cappadocia's wine country, and the old cellars around Temenni hill pour Kalecik Karası and Emir straight from the barrel.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; the grape harvest and wine festival fall in September
properties.tip: Saturday is the town market — go for the dried apricots and pekmez rather than the carpet shops on Kayseri Caddesi.
properties.rev: Rated the most liveable base in Cappadocia with the best restaurants, though visitors note it is spread out, the sights are thin compared with Göreme, and hotel prices on Esbelli hill have climbed well past what the town otherwise costs.
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) airport 75 km or Nevşehir (NAV) 25 km; shuttles meet most flights and drop at the otogar

properties.name: Soğanlı Valley
properties.desc: Two branching valleys with around a hundred rock churches, the best of them free-standing: Kubbeli, a domed chapel carved out of a single fairy chimney, and Karabaş with 11th-century frescoes on a black ground. Village women sell cloth dolls at the entrance, a Soğanlı craft going back generations.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; the valley floor is muddy after rain and very quiet in winter
properties.tip: Take the northern branch first for Kubbeli and Yılanlı, and pay the ticket at the entrance kiosk — the church doors up the valley are unlocked only if the warden knows you are in there.
properties.rev: Repeatedly described as Cappadocia thirty years ago, with the fair warnings that many frescoes are smoke-blackened or defaced, the churches are scattered over several kilometres of walking, and there is one restaurant and no public transport.
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) airport, then 90 km southwest via Yeşilhisar; from Ürgüp it is 60 km, car only

properties.name: Çamardı
properties.desc: The base town under Demirkazık: a small grid of stone houses, a Thursday market where shepherds come down off the yayla, and a handful of trekking pensions that also run mule support into the Aladağlar. Apple orchards fill the valley, and the mountains stand up directly behind the last street.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for trekking; deep snow and a very quiet town from December to March
properties.tip: Book mules and a guide at the Çukurbağ pensions rather than from Niğde — the Çukurbağ families hold the actual permits and know the current state of the passes.
properties.rev: Trekkers find the pensions warm and cheap and the logistics reliable; nobody pretends the town itself is scenic, and visitors mention limited food options, minibuses that stop by mid-afternoon, and almost everything shut out of season.
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) or Adana (ADA) airport, then Niğde; dolmuş Niğde–Çamardı runs a few times daily, last one early afternoon

properties.name: Aladağlar National Park
properties.desc: Limestone walls and karst basins in the Anti-Taurus, with Demirkazık at 3,756 m and the Yedigöller plateau of seven small lakes at 3,000 m behind it. This is Turkey's best alpine rock, with big multi-pitch routes, ibex on the screes and shepherd camps in the high yaylas through summer.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for the high routes; snow blocks the passes from November to May
properties.tip: The Yedigöller crossing from Demirkazık to Kapuzbaşı is a serious two-day trek — hire a local guide in Çukurbağ, and do not attempt it without carrying water.
properties.rev: Alpinists rate the limestone world-class and the solitude complete; the standard warnings are almost no marked trails or refuges, a bad-weather commitment far from help, and access roads that need a high-clearance vehicle.
properties.entry: Free · guided trekking from ≈₺3,000 (€65) per day per group
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) or Adana (ADA) airport, then Niğde and 50 km east to Çamardı and Çukurbağ; car essential

properties.name: Kapuzbaşı Waterfalls
properties.desc: Seven falls bursting straight out of a limestone cliff face 70 metres up, fed by underground karst rather than a river above — the water simply appears out of the rock. They sit at the bottom of the Aladağlar on the Zamantı river, and the spray keeps the gorge cold even in August.
properties.season: May–Jul at full volume; by September the flow drops sharply
properties.tip: The last 40 km from Yahyalı is a narrow gorge road with drops and no barrier — start early, and do not attempt it in the dark or in a wide vehicle.
properties.rev: Those who make it call it the most spectacular waterfall in Anatolia and worth the whole day; every account also mentions the punishing access road, minimal facilities at the end and much less water after midsummer.
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) airport, then 130 km south to Yahyalı and a slow 40 km gorge road; high-clearance car recommended

properties.name: Sultan Marshes
properties.desc: A Ramsar wetland where fresh and salt marsh meet on the Develi plain under Erciyes, with over 300 recorded bird species. Flamingos stand in the shallows through summer, cranes and pelicans pass in migration, and flat-bottomed boats push through reed channels from the Ovaçiftlik observation tower.
properties.season: Apr–May and Sep–Oct for migration; flamingos stay into August
properties.tip: Be at the Ovaçiftlik tower for first light and take the reed-boat trip then — by ten the heat haze makes long-lens work pointless.
properties.rev: Birders rate it among Turkey's top wetlands and the boatmen knowledgeable, while noting water levels have dropped badly with irrigation, some years the salt lake is nearly dry, and facilities amount to one visitor centre and a tower.
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) airport, then 60 km south via Develi to Ovaçiftlik; a car is the only practical way

properties.name: Yahyalı and the Kapuzbaşı road
properties.desc: Yahyalı weaves double-knotted wool carpets in madder red and indigo, still on looms in the villages, and it is where the road into the southern Aladağlar starts. Forty kilometres of single-track cut above the Zamantı gorge follow, past Kapuzbaşı, with cliffs on one side and a long drop on the other.
properties.season: May–Oct for the gorge road; snow and rockfall close it in winter
properties.tip: Fill the tank in Yahyalı — there is no fuel, no shop and barely any phone signal for the whole gorge stretch to Kapuzbaşı.
properties.rev: Drivers describe the gorge as one of the great roads in Anatolia and the carpet workshops genuinely traditional; the same accounts warn of no barriers, blind bends, occasional rockfall and a carpet trade that has shrunk to a few families.
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) airport, then 130 km south; buses reach Yahyalı, but the gorge road needs your own vehicle

properties.name: Sarıkaya Roman Bath
properties.desc: A second-century Roman thermal bath excavated out from under a modern town, with the marble-lined pool still filling from its original hot spring and steps worn by Roman feet descending into the water. Known in antiquity as Basilica Therma, it stayed in use for centuries. The scale of the surviving pool and its rising steam catch people off guard.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov — the steam shows best on a cold clear morning
properties.tip: Nobody has bathed here for a long time despite what the town's own signage implies; come to look at the masonry and go to a modern thermal hotel nearby to actually swim.
properties.rev: Impressive for a site so few people have heard of, though excavation and restoration are ongoing, walkways are makeshift, and opening hours can be improvised.
properties.onward: Ankara Esenboğa (ESB) airport, then 260 km east via Yozgat towards Sorgun and Sarıkaya; buses reach Sarıkaya but a car is easier.

properties.name: Mount Erciyes
properties.desc: The 3,864-metre volcano that dominates every view in Kayseri and supplied the ash that became Cappadocia. Its northern flank carries Turkey's largest ski area — over 100 km of pisted runs and gondolas from Tekir Yaylası — and in summer the same lifts serve walkers heading for the crater rim.
properties.season: Dec–Mar for skiing with reliable snow; Jul–Sep for the summit scramble
properties.tip: Lifts run from Develi on the south side too, and that base is emptier and cheaper than Tekir on winter weekends when Kayseri comes up en masse.
properties.rev: Skiers rate the snow reliable, the lifts modern and the prices a fraction of the Alps, then complain about wind holds closing the upper gondolas, weekend queues from the city, thin apres-ski and a summit route that is loose volcanic rubble.
properties.entry: Ski day pass ≈₺1,600 (€35) · mountain access free in summer
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) airport 25 km, then a 40-minute shuttle to Tekir Yaylası; ski buses run from Kayseri in winter

properties.name: Kayseri Covered Bazaar and pastırma
properties.desc: A 500-year-old bazaar wrapped around the black basalt citadel, with the Bedesten and Vezir Han still trading. The pastırma shops hang whole beef fillets crusted in çemen — fenugreek, garlic and paprika — cured since the Byzantine period, and the mantı here are thumbnail-sized and served under garlic yoghurt.
properties.season: Year-round; pastırma is cured in autumn, so October has the fresh season's meat
properties.tip: Buy pastırma cut from the sırt (loin) rather than the cheaper cuts, and ask for it sliced paper-thin in front of you — pre-packed vacuum trays are a different product.
properties.rev: Food travellers rate the pastırma the best in Turkey and the bazaar genuinely working rather than touristic; the complaints are a heavily modernised citadel interior full of chain shops, aggressive parking, and a city centre that is short on charm.
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) airport 5 km from the centre; the tram stops at the citadel and the bazaar is at its foot

properties.name: Develi (Everek)
properties.desc: A market town under the south face of Erciyes with a 13th-century Ulu Cami, the ruined Aziz Toros church from the Armenian quarter, and streets of cut-stone houses in the old Everek district. It is also the quiet approach to the Sultan Marshes and to Erciyes' southern ski lifts.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; winter is cold but the ski base is 20 minutes away
properties.tip: The Everek quarter behind the main street is where the stone houses and the old church are — the modern centre gives no hint they exist.
properties.rev: Worth an hour on the way to Sultansazlığı and pleasantly unvisited; the honest verdict is that the Armenian church is a roofless shell, much of the old quarter has been replaced by concrete, and there is little tourist infrastructure.
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) airport, then 40 km south by road; frequent buses from Kayseri otogar to Develi

properties.name: Talas
properties.desc: The old Greek and Armenian hill quarter above Kayseri, where merchants who traded with Istanbul built black basalt mansions with carved doorways. Many are restored as cafés and boutique hotels now; the Panagia church and the Ali Dağı ridge above give the district its skyline, with Erciyes filling the horizon.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; pleasant evenings when central Kayseri is still hot
properties.tip: Walk up to Ali Dağı at dusk for the city lights against Erciyes — paragliders use the same launch, and there is a tea kiosk at the top.
properties.rev: Visitors like the stonework and the café scene and call it the pleasant side of Kayseri; the criticism is that restoration has been uneven, several landmark houses are closed or converted, and student nightlife makes the centre loud at weekends.
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) airport 15 km; city buses and the Kayseri tram reach Talas in 25 minutes from the centre

properties.name: Kültepe (Kanesh)
properties.desc: The Assyrian merchant colony where over 23,000 cuneiform tablets were found — the oldest written records in Anatolia, private letters and contracts from around 1900 BC that name the earliest known Anatolian rulers. The mound and the lower karum town are excavated, with mud-brick house walls and street lines visible.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; the plain is exposed, with no shade on the excavation
properties.tip: See the tablets and the Kültepe finds in the Kayseri Archaeological Museum first — the site itself is foundations, and it only makes sense once you have seen what came out of it.
properties.rev: Historically one of the most important sites in Turkey, but visitors consistently report low mud-brick foundations, sparse signage, a site sometimes locked out of excavation season and very few other people — go for the story, not the spectacle.
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) airport, then 20 km northeast on the Sivas road towards Kültepe; car or taxi

properties.name: Ağırnas
properties.desc: Mimar Sinan was born here in 1490, and his family house — a stone building over a rock-cut cellar — is now a small museum. The real interest is underneath: a tunnel system linking cellars, wells and rooms across the village, dug into the same soft rock as the Cappadocian cities and still partly walkable.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; underground sections are cool and open year-round
properties.tip: The underground passages are entered from the courtyard of the Sinan house — ask the attendant to unlock them, because they are not part of the standard walk-through.
properties.rev: Architecture-minded visitors like the connection to Sinan and the odd underground layer; others find the museum thin, the tunnels only partly accessible, and the village largely rebuilt in modern concrete around the historic core.
properties.onward: Kayseri (ASR) airport 20 km, then the Sivas road towards Ağırnas; city bus from Kayseri or a short taxi

properties.name: Sivas Seljuk Madrasas
properties.desc: Three thirteenth-century madrasas stand within a few hundred metres of each other on and around Konak Square: the Gök Medrese with its twin brick minarets and blue tile, the Çifte Minareli Medrese reduced to a single spectacular façade, and the Şifaiye, a hospital whose tiled tomb chamber holds Sultan Keykavus. No other Turkish city has this density of Seljuk work in walking distance.
properties.season: May–Oct — Sivas sits at 1,285 m and winters are long and hard
properties.tip: Walk them in one loop from the square in an hour, and check whether the Gök Medrese has reopened — it spent years behind restoration hoarding.
properties.rev: Compact and impressive, with the standing complaint that the Çifte Minareli is now only a front wall and restoration closures are frequent and poorly announced.
properties.entry: Free · small fee at the Şifaiye museum rooms
properties.onward: Sivas (VAS) airport, 25 minutes from the centre; Sivas is also on the Ankara–Kars rail line and the new YHT route.

properties.name: Şuğul Canyon
properties.desc: A narrow green gash in the Kangal steppe: walnut and poplar trees, a cold stream, small waterfalls and rock-cut chambers in the canyon walls, all invisible until you are at the rim. After hours of treeless plateau the sudden shade and running water feel unreasonable. Local families come to picnic and to drink from the springs.
properties.season: May–Sep — the stream runs low by late August, roads poor in winter
properties.tip: The last stretch is an unpaved track through village fields; ask in Yellice for directions because the canyon is signed only intermittently.
properties.rev: Those who find it describe a small green paradise, tempered by a rough access track, no marked path beyond the picnic area, and weekend litter along the stream.
properties.onward: Sivas (VAS) airport, then about 90 km south towards Kangal and onto village roads near Yellice; a car with clearance helps.

properties.name: Gökpınar Lake
properties.desc: A spring-fed pool near Gürün so clear that the trout appear to hang in air above the pale gravel bed, ringed by willows in an otherwise dry, stony landscape. The water stays around 20 °C year-round and holds its blue-green colour through winter. Small, quiet and startling the first time you see it from the path.
properties.season: May–Oct — the colour is strongest under midday sun
properties.tip: Swimming is not allowed and the trout are protected; bring a polarising filter instead, or you will photograph nothing but sky reflection.
properties.rev: Genuinely beautiful and rarely busy, but it is very small, the walk round takes fifteen minutes, and weekend picnic litter and roadside stalls have crept in.
properties.entry: Free · small parking fee at weekends
properties.onward: Sivas (VAS) airport, then 170 km southwest via Kangal to Gürün, then a few kilometres out of town; a car is needed.

properties.name: Balıklı Kaplıca (Doctor Fish Spa)
properties.desc: A thermal pool on the bare Kangal steppe where two species of small fish strip the scaling from psoriasis sufferers who sit in the 35 °C water for hours a day. It has been a medical destination since the 1960s, with a spartan hotel attached and patients on three-week courses. Not a novelty pedicure — an actual treatment centre.
properties.season: May–Sep — the site is remote and cut off in heavy winter
properties.tip: Day visits are possible but the point is the multi-day course; book the on-site accommodation in advance because there is nothing else within 20 km.
properties.rev: Psoriasis patients report real results and a supportive atmosphere; casual visitors find the facilities dated, the location bleak, and the fish sensation unpleasant at first.
properties.entry: Day entry roughly ₺400 (≈€8) · treatment packages priced separately
properties.onward: Sivas (VAS) airport, then 100 km south towards Kangal and 13 km on a side road; a car or a pre-booked hotel transfer.

properties.name: Kangal
properties.desc: A high steppe district that gave its name to the massive fawn-coloured livestock guardian dog bred here for centuries to fight wolves. There is little to see in the town itself; the reason to come is the country around it — treeless rolling grassland, shepherds with their dogs and flocks, and long empty roads under enormous sky.
properties.season: May–Sep — winters at 1,500 m are severe and roads drift shut
properties.tip: Do not approach a working Kangal at a flock — they are guarding, not greeting; if you want to see the breed properly, visit the state breeding station rather than a roadside herd.
properties.rev: Dog enthusiasts make the pilgrimage happily; others find the town itself drab, the breeding station's hours unpredictable, and the guardian dogs genuinely intimidating up close.
properties.onward: Sivas (VAS) airport, then 100 km south on the D850 towards Malatya; Kangal is also a stop on the Sivas–Malatya railway.

properties.name: Tödürge Lake
properties.desc: A karst lake east of Sivas fed from below by springs, with reed islands that drift on the surface and shift position with the wind. Herons and grebes work the margins, the water is drinkably clear at the spring mouths, and the surrounding hills are bare and pale. Locals fish it from flat-bottomed boats.
properties.season: May–Oct — it freezes over in a hard winter
properties.tip: The floating islands are the local curiosity: ask a fisherman at Demiryurt village, and you may get taken out to one for very little.
properties.rev: A quiet, unexpectedly pretty stop on the road east, though there are no facilities beyond a tea shack and the shoreline is muddy and hard to walk in places.
properties.onward: Sivas (VAS) airport, then 60 km east on the D100 towards Erzincan; the lake is visible from the highway near Demiryurt.

properties.name: Great Mosque and Hospital of Divriği
properties.desc: In a small town at the far east of Sivas province stands the strangest stone carving in the Islamic world: four portals of 1228 covered in three-dimensional palmettes, sunbursts and vegetation so deeply undercut they cast shadows like foliage. Nothing else in Anatolia looks remotely like it. Inside, sixteen piers carry a vault over the joined mosque and hospital.
properties.season: May–Oct — Divriği is high, remote and hard going in deep winter
properties.tip: Come in raking morning or late afternoon sun; the flat midday light kills the relief that is the entire reason the building is on the UNESCO list.
properties.rev: Architecture travellers call the journey worth it on its own, but long restoration campaigns have kept parts under scaffold for years and Divriği is a five-hour round trip from Sivas.
properties.onward: Sivas (VAS) airport, then 170 km east; the scenic Sivas–Divriği train along the Kızılırmak is a better ride than the road.

properties.name: Göynük
properties.desc: White houses with black timber frames stacked up a hillside above a stream, restored hard over the last decade and used as a set for period television. Akşemseddin, the teacher of Mehmed the Conqueror, is buried at the top of the thousand-step stone stair, and the small covered market still sells the local pear and pastırma.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov; midsummer is hot in the valley
properties.tip: Climb to the Zafer clock tower at dusk, when the whole white-and-black grid below switches its lights on.
properties.rev: Most reports praise the restored streets and the quiet, but a fair number find the make-over too uniform, the museums shut outside summer, and weekend day-trip buses filling the one main lane.
properties.onward: Istanbul (IST/SAW), motorway to Düzce or Bolu, then about an hour south; dolmuş from Bolu and Adapazarı

properties.name: Akçakoca
properties.desc: Düzce's seaside town: hazelnut hills running down to a long grey-sand shore, a Genoese castle ruin on the Ceneviz headland and a row of fish restaurants along the front. The water is cold and honest, the surf can turn dangerous within an hour, and the whole place empties after mid-September.
properties.season: Jul–Aug for swimming; the sea here rarely passes 22 °C
properties.tip: Drive 6 km west to Karaburun for the lighthouse and a beach without loudspeakers.
properties.rev: Weekenders like the cheap fish and the short drive from İstanbul; the constant complaints are rip currents and drownings on unpatrolled stretches, concrete blocks along the shore and August crowds.
properties.onward: Istanbul (IST/SAW), motorway to Düzce, then 38 km north over the hazelnut ridge; frequent dolmuş from Düzce otogar

properties.name: Topuk Yayla
properties.desc: A high meadow above the Bolu Dağı tunnels with a small lake, a boardwalk, horses grazing and a resort hotel that put the place on the map. The forest tracks beyond the gate are free and usually empty, and on most mornings the cloud sits in the valley below while the plateau is in sun.
properties.season: May–Oct for the meadow; Dec–Feb for snow, when the access road needs care
properties.tip: The lakeside path and picnic meadows are public — park below the hotel gate rather than paying for anything.
properties.rev: Guests rate the setting and the cool air highly, while day visitors report feeling pushed toward hotel prices, a small lake that underwhelms in dry summers, and mud everywhere after rain.
properties.entry: Free for the public meadow and lake path
properties.onward: Istanbul (IST/SAW), motorway to the Bolu Dağı exit, then 12 km up a paved forest road

properties.name: Mudurnu
properties.desc: An Ottoman market town folded into a valley, where the medieval craftsmen's guild still opens the week with a prayer over the shopkeepers' takings. Timber-framed houses lean over stone lanes, Yıldırım Bayezid's 1382 hamam still takes bathers, and the Armutçular konak shows the tall dark rooms behind those façades.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; winter is grey and half the konaks shut
properties.tip: Be in the Yıldırım Bayezid mosque courtyard early on a Friday for the ahi guild ceremony — it is not staged for visitors.
properties.rev: Visitors call it the least touristed Ottoman town within three hours of İstanbul, while noting that restoration is patchy, several konaks are locked with no keyholder in sight, and there is very little to eat after dark.
properties.onward: Istanbul (IST/SAW), motorway to Bolu, then 52 km south over the pass; hourly dolmuş from Bolu otogar

properties.name: Samandere Waterfall
properties.desc: A twenty-metre fall dropping into a mossy basalt slot in dense beech forest, reached by a few hundred wooden steps down from the road. Spray keeps the rock slick and the air cold even in August. Protected as a natural monument since 1988, with trout restaurants at the top that are half the reason people stop.
properties.season: Apr–Jun at full flow; Sep–Oct for the colour, thin water by late summer
properties.tip: Skip the crowded lower platform and follow the path 200 m upstream to the second cascade, where almost nobody goes.
properties.rev: Reports call it a genuinely pretty half-hour, spoiled on summer weekends by picnic crowds on the narrow stairs, slippery unrailed rock and a car park that fills before ten.
properties.onward: Istanbul (IST/SAW), motorway to Düzce, then 25 km south through the villages; no useful public transport

properties.name: Lake Abant
properties.desc: A dark green lake at 1,300 m ringed by fir and beech, with a seven-kilometre path all the way round and horse-drawn phaetons clopping past the hotels. Weekends bring İstanbul families, gözleme stalls and woodsmoke; on a midweek morning in winter the surface freezes and the forest goes completely silent.
properties.season: May–Jun for wildflowers, Oct for colour; Jul–Aug weekends are heaving
properties.tip: Walk the far western shore — almost nobody gets past the first kilometre of stalls near the car park.
properties.rev: People love the walk and the air; recurring gripes are weekend crowds, overpriced hotel food, horses working in the heat, and a nature-park fee that keeps climbing.
properties.entry: ≈₺100 (€2.20) per person, extra for a car
properties.onward: Istanbul (IST/SAW) or Ankara (ESB) to Bolu, then 34 km on a good mountain road; weekend dolmuş from Bolu otogar

properties.name: Güzeldere Waterfall
properties.desc: A hundred-metre ribbon down a black rock face in the forest above Gölyaka, seen either from a platform level with the lip or from the bottom of some seven hundred wooden steps. In spring it thunders and soaks the viewing deck; by late August it is a thin veil. The drive up through hazel groves is half the outing.
properties.season: Apr–Jun for volume; Oct for colour; the road ices over in winter
properties.tip: Take the upper platform first for the whole drop, then decide whether your knees want the steps down and back up.
properties.rev: Visitors are impressed by the height and unimpressed by the climb back, the state of some of the steps, and how little water is left after July.
properties.onward: Istanbul (IST/SAW), motorway to Düzce, then 30 km via Gölyaka on a narrow paved road

properties.name: Cehennemağzı Caves
properties.desc: Three caves above Karadeniz Ereğli that antiquity called a mouth of Hades — the place where Heracles was said to have dragged up Cerberus. The middle one was used as a chapel by early Christians and keeps a rock-cut altar and a spring; Byzantine scratchings survive on the walls. Small, strange, ten minutes from the town centre.
properties.season: All year; the steps are slick after rain
properties.tip: Ask at the ticket hut to have the lights switched on in the third cave — it is usually left dark and people miss it entirely.
properties.rev: Visitors find the mythology and the chapel worth the short stop but describe the site as neglected, poorly lit and hemmed in by housing, with a strong smell of damp in the lower cave.
properties.onward: Zonguldak (ONQ) airport 50 min, or Istanbul and 3 h by coach to Ereğli; the caves are a short taxi ride from the otogar

properties.name: Sülüklü Lake
properties.desc: A leech-named tarn at 1,450 m in the fir forest above Mudurnu, reached by a dozen kilometres of forest track that turns to mud after rain. Dead trunks stand in black water, fog rolls in most afternoons, and it is one of the few places within four hours of İstanbul where you can camp and hear nothing at all.
properties.season: Jun–Sep; the track is impassable with snow or heavy rain
properties.tip: The final eight kilometres need clearance and dry weather — after rain the villagers tell you to walk it, and they are right.
properties.rev: Campers describe it as genuinely wild and eerily quiet; the complaints are the state of the access track, rubbish left by weekend groups, mosquitoes in July and no facilities of any kind.
properties.onward: Istanbul (IST/SAW), motorway to Bolu, then Mudurnu and 20 km of forest track — high clearance strongly advised

properties.name: Gölcük Lake
properties.desc: A small dark lake in the fir forest 15 km south of Bolu, circled by a wooden walkway you can cover in half an hour. Half-drowned trunks stand out of the shallows and the mist usually sits on the water until the sun clears the ridge. It is the easiest piece of proper forest near the İstanbul–Ankara motorway.
properties.season: May–Oct; snow closes the last stretch of road most winters
properties.tip: Weekday mornings only — at weekends the walkway is a wedding-photo conveyor belt.
properties.rev: Called a perfect two-hour stop by most who go, with the usual complaints about weekend picnic crowds, loud music from the car park and a fee for what is essentially a short stroll.
properties.onward: Istanbul (IST/SAW) or Ankara (ESB) to Bolu, then 13 km up the Aladağ road; taxi from Bolu is cheap

properties.name: Yedigöller National Park
properties.desc: Seven small lakes strung down a forested valley, each one dammed by an old landslide and linked by short board-walk paths. Late October turns the beech and hornbeam into a wall of copper, and the reflection everyone photographs happens at Büyükgöl before nine in the morning. The rest of the year it is damp, quiet and full of birdsong.
properties.season: Late Oct for colour, Jun–Sep for calm; the northern forest road is often snowbound Dec–Mar
properties.tip: Come on a weekday — on autumn weekends the one-lane forest road from Bolu jams solid and you queue an hour just to park.
properties.rev: Visitors agree the autumn colour matches the photographs, then complain about 40 km of rough forest road from Bolu, gridlock on October weekends, and litter around the main picnic lake.
properties.entry: ≈₺120 (€2.50) per person plus a vehicle fee at the gate
properties.onward: Istanbul (IST/SAW) or Ankara (ESB), then the motorway to Bolu and 40 km of forest road north — a car is the only realistic way in

properties.name: Kartalkaya
properties.desc: Bolu's ski mountain, 1,850 to 2,200 m of fir forest and open bowl on the Köroğlu range, with two hotel clusters and lifts that run straight from the door. Snow is reliable from late December, the runs are short but tree-lined, and it is the closest proper skiing to İstanbul at roughly three and a half hours.
properties.season: Late Dec–mid Mar for snow; in summer the ridge is empty grazing land with paragliding launches
properties.tip: Buy a day pass at the smaller Kartal side rather than the big resort — same lifts, shorter queues, cheaper lunch.
properties.rev: Skiers rate the tree runs and the short transfer from İstanbul, then complain about half-term lift queues, dated hotel packages with compulsory full board, and a road up that needs chains after every fresh fall.
properties.entry: Day lift pass ≈₺1,500 (€32); hotels sell all-in packages
properties.onward: Istanbul (IST/SAW) or Ankara (ESB) to Bolu, then 38 km of switchbacks; hotel shuttles meet buses at Bolu otogar

properties.name: Gökgöl Cave
properties.desc: Three kilometres of active river cave right beside the Zonguldak–Ankara road, of which about a kilometre is lit and walkable on steel catwalks. Curtain formations, a permanent stream running under your feet and a constant 12 °C. It is one of the easiest big caves in the country to visit and takes roughly forty minutes.
properties.season: All year; spring meltwater can close the lower gallery
properties.tip: Bring a fleece and shoes with grip — the air stays around 12 °C and the walkway drips the entire way.
properties.rev: Rated a good-value stop with well-built walkways, though visitors mention harsh coloured lighting, a short circuit for the ticket, and closures after heavy rain that are not posted anywhere.
properties.onward: Zonguldak Çaycuma (ONQ) airport 40 min, or Istanbul then the coast road; the cave sits 4 km east of Zonguldak on the D-750

properties.name: Tios (Filyos)
properties.desc: A Greek colony on a bluff where the Filyos river meets the sea, dug slowly since 2006: a Roman theatre, a bath complex, stretches of city wall and a gate that looks straight out at the surf. The site is unfenced and half-overgrown, sharing its headland with a fishing hamlet and an enormous new port under construction downstream.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; the headland is exposed and wet in winter
properties.tip: Go for the last hour of daylight — the theatre faces west over the river mouth, and there is no lighting or staff after dark.
properties.rev: Those who make the detour like having a Roman theatre entirely to themselves, but report no signage, waist-high weeds in summer, active trenches fenced off, and the port works dominating the view.
properties.onward: Zonguldak Çaycuma (ONQ) airport 25 min, then the coast road to Filyos; buses from Zonguldak run to Çaycuma only

properties.name: İnkumu
properties.desc: Bartın's own beach: two kilometres of pale sand backed by pines, shallow enough for small children and full of Bartın families from July. Four kilometres west, the Güzelcehisar basalt columns rise straight out of the shore — a wall of hexagonal lava pillars with a viewing platform above and almost nobody on it.
properties.season: Jul–Aug for swimming; May–Jun and Sep for the walk and the columns
properties.tip: Drive on to Güzelcehisar for the basalt cliffs — free, signposted badly and usually empty even in August.
properties.rev: Families rate the safe shallow water and cheap pensions; complaints run to summer-weekend crowding, thin sand in places, and litter after busy days.
properties.onward: Zonguldak (ONQ) airport 1 h, or Ankara (ESB) 4.5 h; frequent dolmuş from Bartın centre, 12 km

properties.name: Amasra
properties.desc: A Byzantine-walled town on a rock tied to the mainland by a Roman bridge, with two harbours — one for boats, one for swimming — and a Genoese citadel that people still live inside. The small museum holds Roman marble dug out of back gardens. Everything smells of fried hamsi and the woodcarvers' workshops.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for the water; on Jul–Aug weekends the causeway becomes a car park
properties.tip: Cross the Kemere bridge to Boztepe and walk out to the Kuşkayası Roman road monument early, before the Safranbolu buses arrive at eleven.
properties.rev: Almost everyone rates the setting and the fish, then warns about August gridlock on the single access road, restaurant bills that arrive higher than the menu suggests, and a crowded, stony town beach.
properties.entry: Town free; museum ≈₺60 (€1.30) · covered by Museum Pass Türkiye
properties.onward: Zonguldak (ONQ) airport then 90 min, or Ankara (ESB) and 4.5 h via Karabük; daily buses from Safranbolu

properties.name: Hadrianopolis
properties.desc: A Roman and early Byzantine town in the fields outside Eskipazar, dug since 2003 and known for church floors paved with mosaic animals — an elephant, a griffin, horses, a peacock — under simple shelters. Baths, a villa and cisterns lie around them in cut grass. There is no ticket office and often nobody else at all.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; the mosaics are sheeted over in winter and the field turns to mud
properties.tip: Come inside working hours on a weekday — the mosaic shelters are locked and the site guard, who has the key, goes home at five.
properties.rev: Those who make the detour rate the mosaics far above the effort, but report locked shelters outside office hours, almost no signage, and nowhere to eat nearer than Eskipazar.
properties.onward: Ankara Esenboğa (ESB) airport, then 180 km north to Eskipazar off the D100; the site is 3 km from the town centre and you need a car

properties.name: Bulak (Mencilis) Cave
properties.desc: A six-kilometre cave system in the hill above Bulak village, of which about four hundred metres is lit and railed. Three levels, an underground stream you hear before you see, and columns the colour of wet clay. The climb to the mouth is a few hundred steps up an open slope with the whole Safranbolu valley behind you.
properties.season: Apr–Nov; the access steps are treacherous in ice and the cave shuts in bad weather
properties.tip: Bring a jacket — it holds around 12 °C inside all year, and the stair up to the entrance is the warm-up, not the visit.
properties.rev: Most rate it good value and quieter than the famous caves, while noting the steep approach steps, permanently wet handrails and lighting that defeats phone cameras.
properties.onward: Ankara Esenboğa (ESB) airport, then Safranbolu and 8 km north-west on the Bulak road; no bus, so drive or take a taxi from Çarşı

properties.name: Safranbolu
properties.desc: An Ottoman caravan town of around two thousand timber-and-plaster houses, preserved whole because the railway and the road both went elsewhere. The Cinci Han still stands over a market of coppersmiths and saddlers, the Kaymakamlar house shows how a merchant family actually lived, and the whole bowl is best read from Hıdırlık hill.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; snow suits the town but closes several konaks
properties.tip: Stay the night — the day-trip coaches leave by five and the old town becomes a completely different, empty place.
properties.rev: Widely rated the best-preserved Ottoman town in Türkiye, with steady complaints about souvenir shops selling the same Turkish delight, coach groups filling the square by mid-morning, and steep cobbles that punish bad shoes.
properties.entry: Town free; each konak-museum ≈₺60 (€1.30) · Museum Pass Türkiye valid at the state museums
properties.onward: Ankara (ESB) then 3 h by road or bus to Karabük; Kastamonu (KFS) airport is a 2 h drive

properties.name: Kaymakamlar House
properties.desc: The best-explained konak in Safranbolu: three floors of an eighteenth-century officer's house, with a stable at ground level, a summer room open to the valley, and cupboards that turn out to be washing cabinets hidden inside the panelling. Mannequins in period dress are corny, but the carpentry and the rotating door are the point.
properties.season: All year; least crowded Nov–Mar
properties.tip: Ask the attendant to open the concealed gusülhane inside the wall cupboard — it is not signposted and most visitors walk straight past it.
properties.rev: Visitors find it the clearest window into how these houses were lived in, while grumbling about the mannequins, the tight stairs and coach parties that fill three rooms at once.
properties.onward: Ankara Esenboğa (ESB) airport, then Safranbolu; the house is a five-minute walk uphill from the Çarşı bazaar

properties.name: Cinci Han
properties.desc: A 1645 caravanserai in the middle of the bazaar, two galleried storeys of stone around a courtyard where camels once stood and tea is now served. It works as a hotel, but nobody stops you walking into the yard. The hamam of the same date and the same founder is a hundred metres away.
properties.season: All year; the stone rooms are cold Dec–Feb
properties.tip: If you stay, insist on an upper-gallery room — the ground-floor cells were storerooms and they are still dark and damp.
properties.rev: Guests praise the setting and the courtyard breakfast, then flag thin mattresses, sound that carries around the gallery, and rooms priced well above the town average.
properties.entry: Free to enter the courtyard · rooms from ≈€45
properties.onward: Ankara Esenboğa (ESB) airport, then Safranbolu; the han sits at the centre of Çarşı, two minutes from the bazaar square

properties.name: Tokatlı Canyon and İncekaya Aqueduct
properties.tr: Tokatlı Kanyonu ve İncekaya Su Kemeri
properties.desc: A limestone gorge a hundred metres deep on Safranbolu's doorstep, crossed by a six-arch aqueduct that İzzet Mehmet Paşa built in 1797 to bring water to the town. You can walk the open water channel on top, which has no railing. Downstream a glass terrace hangs over the drop, and the canyon path continues into the trees.
properties.season: Apr–Nov; the canyon path is slick and often closed after heavy rain
