properties.tip: Walk the aqueduct channel itself — almost everyone stops at the crystal terrace 700 m away and never crosses the arches.
properties.rev: Walkers love the aqueduct crossing and are less kind about the terrace: a queue, a fee, plastic overshoes, and scratched glass that ruins the photograph everyone came for.
properties.onward: Ankara Esenboğa (ESB) airport, then Safranbolu and 6 km north on the Bulak road; walkable from Çarşı in about an hour uphill

properties.name: Kurucaşile
properties.desc: A one-street coastal town that has built wooden boats for centuries — yards along the shore still lay keels by eye, and the smell of larch and pitch carries up the road. Beyond it the coast east toward Cide is among the emptiest and most twisting stretches of the whole Black Sea shore.
properties.season: Jun–Sep; the coast road is landslide-prone after winter storms
properties.tip: Walk into a boatyard and ask — the builders are used to visitors and will happily show you a hull in frame.
properties.rev: Travellers describe an unspoiled working town with real character, while noting there is almost nothing to do after dark, few beds, and a coast road that takes far longer than the map suggests.
properties.onward: Zonguldak (ONQ) airport then 2 h via Amasra, or Kastamonu (KFS) and 3 h through Cide; minibuses from Bartın

properties.name: Yörük Köyü
properties.desc: A stone-and-timber village twelve kilometres east of Safranbolu, settled by Yörük nomads and left almost untouched: a communal laundry with its stone basins still in place, a square of blackened konaks, and the Sipahioğlu house opened by the family that owns it. Perhaps thirty people live here through the winter.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; very quiet and often shut in midwinter
properties.tip: Knock at the Sipahioğlu Konağı rather than waiting for a guide — the owners show you the hidden women's gallery themselves.
properties.rev: Visitors call it Safranbolu without the crowds and with more honest decay; the flip side is that half the houses are locked, restoration money is visibly thin, and there is nowhere to eat beyond one tea garden.
properties.onward: Ankara (ESB) then Karabük; from Safranbolu it is 12 km by taxi or the Konarı dolmuş

properties.name: Cide and Gideros Cove
properties.desc: Cide has a long grey-sand and pebble beach with almost no hotels on it, and twelve kilometres west, Gideros is a near-circular rock cove where ancient Cytorus stood — two fish restaurants, a few boats, and cliffs closing the mouth. Behind them the Loç valley runs up into the Küre forests.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for swimming; the sea is cold and rough Oct–May
properties.tip: Gideros has no beach — you swim off the rocks or the jetty; the sand is back east at Uğurlu, and the cove restaurants want you to book in August.
properties.rev: People describe an undeveloped stretch of Black Sea coast worth the drive, then warn about the twisting coast road, strong undertow off Cide's open beach, and everything shutting after mid-September.
properties.onward: Kastamonu (KFS) airport, then 130 km north on the Azdavay road, or the coast road west from Sinop; the last hour is slow and winding

properties.name: Horma Canyon and Ilıca Waterfall
properties.desc: Valla's approachable neighbours, both a short drive from the village of Pınarbaşı. A boardwalk bolted to the rock runs two and a half kilometres above the Horma stream, cold and loud even in August; the Ilıca waterfall drops into a mossy bowl fifteen minutes' walk from its car park. Trout restaurants sit at both ends.
properties.season: May–Oct; the boardwalk is closed by snow and ice roughly Dec–Mar
properties.tip: Walk Horma from the upper entrance downhill and arrange a lift back — the return climb in the gorge is the part people regret.
properties.rev: Walkers call it one of the easiest ways to see serious canyon country, while noting slippery planks after rain, weekend picnic crowds and a boardwalk that shows its age in places.
properties.onward: Kastamonu (KFS) airport, then 80 km north to Pınarbaşı via Azdavay; minibuses run from Kastamonu but not to the canyon gates

properties.name: Küre Mountains National Park
properties.desc: A karst massif of beech and fir between Bartın and Kastamonu, protected as one of Europe's PAN Parks: sinkholes, underground rivers and canyons cutting four hundred metres deep. Ulukaya waterfall, the Ilgarini cave and the Valla rim all sit inside it, and bears and wolves are genuinely present rather than notional.
properties.season: May–Oct; forest tracks are impassable with snow Dec–Mar
properties.tip: Base yourself in Azdavay or Pınarbaşı rather than Bartın — the trailheads, guides and village guesthouses are all on the Kastamonu side.
properties.rev: Walkers praise genuinely wild forest and near-total solitude, while flagging unmarked trails, no rescue infrastructure, tick-heavy undergrowth in summer and villages where nobody speaks English.
properties.onward: Kastamonu (KFS) airport, then the Azdavay or Pınarbaşı road; from the Bartın side the Ulus forest road is slow and unpaved in places

properties.name: Ilgaz Mountain Ski Centre
properties.desc: The black-pine ridge between Kastamonu and Çankırı, topped by Büyük Hacet at 2587 m, with lifts at Yurduntepe and Kadınçayırı around 1800 m. Runs are short and gentle by Alpine standards and the snow is reliable from January. In summer the same road gives cool forest walks and yayla meadows an hour from the coast road.
properties.season: Jan–Mar for snow, Jun–Sep for walking; Apr–May is mud and closed lifts
properties.tip: Ski midweek — Ankara and Kastamonu empty onto this mountain at weekends and the lift queues double the price of the day in time.
properties.near: Yurduntepe Kayak Merkezi, Ilgaz, Kastamonu, Türkiye
properties.rev: Skiers call it decent value and family-friendly, then complain about short pistes, weekend queues, tired rental gear and hotels that charge Alpine prices for half-board.
properties.entry: Day lift pass ≈₺600 (€13) · the road and summer trails are free
properties.onward: Kastamonu (KFS) or Ankara Esenboğa (ESB) airport, then the D765; the ski road climbs 25 km from the Ilgaz pass and needs winter tyres

properties.name: Mahmut Bey Mosque
properties.desc: A plain barn of a building in Kasaba village that opens into a forest of painted wooden columns, built in 1366 and joined with pegs rather than nails. Red, black and white vegetal patterns still cover the beams and the muqarnas capitals. It became a World Heritage site in 2023 as one of five wooden hypostyle mosques.
properties.season: All year; the village road is fine in winter but the mosque is unheated
properties.tip: It is kept locked — phone ahead or ask in the village shop for the caretaker, who lives two streets away and will open it for you.
properties.rev: Everyone who gets inside calls it extraordinary; the recurring problems are the locked door, no fixed opening hours, and a low-lit interior that photographs badly without a tripod.
properties.entry: Free · a donation to the caretaker is normal
properties.onward: Kastamonu (KFS) airport, then 17 km north-west to Kasaba village on the Daday road; there is no bus, so drive or take a taxi

properties.name: Kastamonu Castle and Old Town
properties.desc: A blunt stone citadel on a crag with the whole town spread below it, and under it a working Ottoman quarter: Nasrullah square and its mosque, the Münire medrese full of craft workshops, and streets of timber konaks that are lived in rather than curated. Atatürk announced the hat reform here in 1925.
properties.season: May–Oct; Kastamonu winters are long, grey and genuinely cold
properties.tip: The castle path starts behind the statue on the north side — the other approach road ends at a dead-end car park with no way through.
properties.rev: Travellers like that the old town is unrestored and unpretentious; the common complaints are a steep unshaded climb to the castle, limited English signage, and shops that shut early on Sundays.
properties.onward: Kastamonu (KFS) airport has a handful of flights, otherwise Ankara Esenboğa (ESB) and 240 km north on the D765; buses run hourly from Ankara

properties.name: Şeyh Şaban-ı Veli Complex
properties.desc: The tomb, mosque and dervish lodge of the sixteenth-century Halveti sheikh who made Kastamonu a Sufi centre, still the town's spiritual address. Pilgrims come by the coachload to the türbe; the old lodge beside it now holds a museum of carved wooden objects, and the courtyard has a plane tree and a fountain.
properties.season: All year; Fridays and Ramadan are busiest
properties.tip: Go on a weekday morning — after Friday prayers the courtyard is solid with pilgrim coaches and the wooden-artefacts museum is unusable.
properties.rev: Visitors describe an atmosphere that outsiders can feel too, while noting strict dress rules, no photography inside the tomb, and coaches that arrive without warning.
properties.onward: Kastamonu (KFS) airport or Ankara (ESB), then the D765; the complex is a twenty-minute uphill walk from Nasrullah square

properties.name: Abana
properties.desc: A small, tidy seaside town where the mountains stop at a pebble beach and a promenade of tea gardens. Nothing much happens: fishermen mend nets, families who emigrated to Istanbul come home in August, and the fish restaurants serve hamsi in season. It is the Black Sea coast without a single tower block.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for swimming; Aug is when the town actually fills up
properties.tip: Eat in the harbour rather than the promenade — the boats land here and the difference in a plate of hamsi is obvious.
properties.rev: Regulars value the quiet and the cleanliness; the complaints are limited nightlife, a pebble rather than sand beach, and prices that jump in the three weeks around 15 August.
properties.onward: Kastamonu (KFS) airport, then 85 km north over the Küre pass to the coast at Bozkurt; minibuses run from Kastamonu's otogar

properties.name: Valla Canyon
properties.desc: Twelve kilometres of limestone slot in the Küre Mountains, with walls that rise more than a kilometre above the river. The through-trip is a two-day scramble with ropes, cold water and no exits, which is why almost everyone stops at the terrace above Muratbaşı and looks down at a green thread of water instead.
properties.season: Late Jun–Sep only for the floor; the terrace is open May–Oct, snowbound in winter
properties.tip: Do not enter the canyon without a licensed guide and a weather check — flash floods have killed walkers here, and there is no phone signal inside.
properties.rev: Trekkers rank it among the hardest and best canyons in Türkiye; the honest reports mention rescue callouts, a rough forest road to the rim, and a viewing terrace that is the whole visit for most people.
properties.entry: Terrace free · guided canyon traverse ≈€120 per person
properties.onward: Kastamonu (KFS) airport or Ankara (ESB), then 80 km north to Pınarbaşı and a rough forest road to the rim; a high-clearance car helps

properties.name: Kastamonu Pastırma and Siyez Bulgur
properties.desc: Kastamonu cures its pastırma in cold mountain air with a thin coat of çemen, so it tastes of meat rather than paste — a different animal from the Kayseri version. The other local staple is siyez, einkorn wheat ground into a nutty bulgur, and Taşköprü's garlic, which has protected status and a summer festival.
properties.season: Sep–Dec for new-season pastırma; the Taşköprü garlic festival is in July
properties.tip: Buy pastırma sliced to order at a Nasrullah square butcher, not vacuum-packed at the bus station — and ask for sırt, the back cut.
properties.rev: Food travellers say it beats the better-known versions and costs less; the caveats are shops that close at six, few English words anywhere, and airline rules on carrying cured meat home.
properties.entry: Free to browse · a plate of siyez pilav ≈₺150 (€3.50)
properties.onward: Kastamonu (KFS) airport, then 40 km north-east to Taşköprü for the garlic and grain, or stay in Kastamonu for the butchers and lokantas

properties.name: Ayancık and the Çangal Forest
properties.desc: A timber town on the coast west of Sinop, with the Çangal fir and beech forest rising behind it — one of the wettest, greenest corners of the country. Logging roads climb to yayla meadows and the small lake at Akgöl, mist sits in the valleys most mornings, and Ayancık still weaves the linen it is named for.
properties.season: Jun–Sep; it rains here all year and forest tracks are impassable after storms
properties.tip: Fill the tank in Ayancık before going up — there is no fuel and no reliable phone signal once the forest road starts climbing.
properties.rev: Those who venture up praise empty forest and cool air, and warn about rough unsigned tracks, sudden fog, and a town with few beds and fewer restaurants.
properties.onward: Sinop (NOP) airport, then 80 km west on the coast road; minibuses reach Ayancık, but the forest needs a car with decent clearance

properties.name: Hattusa
properties.desc: The Hittite capital spread over six kilometres of high grassland: a Lion Gate, a Sphinx Gate above the Yerkapı tunnel that runs right through the rampart, and the Great Temple's foundations with a green stone nobody can explain. A one-way loop road links them. The scale and the emptiness are what stay with you.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct; the plateau is 1000 m, freezing in winter and shadeless in Jul–Aug
properties.tip: Drive the loop anticlockwise and take Yerkapı first — by midday the tunnel is a queue and the ridge wind is hard work.
properties.rev: Visitors are impressed by the scale and frustrated by how little stands above knee height; the standard gripes are no shade, a 6 km circuit that punishes anyone without a car, and thin signage.
properties.entry: ₺600 (≈€13) joint with Yazılıkaya · covered by Museum Pass Türkiye
properties.onward: Ankara Esenboğa (ESB) airport, then 200 km east via Sungurlu, or Amasya Merzifon (MZH) 130 km; buses reach Sungurlu, then a taxi covers the last 30 km

properties.name: Yazılıkaya
properties.desc: Two natural rock chambers two kilometres from Hattusa, their walls carved with a procession of more than sixty Hittite gods meeting in the middle — the open-air sanctuary of the empire. In the narrow second chamber the god Sharruma has his arm around King Tudhaliya, and a sword god is driven into the rock like a blade.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct; afternoon light suits the reliefs, winter can be snowbound
properties.tip: Come in the afternoon — morning light leaves the main chamber's reliefs flat, and the low sun brings the processions out of the rock.
properties.rev: Most call it the highlight of the Hittite trip and better preserved than Hattusa, while noting the site takes barely half an hour, offers no shade, and the reliefs are weathering visibly.
properties.entry: Included in the Hattusa ticket · covered by Museum Pass Türkiye
properties.onward: Ankara Esenboğa (ESB) airport, then Boğazkale; Yazılıkaya is 2 km north-east of the village and signposted from the Hattusa loop

properties.name: Alacahöyük
properties.desc: A mound occupied since the Bronze Age, entered through a Sphinx Gate with a double-headed eagle cut into the jamb. Behind it lie thirteen royal Hatti tombs that produced the sun discs and bull standards now used as symbols of Anatolia — the originals are in Ankara, but the shaft graves are open and a small museum holds the rest.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct; the site is open ground with no shade in summer
properties.tip: See the site museum first — the reconstruction drawings make sense of the tomb shafts, which otherwise look like empty pits.
properties.rev: Archaeology-minded visitors find it essential context for Hattusa; others note the famous finds are all in Ankara, the site is small, and the village has almost no facilities.
properties.onward: Ankara Esenboğa (ESB) airport, then 210 km east via Sungurlu, or 45 km north of Boğazkale by road; no public transport to the village

properties.name: Erfelek Tatlıca Waterfalls
properties.desc: Twenty-eight cascades strung along a single kilometre of stream in a beech gorge, linked by wooden stairs and bridges that cross the water again and again. None of the falls is tall, but the sequence is relentless and the air stays cold in August. The walk up and back takes about ninety minutes.
properties.season: May–Oct; boards are icy and often closed Dec–Mar, and the flow is thin in late Aug
properties.tip: Arrive before ten or after four — the car park fills by eleven at weekends and the narrow boardwalk becomes a single-file queue.
properties.rev: Almost everyone calls the walk lovely and short; the standard complaints are slippery planks after rain, weekend queues on the bridges and identical souvenir stalls at the entrance.
properties.onward: Sinop (NOP) airport, then 35 km south-west via Erfelek town and 12 km of narrow valley road; minibuses reach Erfelek but not the falls

properties.name: İnceburun
properties.desc: The northernmost point of Türkiye: a low limestone cape with a small white lighthouse, a wind that never stops, and nothing else. The rock is scoured into ledges and pools, the sea is usually white where it hits them, and on a clear day the horizon is genuinely empty. It takes ten minutes and stays with you.
properties.season: May–Oct; winter storms make the exposed cape unpleasant and the track muddy
properties.tip: The last two kilometres are unsurfaced and rutted — leave a low car at the top and walk down, especially after rain.
properties.rev: People enjoy the emptiness and the bragging rights, while warning about the rough access track, zero facilities, and a lighthouse compound you cannot enter.
properties.onward: Sinop (NOP) airport, then 22 km north-west past Akliman and a final gravel track; no public transport, so drive or hire a taxi to wait

properties.name: Çorum Leblebi
properties.desc: Roasted chickpeas are a national snack, and Çorum is where they are taken seriously: a whole arcade of leblebi shops, sacks of white, yellow and double-roasted, plus salted, chilli and sugar-coated versions nobody outside the town admits to buying. The process runs over several days in wood-fired drums and the smell fills the street.
properties.season: All year; the shops are busiest around the Hittite festival in July
properties.tip: Ask for çifte kavrulmuş — double-roasted — and taste before you buy; every shop will hand you a scoop, and the difference between them is real.
properties.rev: Visitors enjoy the free tasting and the theatre of the roasting drums, then note the shops all look identical, prices vary wildly, and the town itself is short on other sights.
properties.onward: Amasya Merzifon (MZH) airport 90 km, or Ankara Esenboğa (ESB) 240 km; the leblebi arcade is in the centre, a few minutes from the otogar shuttle stop

properties.name: Hamsilos Bay
properties.desc: A narrow green inlet cut two hundred metres into the coast, pines leaning over water so still that boats sit on their own reflections. Guides call it Türkiye's only fjord, which it is not, but the shape is odd enough to be worth the eleven kilometres from Sinop. Akliman beach and the Sarıkum lagoon are next door.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for swimming; Apr–May and Oct for walking the pine paths
properties.tip: Swim off the rocks on the eastern arm — the head of the inlet is silty and the western picnic area is claimed by families before noon.
properties.rev: Visitors like the shape and the shade, then note the fjord label is oversold, the picnic crowds leave litter, and the water can be murky after a storm.
properties.entry: Free · small car park fee in summer
properties.onward: Sinop (NOP) airport, then 11 km north-west past Akliman; city minibuses run to Akliman in summer, otherwise take a taxi

properties.name: Sinop Fortress Prison
properties.desc: A prison built inside the ancient citadel in 1887 and used until 1997, with a reputation as the place nobody escaped from. Cell blocks, exercise yards and workshops stand as they were left, walls scratched with names and dates. Sabahattin Ali did time here, and the writing about it is half of Türkiye's prison literature.
properties.season: All year; May–Sep is pleasant, the yards are baking at midday in Jul–Aug
properties.tip: Walk the citadel ramparts afterwards from the northern gate — the same ticket area gives you the sea view the prisoners never had.
properties.rev: Most find the empty cells genuinely affecting; the repeated complaints are thin English captions, a few rooms roped off without explanation, and hard glare in the yards in high summer.
properties.onward: Sinop (NOP) airport 6 km away, or Samsun Çarşamba (SZF) and 170 km west on the coast road; the prison is in the old town, walkable from the harbour

properties.name: Balatlar Church
properties.desc: A seventh-century Byzantine church wedged into the shell of a second-century Roman bath, roofless and open to the sky in a residential street above Sinop harbour. Patches of fresco survive high on the brick walls — saints' faces, ochre and blue. It has been under excavation since 2010, so what you see changes year to year.
properties.season: Apr–Oct; the site is exposed and turns to mud in winter
properties.tip: Go in the morning, when the light reaches the frescoes on the north wall; by afternoon that side is in deep shadow.
properties.rev: Visitors find the layering of Roman and Byzantine work fascinating and complain that half the site is fenced for excavation, explanation is minimal, and it is easy to walk past the gate.
properties.onward: Sinop (NOP) airport, then the old town; the church is a ten-minute uphill walk from the harbour, signposted from the main street

properties.name: Gerze
properties.desc: A fishing town of wooden houses forty kilometres down the coast from Sinop, with a small harbour of blue boats, boatyards still cutting timber, and tea gardens looking straight at the sea. It made national news once for stopping a coal plant, then went back to being quiet. The pace is the attraction.
properties.season: Jun–Sep; out of season half the seafront closes and the wind comes straight in
properties.tip: Eat at the harbour before eight — kitchens shut early outside July and August, and the last dolmuş back to Sinop leaves around seven.
properties.rev: Visitors describe a genuinely unpolished coastal town, and mention the narrow pebble beach, limited accommodation and the highway that runs right behind the seafront.
properties.onward: Sinop (NOP) airport, then 40 km south-east on the coast road; frequent minibuses run from Sinop otogar and stop on the main street

properties.name: Şapinuva
properties.desc: The Hittites' second royal centre, in the fields outside Ortaköy, where a burnt building baked and preserved more than three thousand cuneiform tablets. Massive cut-stone foundations run across a slope of stubble, trenches are open, and the dig is still going. There is no visitor centre and often nobody but the site guard.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct; the excavation season is summer, when you may see work in progress
properties.tip: Visit on a weekday in July or August and you can watch the dig itself — the team will usually explain what they are lifting.
properties.rev: Hittite enthusiasts find it thrilling to stand in a working excavation; everyone else reports little standing above knee height, no shade, no signage and no facilities.
properties.onward: Ankara Esenboğa (ESB) or Amasya Merzifon (MZH) airport, then Çorum and 55 km south-east to Ortaköy; the site is 2 km from the town and needs a car

properties.name: İncesu Canyon
properties.desc: A twelve-kilometre limestone gorge south of Ortaköy with poplars along the stream, a road hugging one bank and a walking track on the other. Byzantine monks cut a church and cells into the cliff, reachable on a rough path. It is the green surprise of a dry province and almost nobody outside Çorum knows it.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; the stream shrinks by late August and the track floods after storms
properties.tip: The rock-cut church is about 1.5 km past the last picnic table on the left bank — nothing marks it from the road, so watch the cliff line.
properties.rev: Visitors call it a genuine find and complain about litter at the picnic areas, an unmarked and eroded path to the church, and a narrow road with nowhere to turn a car.
properties.onward: Ankara Esenboğa (ESB) airport, then Çorum and 55 km south-east to Ortaköy; the canyon road runs south from the town and needs your own car

properties.name: Şahinkaya Canyon
properties.desc: The Kızılırmak backed up behind the Altınkaya dam has flooded a gorge into a corridor of green water between three-hundred-metre cliffs. Small boats run from the village jetty for an hour up the canyon and back, and a glass terrace juts out over the drop above. Eagles use the thermals against the rock face.
properties.season: May–Oct; boats stop running in winter and the access road ices over
properties.tip: Boats only leave when they fill, so arrive at midday or expect to pay for the whole boat yourself.
properties.rev: Day-trippers call the boat hour genuinely dramatic; the recurring problems are waiting for a boat to fill, a scratched glass terrace, and a long slow drive from Samsun.
properties.onward: Samsun Çarşamba (SZF) airport, then 130 km west via Vezirköprü and 30 km of hill road to the jetty; a car is essential

properties.name: Havza Thermal Springs
properties.desc: Hot springs that have been in use since Roman times, rising at around fifty-five degrees in an ordinary inland town on the Samsun–Amasya road. Atatürk stayed here for two weeks in May 1919 and took the cure; his hotel is now a small museum. The bathing itself is unglamorous municipal hamams and hotel pools, and it works.
properties.season: Oct–Apr is the point of a thermal town; Jul–Aug is too hot to enjoy it
properties.tip: Ask for a private küvet room at a hotel spa rather than the public pool if you want quiet — they cost little more and include a soaking tub.
properties.rev: Turkish spa-goers rate the water highly, while noting tired facilities, separate men's and women's hours that catch couples out, and a town with little else to do.
properties.entry: Public bath ≈₺150 (€3.50) · hotel spa packages more
properties.onward: Samsun Çarşamba (SZF) airport, then 110 km south-west on the Amasya road; buses between Samsun and Amasya stop in Havza

properties.name: Amasya Apple Orchards
properties.desc: The misket apple that put Amasya on the province's coat of arms is small, striped red over yellow, tart and strongly scented — nothing like a supermarket apple. Orchards line the Yeşilırmak valley and the Suluova plain, and from late September roadside tables sell them by the crate along with dried okra strung like beads.
properties.season: Late Sep–Nov for harvest; blossom in late Apr is the other reason to come
properties.tip: Buy from a roadside grower rather than a town shop and ask for misket by name — most stalls also sell modern varieties that look better and taste of nothing.
properties.rev: Food travellers say the apple deserves the reputation, while warning that many stalls sell ordinary varieties under the local name and that the season is short.
properties.entry: Free · a kilo at a roadside stall ≈₺40 (€1)
properties.onward: Amasya Merzifon (MZH) airport, then the Suluova and Amasya road; the stalls line the D100 and the valley road, so you need a car to stop

properties.name: Harşena Castle
properties.desc: The fortress on the crag three hundred metres above Amasya, rebuilt so many times that Pontic, Roman, Byzantine and Ottoman masonry sit in the same wall. The real find is Cilanbolu: a rock-cut stairway plunging down a shaft to a cistern, unlit at the bottom. The view over the tombs, the river and the whole valley is the best in town.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; the summit road is icy in winter and the walk up is brutal in Jul–Aug heat
properties.tip: Take a torch for the Cilanbolu water shaft — around 150 steps down into black rock with no lighting and no handrail at the bottom.
properties.rev: Visitors rate the panorama and the tunnel highly, while flagging a narrow road with nowhere to pass, a scramble on loose stone at the top, and restoration work that closes sections without notice.
properties.onward: Amasya Merzifon (MZH) airport, then Amasya; the castle road climbs 5 km from the western edge of town, or walk up in an hour from Yalıboyu

properties.name: Amasya Rock Tombs and Yalıboyu Houses
properties.tr: Amasya Kral Kaya Mezarları ve Yalıboyu Evleri
properties.desc: Five vast tombs of the Pontic kings are cut straight into the cliff above the town, hollow rooms with a walkway carved around them. Below, Ottoman timber houses stand with their feet in the Yeşilırmak and their reflections in it. At night the cliff and the tombs are floodlit and the whole valley looks staged.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; Jul–Aug is hot in the closed valley, Jan–Feb cold and grey
properties.tip: Photograph the houses from the north bank in the late afternoon, then climb to the tombs after dark when the floodlights are on and the stairs are empty.
properties.rev: Nearly everyone rates Amasya's setting above its museums, and mentions the steep tomb stairway, a loud road on the south bank, and cafés on the waterfront charging tourist prices.
properties.onward: Amasya Merzifon (MZH) airport 45 km away, or Samsun (SZF) 130 km; the train from Samsun stops in Amasya and the old town is a short walk from the station

properties.name: Ferhat and Şirin Water Channel
properties.desc: An irrigation channel cut into the rock face above the Yeşilırmak, ancient engineering that legend hands to Ferhat the stonemason, who was told to carve water through a mountain before he could marry Şirin. You walk the ledge beside the channel with the valley dropping away and Amasya laid out downstream. It takes half an hour and few people bother.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; the ledge is slippery after rain and exposed in summer heat
properties.tip: Start from the western end near the picnic area — the eastern approach involves a scramble that families regret halfway along.
properties.rev: Walkers enjoy the quiet and the drop, and mention crumbling handrails, no shade at all, and an unmarked start that costs most people twenty minutes of searching.
properties.onward: Amasya Merzifon (MZH) airport, then Amasya; the channel starts about 3 km west of the centre on the north bank, reachable by taxi or a riverside walk

properties.name: Zile
properties.desc: A castle on an artificial mound where Caesar beat Pharnaces in 47 BC and reported it in three words — veni, vidi, vici. The arc of a Roman theatre is built into the mound's flank, houses have grown over the rest, and a clock tower stands on top. Below it a working bazaar sells pekmez and the town's own leblebi.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; the mound is exposed and hot in Jul–Aug
properties.tip: Walk up through the old quarter instead of driving — the theatre arcs are embedded in the house walls along the way and you miss them from the road.
properties.rev: Visitors enjoy the layers of history in an ordinary market town, and mention that nothing is explained on site, the castle is fenced in places, and the famous inscription is a modern plaque.
properties.onward: Tokat (TJK) airport, then 65 km west on the Turhal road; minibuses run from Tokat and Amasya

properties.name: Ladik Lake
properties.desc: A shallow reed-ringed lake under the Akdağ ridge, known for floating islands of matted reed that drift across the water when the wind turns. Storks work the shallows, fishermen push flat boats through the channels, and a boardwalk and a few cafés sit on the south shore. It is an hour's detour off the Samsun–Amasya road.
properties.season: Apr–Jun for birds and green, Sep–Oct for calm; Jan–Feb it can freeze at the edges
properties.tip: Go early — the reed islands move with the morning breeze and by afternoon the light on the water is flat and hazy.
properties.rev: Visitors find it peaceful and photogenic, then mention litter at the picnic areas, a lakeside road with no proper viewpoints, and very little to do beyond an hour's stop.
properties.onward: Samsun Çarşamba (SZF) airport, then 90 km south-west via Havza to Ladik; buses on the Samsun–Amasya route pass the turn-off

properties.name: Kızılırmak Delta Bird Paradise
properties.desc: Where Anatolia's longest river reaches the sea near Bafra, a mosaic of lagoons, reedbeds and wet pasture that logs well over three hundred bird species. Cernek lake has hides and a ringing station; water buffalo stand chest-deep in the channels; flamingos and pelicans pass through in numbers. It is flat, wet and very big.
properties.season: Apr–May and Sep–Oct for migration; Jul mosquitoes are genuinely punishing
properties.tip: Take binoculars and your own transport to the Cernek hides — the ringing station is 12 km of unpaved dyke road past the last village.
properties.rev: Birders rate it among the best wetlands in Türkiye and warn about mosquitoes, unpaved tracks that flood, poor signage, and boatmen who quote by the boat rather than the seat.
properties.onward: Samsun Çarşamba (SZF) airport, then 80 km west past Bafra; the delta tracks start north of the town and need your own vehicle

properties.name: Sebastopolis
properties.desc: A Roman city sitting inside the village of Sulusaray, so the excavation trenches run between houses and gardens. Bath walls, column drums and mosaic floors under cover, with hot spring water that the Romans used and the villagers still do. Digging restarted recently, and the site changes shape from one season to the next.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; the fields turn to mud in winter and there is no shade in summer
properties.tip: Ask at the muhtar's office if the covered mosaic shelter is locked — someone in the village always has the key.
properties.rev: Amateur archaeologists like ruins woven into a living village; the common complaints are a site fenced in pieces, half-excavated trenches, and gates that are locked with nobody obvious to ask.
properties.onward: Tokat (TJK) airport, then 68 km south-west via Artova; there is one minibus a day from Tokat, so a car is much easier

properties.name: Borabay Lake
properties.desc: A landslide-dammed lake at eight hundred metres, ringed by beech forest so close that the water is green with it. A path loops the shore in under an hour, wooden bungalows and a trout restaurant sit at one end, and mist lies on the surface most mornings. It is the coolest place in the province in August.
properties.season: May–Oct; the forest road is often snowbound Dec–Mar
properties.tip: Stay the night in a bungalow if you can — the lake at dawn, before the day-trippers from Taşova arrive, is a different place entirely.
properties.rev: Visitors describe genuine forest calm on weekdays and a picnic circus at summer weekends, with complaints about a narrow twisting access road and basic bungalows.
properties.entry: Small vehicle fee at the gate
properties.onward: Amasya Merzifon (MZH) airport, then 90 km east via Taşova and 15 km of forest road; there is no bus to the lake

properties.name: Ballıca Cave
properties.desc: A cave on a hilltop near Pazar with almost seven hundred metres of walkway across two levels and eight halls, best known for stalagmites shaped like giant mushrooms — flat caps grown by dripping from a high roof. Bats live in the upper galleries and the air is famously easy on the lungs.
properties.season: All year; the cave holds a steady temperature, but the hill road is awkward in ice
properties.tip: Go early on a weekday — coach parties fill the narrow walkway and there is no way to pass anyone once you are inside.
properties.rev: Reviewers rank it among the country's best caves, with the usual caveats: around three hundred steps, coloured lighting that ruins photographs, and coaches blocking the hilltop car park at weekends.
properties.onward: Tokat (TJK) airport, then 30 km south-west via Pazar and 7 km up a hill road; buses reach Pazar but not the cave

properties.name: Amisos Hill and Cable Car
properties.desc: A cable car lifts you from the shore park to a pine hill above Samsun where Hellenistic chamber tombs were opened in 1995 and gave up a hoard of gold jewellery, now in the city museum. The tombs are open and empty; the reason people come is the terrace, the tea gardens and the whole bay laid out below.
properties.season: All year; May–Oct for clear evenings, winter can be low cloud all week
properties.tip: Ride up an hour before sunset and walk down through the tomb terrace — the last cabins down are packed with wedding parties.
properties.rev: Locals and visitors agree the view is the point; complaints are queues for the cable car at weekends, overpriced tea on the terrace, and tombs with almost no interpretation.
properties.onward: Samsun Çarşamba (SZF) airport, then 25 km west into the city; the cable-car base station is in Batıpark on the seafront tram line

properties.name: Bandırma Vapuru Museum Ship
properties.desc: A full-size replica of the elderly steamer that carried Atatürk from Istanbul to Samsun on 19 May 1919, the day the independence war is dated from. It sits in a park by the sea with wax figures in the saloon and a panorama museum of the campaign beside it. For Turks it is a pilgrimage; for others, a short and blunt history lesson.
properties.season: All year; 19 May is a national holiday and the park is packed
properties.tip: Do the panorama museum next door first — it makes sense of the ship, which takes fifteen minutes on its own.
properties.rev: Turkish visitors find it moving, foreign visitors find it small and staged, and both mention wax figures that have seen better days and sparse English labelling.
properties.onward: Samsun Çarşamba (SZF) airport, then 25 km west; the ship is in the seafront park, one stop on the tram from the city centre

properties.name: Tokat Castle and Latifoğlu Konak
properties.desc: The castle sits on a rock spur over the town with twenty-eight towers, rock-cut cisterns and a restored path to a viewing platform on the edge. Ten minutes below, the Latifoğlu Konak is an eighteenth-century mansion whose painted ceilings and Baroque-influenced pasha's room are the finest interiors in the region.
properties.season: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; the castle climb is unpleasant in Jul–Aug heat
properties.tip: Do the konak in the middle of the day and the castle late — the platform faces west and the town below turns gold about an hour before sunset.
properties.rev: Visitors praise the konak's interiors and the castle view, while noting steep uneven steps, sections of the fortress fenced for restoration, and irregular opening hours at the mansion.
properties.onward: Tokat (TJK) airport 20 km away, or Samsun (SZF) 240 km; both sites are in the centre and walkable from the main square

properties.name: Tokat Kebabı
properties.desc: Lamb ribs, aubergine, tomato, potato, whole garlic cloves and a pointed pepper threaded onto a flat skewer with a piece of tail fat, stood upright in a wood-fired oven for an hour. The bread underneath catches everything that drips. It is ordered by weight, shared, and better in Tokat than anywhere else.
properties.season: All year; ovens are lit from late morning and the best kitchens sell out by two
properties.tip: Order by weight for two people and phone an hour ahead — good ovens will not start a skewer for a single portion.
properties.rev: Visitors call it worth the detour and warn that portions are large, the good places close in the afternoon, and vegetarians have almost nothing to order.
properties.entry: ≈₺450 (€10) per person in a kebap salonu
properties.onward: Tokat (TJK) airport 20 km away, or Samsun (SZF) 240 km; the kebap houses cluster around the old bazaar in the town centre

properties.name: Almus Lake
properties.desc: The Yeşilırmak dammed in 1966 into a long lake between forested hills east of Tokat, with trout farms on the inlets, lakeside restaurants built over the water on stilts, and boats for hire in summer. The road along the north shore is the reason to come — pine, water and almost no traffic.
properties.season: May–Oct; the water level drops noticeably by late summer
properties.tip: Order the trout at a stilt restaurant on the far shore rather than the ones by the dam wall — same fish, half the coach traffic.
properties.rev: Locals rate the fish and the quiet; visitors note that the shoreline is a reservoir rather than a natural lake, litter builds up at picnic spots, and swimming is discouraged.
properties.onward: Tokat (TJK) airport, then 35 km east on the Almus road; minibuses run from Tokat to Almus town but not around the lake

properties.name: Niksar
properties.desc: Ancient Neocaesarea, later the Danişmend capital, on a shelf above the Kelkit valley with walnut and cherry orchards below the walls. The citadel is half ruin and half neighbourhood, the Yağıbasan medrese claims to be Anatolia's first, and the town's mosques carry carved doors nobody queues to see.
properties.season: Apr–Jun for blossom and cherries, Sep–Oct for walnuts; hot and dusty in Jul–Aug
properties.tip: Buy cherries in June from the orchard stalls on the Erbaa road — Niksar's are what Istanbul greengrocers charge a premium for.
properties.rev: Travellers like the unforced, lived-in feel and note that monuments are locked as often as open, restoration is patchy, and there is little accommodation beyond basic town hotels.
properties.onward: Tokat (TJK) airport, then 55 km north-east on the Erbaa road; regular minibuses run from Tokat otogar

properties.name: Aybastı
properties.desc: A highland market town at 900 m where the hazelnut country ends and the pasture begins, and the gateway to Perşembe Yaylası. The Thursday market brings down cheese, butter and beans from the yaylas, and half the shops still sell scythes and cowbells. Nobody comes here for sights; they come for the road above it.
properties.season: May–Oct; the town works year-round but the plateau road above closes with snow
properties.tip: Time your visit for the Thursday pazar and buy the yayla butter there rather than from the roadside stalls higher up, which charge triple.
properties.rev: Travellers describe an unpretentious working town with genuinely good dairy and no tourist infrastructure at all — no proper hotel, limited evening food, and everything shut by nine.
properties.onward: Ordu–Giresun (OGU) airport, then 90 km inland; regular minibuses run from Ordu and Fatsa otogar

properties.name: Perşembe Plateau
properties.desc: An unusually flat grass plateau at 1,800 m above Aybastı, ringed by low ridges and dotted with stone-and-timber yayla houses. Cloud pours in from the coast most afternoons and swallows the whole plain in twenty minutes. In July the kemençe and the tulum come out for the festival and the meadow fills with cars.
properties.season: Jun–Sep only; the access road is snow-blocked roughly Nov–May and fog can sit for days
properties.tip: Come the week before the July şenlik — same wildflowers, same butter, none of the twenty thousand people.
properties.rev: Visitors call the light and the silence worth the climb, but warn about the festival weekend crush, near-zero visibility in fog, almost no accommodation, and shepherd dogs that take their job seriously.
properties.onward: Ordu–Giresun (OGU) airport, then 100 km inland via Aybastı; the last 20 km is paved but narrow and steep

properties.name: Ulugöl
properties.desc: A small landslide lake at 1,100 m in the hills above Gölköy, black-green under alder and hornbeam, with a level path all the way round in half an hour. There are rowing boats, a few wooden picnic decks and a trout restaurant. Mist comes off the water at dawn and burns away by nine.
properties.season: May–Oct; the lake often freezes over Jan–Feb and the road ices
properties.tip: Walk the far shore where the boardwalk ends — the picnic crowd never gets past the boat jetty.
properties.rev: Locals rate it as a cheap easy day out; the standard complaints are weekend picnic litter, loud music from the car park, and a narrow approach road that is genuinely awkward for a wide vehicle.
properties.entry: ≈₺60 (€1.30) per car at the nature park gate
properties.onward: Ordu–Giresun (OGU) airport, then 75 km inland via Gölköy; last 12 km narrow and paved

properties.name: Jason Cape
properties.desc: A blunt green headland west of Perşembe where the old coast road still runs, with a small 1868 Greek church on the tip and shingle coves on both flanks. Argonaut legend gets attached to it, deservedly or not. The sea here is clear enough to swim and there is no hotel strip, only fishing boats and a tea garden.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for swimming; autumn storms hit this cape hard
properties.tip: Take the old coastal road from Perşembe rather than the new dual carriageway — the tunnels bypass the cape entirely and you will miss the turning.
properties.rev: Reviewers love the setting and the free access, but say the church is usually locked, the coves get windy fast, and summer weekends bring picnickers who leave the shingle a mess.
properties.onward: Ordu–Giresun (OGU) airport, then 40 km west; leave the D010 at Perşembe and follow the old shore road

properties.name: Boztepe and the Ordu Cable Car
properties.desc: A 550-metre hill straight behind the city, reached by a four-minute gondola from the seafront. The summit itself is just tea terraces and a car park, but the view down the curve of the bay — hazelnut slopes one side, cargo cranes the other — is why Ordu built the thing. Sunset fills it with local families rather than tourists.
properties.season: May–Oct for clear air; the gondola stops in strong wind, which is common Nov–Feb
properties.tip: Ride up before sunset and walk the forest road back down to the harbour in about 45 minutes instead of paying for the return leg.
properties.rev: Nearly everyone rates the view and the cheap ride, then complains about weekend queues at the lower station, closures in wind or fog, and a summit that has been paved over with cafés.
properties.onward: Ordu–Giresun (OGU) airport, then 25 km west into Ordu; the lower station is a 10-minute walk from the seafront

properties.name: Çambaşı Plateau
properties.desc: A broad spruce-fringed plateau at 1,850 m in Kabadüz, with a small ski centre of two lifts and a handful of hotels. In winter the snow is deep and dry and the queues are nonexistent; in summer the same slopes are cattle pasture and the road is lined with people selling honey out of car boots.
properties.season: Jan–Mar for snow, Jun–Sep for the pasture; April and November are mud and closed lifts
properties.tip: The ski centre only guarantees weekend lift operation outside school holidays — phone the hotel before driving up midweek.
properties.rev: People praise the empty pistes and the price, then note the tiny ski area, patchy lift operation midweek, thin après-ski, and a summit road that ices badly after dark.
properties.entry: Free to enter; ski lift pass ≈₺400 (€8.50) a day
properties.onward: Ordu–Giresun (OGU) airport, then 55 km south via Kabadüz on a fully paved mountain road; winter tyres essential

properties.name: Kulakkaya Plateau
properties.desc: A 1,500 m plateau above Bulancak, close enough to the coast that on a clear evening you can see the Black Sea from the meadow. Spruce forest, a couple of hotels and a paraglider launch that catches thermals off the ridge. It is the yayla people from Giresun drive up to for supper and drive home from the same night.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for the meadow; some winter weekends work for snow when the road is cleared
properties.tip: Book a table at a plateau restaurant for the hour before sunset — the sea view only appears when the afternoon haze drops.
properties.rev: Praised as an easy escape from the coastal heat with real food and a rare sea view, but people warn of fog closing in for days, weekend crowds from Giresun, and hotel prices that spike in August.
properties.onward: Ordu–Giresun (OGU) airport, then 30 km east to Bulancak and 25 km up a paved mountain road

properties.name: Şebinkarahisar Castle
properties.desc: A fortress welded onto a black volcanic plug 1,300 m above an inland plain, three hours from the sea and in a completely different climate. Walls, cisterns and a rock-cut stair survive; the summit is a knife edge with a 300-metre drop on the town side. Below it the Meryem Ana monastery clings to another cliff.
properties.season: May–Oct; the plateau is cold and often snowy Dec–Mar
properties.tip: Drive to the upper car park then take the stepped path — the older track from the town centre is a punishing 45-minute climb in full sun.
properties.rev: Visitors call it the most dramatic castle site in the region and are surprised how empty it is; the complaints are unprotected drops, patchy restoration, and a long 110 km drive from the coast on a slow road.
properties.onward: Ordu–Giresun (OGU) airport, then 110 km inland from Giresun over the mountains — about 2.5 hours by car or bus

properties.name: Giresun Island
properties.desc: The only real island in the eastern Black Sea, a 40,000 m² lump of rock and scrub two kilometres offshore, carrying a ruined Byzantine wall, a chapel and the so-called Hamza Taşı. Ancient writers made it the Amazons' island of Ares. On 20 May the whole city sails out for the Aksu festival and circles the rock three times.
properties.season: May–Sep for boats; nothing runs in a swell, which means most of Nov–Mar
properties.tip: Outside the 20 May festival you need to hire a fishing boat from the harbour yourself — there is no scheduled service, and the crossing is cancelled the moment the wind turns.
properties.rev: The setting and the legend win people over; the recurring gripes are unreliable boats, no facilities whatever on the island, overgrown paths, and a landing that is impossible in any sea at all.
properties.entry: Free to land; boat hire from Giresun harbour ≈₺500–800 (€11–17) per boat
properties.onward: Ordu–Giresun (OGU) airport, then 45 km east to Giresun; boats leave from the town harbour

properties.name: Kümbet Plateau
properties.desc: A 1,650 m plateau in Dereli that is really a small summer village — wooden houses, a mosque, a church-shaped chapel and a permanent row of tea houses. It is the easiest of the Giresun yaylas to reach and the busiest, with a July festival that closes the road. Beyond the last house the pasture runs empty for kilometres.
properties.season: Jun–Sep; road usually snowbound Dec–Apr
properties.tip: Push another 8 km past the village towards Karagöl for the views everyone photographs and thinks they took at Kümbet.
properties.rev: Visitors find it green, cool and easy to reach, then complain that it has become a car park with cafés, that fog cancels the view without warning, and that festival weekends are gridlock.
properties.onward: Ordu–Giresun (OGU) airport, then 60 km south of Giresun via Dereli; paved the whole way, minibuses in summer

properties.name: Bektaş Plateau
properties.desc: Higher, barer and far quieter than Kümbet, at around 2,100 m on the Giresun mountain ridge, with a scatter of huts and horses grazing among rock outcrops. Above the tree line the cloud sits below you most mornings. The onward track towards Şebinkarahisar over the ridge is one of the best rough drives in the region.
properties.season: Late Jun–mid Sep; snow lingers into June and returns in October
properties.tip: The ridge track south to Karagöl and Şebinkarahisar needs high clearance and is nothing to attempt in fog — turn back if the cloud drops below the huts.
properties.rev: People rate the emptiness and the light highly; the complaints are a rough final stretch of road, only basic bungalow accommodation, no phone signal, and cold nights even in August.
properties.onward: Ordu–Giresun (OGU) airport, then 80 km south from Giresun via Dereli; the last 15 km is gravel

properties.name: Mavi Göl
properties.desc: A small landslide-dammed lake on the Dereli road, sitting in a steep spruce gorge with drowned tree trunks still standing in the shallows. The colour swings from turquoise to slate depending on rain and light, and it is at its best when the water is low enough to expose the pale stone shoreline.
properties.season: May–Oct; heavy spring rain turns the water brown and muddy
properties.tip: Stop on the way up to Kümbet rather than on the way down — morning light hits the water, and by afternoon the gorge is in shadow.
properties.rev: A quick and genuinely pretty roadside stop, though visitors note that the colour depends entirely on recent rain, the shore is littered, and there is nowhere safe to park more than two cars.
properties.onward: Ordu–Giresun (OGU) airport, then 45 km south of Giresun on the Dereli–Kümbet road

properties.name: Tirebolu
properties.desc: A small port between two bays with a Genoese-era castle, St Jean, on the headland dividing them and a row of old timber houses behind the quay. Hazelnut sacks stack on the pavement in August. It is the one town on this coast where the dual carriageway did not obliterate the waterfront.
properties.season: Jun–Sep for the sea; the town is pleasant year-round but wet
properties.tip: Walk out to St Jean castle at dusk — the gate is unlocked and the two bays light up on either side of you.
properties.rev: Travellers like the relaxed harbour and cheap fish; the usual gripes are the highway noise behind the town, a small stony beach, and a castle that is little more than walls with no signage.
properties.onward: Ordu–Giresun (OGU) airport, then 85 km east on the coast road; every Trabzon–Giresun bus stops here

properties.name: Tomara Waterfall
properties.desc: Water bursting straight out of a limestone cliff face in a fifty-metre-wide sheet above Şiran — a karst spring rather than a river fall, which is why it runs the same volume in August as in April. Steps and a platform lead to the base, and the spray keeps the whole hollow ten degrees cooler than the plateau.
properties.season: May–Oct; the plateau around is snow-covered and bleak Dec–Mar
properties.tip: This is spring-fed, so unlike almost every other waterfall in the region it is worth visiting in late summer when everything else has dried up.
properties.rev: Visitors are surprised by the width and the volume; the recurring gripes are commercial development right at the base, loud music from the restaurants, weekend crowds and a slippery stair.
properties.onward: Trabzon (TZX) airport, then 200 km south via Gümüşhane to Şiran, or Erzincan (ERC) from the south; car needed for the last 15 km

properties.name: Limni Lake
properties.desc: A small dark lake at 1,600 m in the pine forest above Torul, with a level path all the way round and a wooden jetty everybody photographs. The water reflects the ridge cleanly on a still morning. In winter it freezes and the forest road becomes a cross-country ski track for the few who know.
properties.season: May–Oct; snow Dec–Mar, when the road is often unploughed
properties.tip: Come up the Zigana side and stop at Torul castle on the way — the lake alone does not justify the drive, the combination does.
properties.rev: Described as pleasant and quiet rather than spectacular, with complaints about a steep narrow access road, a small car park that fills on weekends, and facilities limited to one café.
properties.entry: ≈₺60 (€1.30) per vehicle at the nature park gate
properties.onward: Trabzon (TZX) airport, then 110 km south over Zigana to Torul and 10 km up a forest road

properties.name: Karaca Cave
properties.desc: A dry, warm show cave at 1,550 m above Torul, packed with travertine pools, curtain formations and columns in white and rust-red across a single large chamber. Unlike most Turkish show caves it is properly lit and the walkway is short. The air is claimed to help asthma, which is why half the visitors sit down and stay.
properties.season: Year-round; the access road above Torul can be icy Dec–Mar
properties.tip: It is only about 100 m of walkway — do not build a day around it, but do pair it with Limni lake, which is twenty minutes away.
properties.rev: Rated as one of the better-presented caves in Türkiye, with the consistent caveats that it is small, the visit takes twenty minutes, the stairs from the car park are steep, and it gets crowded with tour buses.
properties.onward: Trabzon (TZX) airport, then 110 km south over Zigana to Torul, then 17 km up a paved side road

properties.name: Santa Ruins
properties.desc: Seven abandoned Greek hamlets spread across a high forested basin, emptied by the 1923 population exchange and left to the trees. Cut-stone houses with intact door lintels, three ruined churches and a school stand roofless among the beech. Nothing is signed, restored or guarded; you find the villages by following the old paths.
properties.season: Jun–Sep; the track is snowbound Nov–May and impassable in mud after rain
properties.tip: Go with someone who knows the paths, or you will find one hamlet and miss the other six — the churches at Piştovlu and Zurnacılı are the ones to aim for.
properties.rev: People who reach it call it the most haunting place in the region; the complaints are a long rough forest track, no signage or map, treasure-hunter damage everywhere, and collapse that gets worse each year.
properties.onward: Trabzon (TZX) airport, then 90 km south towards Gümüşhane and a long unsurfaced forest track from Dumanlı; 4x4 or a local guide

properties.name: Çal Cave
properties.desc: A wet, cold river cave in the hills above Düzköy, with about a kilometre lit and walkable of a system that runs far deeper. Water runs through the whole length, there are small lakes and a constant drip, and the air stays around 6 °C. It is a genuine caving experience rather than a floodlit corridor.
properties.season: Year-round inside; the approach road is awkward in snow Dec–Mar
properties.tip: Wear proper shoes and take a jacket — the floor is running water and people turn back at the first pool in sandals.
properties.rev: People are impressed by the scale and the running water, and equally consistent about the cold, the constant dripping that ruins cameras, slippery steps, and a long narrow road up from the coast.
properties.onward: Trabzon (TZX) airport, then 45 km west and inland via Düzköy; car or taxi only, no public transport to the cave

properties.name: Krom Valley
properties.desc: A steep valley of abandoned Greek mining villages north of Gümüşhane, with stone houses stacked on the slopes and several roofless churches still holding their apses. Silver and lead were dug here for centuries; the people left in 1923. Descendants come back most summers and services are occasionally held in the ruins.
properties.season: Jun–Sep; the valley road is impassable with snow Nov–May
properties.tip: Ask in Yağmurdere for the road to Ristbaşı and Kaban — the ruins are strung over fifteen kilometres and there is not a single sign in the valley.
properties.rev: A find for anyone interested in Pontic history, though visitors report the track is rough and long, buildings are collapsing and dug over by treasure hunters, and there is nowhere to eat or sleep in the valley.
properties.onward: Trabzon (TZX) airport, then 130 km via Gümüşhane and a long mountain road to Yağmurdere; high-clearance vehicle strongly advised

properties.name: Vazelon Monastery
properties.desc: The other cliff monastery of Maçka, dedicated to St John, older than Sümela and left almost entirely alone. Roofless halls, a fresco of the Last Judgement fading on an outer wall, hazel and ivy growing through the floors. There is no ticket office, no shuttle and usually nobody else at all.
properties.season: May–Oct; the forest track is impassable after heavy rain and in snow
properties.tip: The last two kilometres are a rough forest track — leave the car at the village of Kiremitli and walk up in about forty minutes.
properties.rev: Those who make it call it more atmospheric than Sümela precisely because it is empty; the complaints are the unsigned rough track, structural collapse, graffiti from treasure hunters, and no facilities whatsoever.
properties.onward: Trabzon (TZX) airport, then 45 km south via Maçka; turn off at Kiremitli — a high-clearance car or a walk from the village

properties.name: Akçaabat
properties.desc: A coastal town west of Trabzon with two separate reasons to stop: Ortamahalle, a hillside quarter of restored nineteenth-century timber-and-stone houses looking over the sea, and the köfte, which is a national brand. The old quarter is small enough to walk in an hour and has a Byzantine church at the top of it.
properties.season: Year-round; May–Oct for the terraces, though it rains in every month
properties.tip: Eat the köfte at a grill in the town centre, not on the Ortamahalle terraces — same meat, half the price, and the local queue tells you which one.
properties.rev: The köfte lives up to its reputation for most people; the recurring complaints are that Ortamahalle is small and partly derelict, parking is hopeless, and the restored houses are mostly closed cafés.
properties.onward: Trabzon (TZX) airport, then 15 km west on the coast road; constant dolmuş from Trabzon Meydan

properties.name: Zigana Pass
properties.desc: The 2,030 m saddle where the ancient Trabzon–Erzurum caravan road crosses the Pontic wall — the point where Xenophon's men are supposed to have seen the sea. Spruce and cloud on the north side, bare brown steppe on the south, within twenty minutes of driving. The 14.5 km tunnel below now takes all the lorries.
properties.season: Jun–Oct for the old pass road; snow closes it frequently Nov–Apr while the tunnel stays open
properties.tip: Skip the tunnel and take the old road over the top — that is where the climate flips and where the roadside honey and kuymak stalls still are.
properties.rev: Drivers rate the scenery and the sudden climate change, but warn about fog, black ice, lorry traffic on the tunnel approaches, and a summit that in bad weather offers nothing but grey.
properties.onward: Trabzon (TZX) airport, then 65 km south on the D885 towards Gümüşhane; every Trabzon–Erzurum bus crosses it, now by tunnel

properties.name: Sümela Monastery
properties.desc: A Greek Orthodox monastery glued to a sheer cliff 300 m above the Altındere valley, founded in the fourth century and rebuilt in stages until 1923. The painted rock chapel is the point: layers of frescoes inside and out, badly vandalised, still extraordinary. From the valley floor it looks impossible, which is exactly the intended effect.
properties.season: May–Oct; sections close after rockfall and the valley road can shut in winter
properties.tip: Take the first shuttle of the day from the lower car park — by eleven the cliff stair is a single-file queue and the chapel interior is unphotographable.
properties.rev: Almost everyone calls it worth the trip, then reports long shuttle queues, restoration scaffolding, parts of the complex roped off, and disappointment that the famous outer fresco wall is only partly accessible.
properties.entry: ≈₺700 (€15) for foreigners · covered by Museum Pass Türkiye
properties.onward: Trabzon (TZX) airport, then 50 km south via Maçka to the Altındere car park, and a compulsory minibus shuttle up the valley

properties.name: Hagia Sophia of Trabzon
properties.desc: A thirteenth-century Komnenian church on a bluff above the sea, with the finest surviving Byzantine frescoes on this coast and a carved stone frieze of Adam and Eve over the south porch. It has been a working mosque again since 2013, so much of the painted interior now sits behind curtains and false ceilings.
properties.season: Year-round; closed to visitors during the five daily prayers
properties.tip: Go mid-morning between prayers and ask the görevli about the narthex — the best frescoes are in the porch, outside the curtained prayer hall.
properties.rev: Visitors call the architecture and the surviving paintings remarkable, but consistently express frustration that the reconversion to a mosque hides most of the frescoes and that photography inside is restricted.
properties.entry: Free — it functions as a mosque; dress modestly and remove shoes
properties.onward: Trabzon (TZX) airport, then 8 km west along the shore; city buses and dolmuş marked Ayasofya run from Meydan

properties.name: Atatürk Mansion, Trabzon
properties.desc: A white neo-baroque villa of 1903, built by a Greek banking family and given to Atatürk by the city; he stayed three times and drafted part of his will here in 1937. The rooms are preserved with his furniture and books, and the terraced garden of magnolia and cedar looks straight down over Trabzon to the sea.
properties.season: Year-round; the garden is best May–Jun when the magnolias are out
properties.tip: The garden is the real attraction and is free to walk in — you only pay if you go inside the house.
properties.rev: Turkish visitors treat it as a pilgrimage and rate it highly; foreign visitors more often find the interior modest, the labelling Turkish-only, and the hillside approach hard to reach without a taxi.
properties.entry: ≈₺60 (€1.30) — municipal museum, not covered by the Museum Pass
properties.onward: Trabzon (TZX) airport, then 6 km up into Soğuksu; a dolmuş marked Köşk runs from Meydan, or a short taxi

properties.name: Hıdırnebi Plateau
properties.desc: A 1,600 m ridge-top pasture above Akçaabat, close enough to the coast that the cloud sea below you is sitting on Trabzon. Timber houses, a small mosque and a July festival with tulum and horon that draws the whole district. Most days a bank of white fog rolls up the valley by mid-afternoon and swallows everything.
properties.season: Jun–Sep; road usually closed by snow Dec–Apr
properties.tip: Stay the night in a plateau pansiyon — the cloud inversion happens at dawn and day-trippers from Trabzon always miss it.
properties.rev: Visitors describe the cloud-sea mornings as the best thing in the province and then list the drawbacks: a steep narrow road, very basic rooms, no food after dark, and fog that can cancel the whole point.
properties.onward: Trabzon (TZX) airport, then 15 km west to Akçaabat and 30 km up a paved but tight mountain road

properties.name: Kop Pass
properties.desc: A 2,400 m crossing between Bayburt and Erzurum over treeless upland, with a monument at the summit to the soldiers who froze here in the winter of 1916. There is no forest, no shelter and nothing softening the view — just brown grass, snow poles and weather. A tunnel now takes traffic under the worst of it.
properties.season: Jun–Oct on the old road; snow and closures are routine Nov–May even with the tunnel open
properties.tip: Check the weather before crossing in winter even now — the tunnel helps, but the approaches still close in blizzards and vehicles get stranded.
properties.rev: Drivers describe it as bleak in the best sense and historically affecting; the complaints are severe wind, sudden fog, ice outside high summer, and very little reason to stop beyond the monument.
properties.onward: Erzurum (ERZ) airport, then 80 km north-west on the D915 towards Bayburt; every Erzurum–Trabzon bus crosses it

properties.name: Bayburt Castle
properties.desc: One of the largest castles in Anatolia, a long walled ridge above the Çoruh with Bagratid foundations and Saltuk and Seljuk rebuilding on top. Restoration has rebuilt long stretches of curtain wall, more heavily than purists like. From the ramparts the whole town and the treeless upland around it lie open.
properties.season: May–Oct; Bayburt is bitterly cold and often snowbound Dec–Mar
properties.tip: Go up at dusk when the walls are floodlit and the town below turns on — daytime light on the bare stone is flat and unrewarding.
properties.rev: Visitors are impressed by the sheer scale and the view and just as often criticise the restoration as over-aggressive concrete work, along with steep uneven paths and little in the way of explanation.
properties.onward: Trabzon (TZX) airport, then 175 km south over Zigana and the Kop pass, or Erzurum (ERZ) and 120 km north; buses run from both

properties.name: Sultan Murat Plateau
properties.desc: A wide pasture at 2,100 m above Çaykara, named for the Ottoman sultan who camped here and marked by a memorial to the Turkish soldiers who died on this ridge in 1916. Above the last houses the grass runs to bare rock and small tarns. It is the highest road-accessible yayla in Trabzon and it feels it.
properties.season: Late Jun–Sep; snow blocks the road roughly Nov–May
properties.tip: Combine it with Uzungöl in one loop rather than backtracking — the link road over the ridge is rough but passable in a normal car in summer.
properties.rev: Reported as spectacular and near-empty, with the standard caveats: a long climb on broken asphalt, no shops, cold even in August, and the monument area busy on national commemoration days.
properties.onward: Trabzon (TZX) airport, then 95 km east via Of and Çaykara, then 25 km of steep mountain road

properties.name: Uzungöl
properties.desc: A landslide lake at 1,100 m under steep spruce ridges, with a wooden mosque on the shore that appears on every poster of the Black Sea. It is also the most heavily developed spot in the region: hotels stacked up both valley walls, jet skis on the water, and Gulf-market restaurants everywhere. The surrounding yaylas are the redeeming part.
properties.season: May–Jun and Sep–Oct; July–Aug is peak Gulf season and fully booked
properties.tip: Sleep in Uzungöl but spend the day up at Demirkapı or Şekersu yayla — the lake itself is worth about ninety minutes.
properties.rev: Opinion splits sharply: the setting is genuinely beautiful, but reviewers repeatedly describe overbuilding, traffic jams on the single valley road, inflated food prices and constant construction noise.
properties.entry: Free; ≈₺60 (€1.30) vehicle fee at the valley barrier
properties.onward: Trabzon (TZX) airport, then 100 km east and inland via Of and Çaykara; minibuses run from Trabzon in summer

properties.name: Rize Ziraat Botanic Garden
properties.desc: A terraced garden on the hill directly above Rize, laid out on the old tea research station: camellia, rhododendron, kiwi and magnolia stepped down the slope with the port and the sea below. The wooden tea house at the top is where the city goes to sit, and the tea is grown fifty metres away.
properties.season: Apr–Jun for the camellias and rhododendrons; open and pleasant year-round
properties.tip: Walk up from the city rather than taking a taxi to the top — the path enters through the lower terraces, which is where the planting is best.
properties.rev: Locals rate it as the best free thing in Rize; visitors note that the tea house gets packed on weekend afternoons, the labelling is thin, and the whole place is exposed to the constant rain.
properties.onward: Rize–Artvin (RZV) airport, then 35 km west into Rize; the garden is a 20-minute walk or short taxi up from the centre

properties.name: Baksı Museum
properties.desc: A contemporary art museum built on a bare ridge above a village 45 km from Bayburt, founded by the artist Hüsamettin Koçan and winner of the Council of Europe Museum Prize in 2014. Modern painting and sculpture sit beside a working collection of local weaving and metalwork, in a building that looks out over empty steppe.
properties.season: May–Oct; the road up is difficult in snow and winter opening is limited
properties.tip: Phone ahead — it keeps short and seasonal hours and people regularly drive 45 km up to a locked door.
properties.rev: Those who get in describe an unexpectedly serious museum in an improbable place; the complaints are erratic opening hours, a long drive on a rough road, and almost no facilities in the village below.
properties.onward: Trabzon (TZX) or Erzurum (ERZ) airport, then to Bayburt and 45 km north on a partly unsurfaced road; car only

properties.name: Anzer Plateau
properties.desc: A remote 2,000 m plateau in İkizdere whose meadows carry an unusual density of flowering herbs, which is why the honey made here sells for more than any other in the country. The village is small and the hives are everywhere. Genuine Anzer honey is scarce, certified, and widely counterfeited on the road below.
properties.season: Jul–Sep, and the flowering peak is late July; the road is closed by snow Nov–Jun
properties.tip: Buy only from a producer in the village with the cooperative's certificate — anything sold as Anzer honey on the coast road is almost certainly not.
properties.rev: Those who make the drive rate the meadows and the honey highly; the standard complaints are a long rough climb, a very short season, no accommodation, and rampant fake honey everywhere below the plateau.
properties.onward: Rize–Artvin (RZV) airport, then 60 km via İkizdere and a further 25 km of steep mountain road; car only

properties.name: Sal Plateau
properties.desc: Pokut's quieter neighbour, an hour's walk along the same ridge, with fewer houses, more grazing cattle and an open view down the Fırtına valley towards the sea. Because almost everyone stops at Pokut for the photograph, Sal keeps its working-yayla character: milk churns, cut hay, and dogs that bark at strangers.
properties.season: Late Jun–Sep; deep snow Nov–May
properties.tip: Walk the ridge from Pokut to Sal in the late afternoon and have someone bring your bag round by track — it is the best hour of light and a genuinely easy path.
properties.rev: Walkers prefer it to Pokut for the quiet and the food, but note there is hardly any organised accommodation, no shop, unreliable phone signal, and the same rough access track.
properties.onward: Rize–Artvin (RZV) airport, then Çamlıhemşin and the Pokut track; most people walk the last hour from Pokut

properties.name: Fırtına Valley and its Arch Bridges
properties.desc: Forty kilometres of gorge running from the sea at Ardeşen up into the Kaçkars, with the fastest river in the country at the bottom of it and a series of high single-arch stone bridges — Şenyuva, Çatal, Mikron — thrown across it in Ottoman times. Tea and hazelnut give way to spruce, then to bare rock.
properties.season: May–Oct; peak snowmelt in May makes the river spectacular and rafting serious
properties.tip: Stop at the Şenyuva bridge and walk across it rather than photographing from the car — from the far bank the whole gorge opens up behind it.
properties.rev: Praised as one of the great valley drives in Türkiye, with recurring complaints about hydroelectric construction scarring the riverbed, landslip closures, a very narrow road, and rain that can last a week.
properties.onward: Rize–Artvin (RZV) airport, then 50 km east to Ardeşen and inland via Çamlıhemşin; minibuses reach Çamlıhemşin, a car beyond it

properties.name: Zilkale
properties.desc: A medieval tower castle on a spur 750 m above the Fırtına river, built to watch the caravan route to the Kaçkar passes and now standing in wet forest with cloud tearing past the keep. The interior is small — a chapel, cisterns, a stair to the tower — but the position is the whole point.
properties.season: May–Oct; the valley road can be closed by landslip after heavy rain, and snow shuts it in winter
properties.tip: Photograph it from the road bend about 500 m below rather than from inside — the classic shot of the castle on its spur cannot be taken from the castle.
properties.rev: Consistently rated for atmosphere and the drive in; complaints are a narrow cliff-edge road with no barrier, a small interior that takes fifteen minutes, and mist that hides it entirely on many days.
properties.onward: Rize–Artvin (RZV) airport, then Ardeşen, Çamlıhemşin and 15 km up the Fırtına valley road; a car is essential

properties.name: Gito Plateau
properties.desc: A grass shoulder at 2,100 m on the far side of the valley from Pokut, reached by a switchback track from Ayder side. Fewer houses, more open meadow, and a horizon of Kaçkar peaks that stays visible longer in the day because the cloud comes up the other valley first. Horses graze loose across the whole plateau.
properties.season: Jul–Sep; snow closes the track Nov–Jun
properties.tip: Gito clears earlier in the morning than Pokut — if you have one dawn and the forecast is bad, come here.
properties.rev: Reported as emptier and more open than Pokut with equally good views, though visitors flag a steep unmade track, a couple of very simple guesthouses, and rain that can set in for a week.
properties.onward: Rize–Artvin (RZV) airport, then Çamlıhemşin and a 4x4 track from the Ayder road; local jeep transfers can be arranged in Ayder

properties.name: Çamlıhemşin
properties.desc: The last real town in the Fırtına valley and the hinge for everything above it: Zilkale, Ayder, Pokut, the Kaçkar trailheads. Hemşin is spoken in the shops, the women wear the black-and-yellow puşi headscarf, and the bakery does a cornbread worth stopping for. Old stone-and-timber houses stand along the river below the road.
properties.season: May–Oct; the town stays open in winter but the roads above it do not
properties.tip: Buy your food here — Ayder and the yaylas above have almost nothing, and prices double for every kilometre of altitude.
properties.rev: Treated by most travellers as a supply stop rather than a destination, and praised for exactly that — though people note the town itself is small, parking is tight, and the through traffic to Ayder never stops.
properties.onward: Rize–Artvin (RZV) airport, then 50 km east to Ardeşen and 20 km inland; frequent minibuses from Ardeşen and Pazar

properties.name: The Tea Terraces of Çayeli
properties.desc: The hills behind Çayeli are terraced with tea from the shoreline to about 800 m, a corrugated green that changes tone three times a day with the light and the rain. Between May and October pickers work the slopes with shears and sacks, and the factories along the coast road run around the clock.
properties.season: May–Oct during the three picking rounds; the bushes are dull and bare-looking Dec–Mar
properties.tip: Ask at a village tea house whether you can walk a row with a picker — most say yes, and it is the only way to understand how steep the ground actually is.
properties.rev: People find the landscape more striking than expected and the growers welcoming; the complaints are almost no signage or organised visits, factories that turn away drop-ins, and constant drizzle.
properties.onward: Rize–Artvin (RZV) airport, then 25 km west to Çayeli; take any village road inland from the coast highway

properties.name: Ayder Plateau
properties.desc: The famous hot-spring yayla at 1,350 m at the head of the Fırtına valley, with waterfalls dropping straight into the settlement and the Kaçkar trailheads starting behind it. It has been ruined and half-repaired by concrete building; a long demolition and regeneration programme has been tearing out illegal hotels for years. The valley above is still superb.
properties.season: Jun–Sep; snowbound and mostly shut Dec–Apr, and it rains in every month
properties.tip: Use Ayder as a bed and start walking at dawn towards Huser or Aşağı Kavrun — the settlement itself empties of interest by mid-morning.
properties.rev: Everyone agrees the setting is exceptional and the building is not: reviews repeatedly cite concrete hotels, ongoing demolition works, mud, day-tripper coach crowds and inflated prices in August.
